Calendly Help Compendium

The official Calendly Help Center (calendly.com/help)

2026-07-28

Calendly Help Compendium

This compendium contains the main content of 334 pages from the official Calendly Help Center at calendly.com/help, crawled to closure. Scope: Calendly on the web and the Calendly iOS app; Calendly publishes no Windows desktop app and no Alexa skill, so the web application serves Windows users through the browser, and platform-specific instructions appear inline where Calendly provides them. Pages are grouped under the Help Center’s own sections, taken from each page’s breadcrumb trail, alphabetized, with titles alphabetized within each section. The long-standing Zendesk knowledge base at help.calendly.com now redirects into this Help Center and contributed no separate articles; sixteen addresses beyond the crawl’s pass limit and two fetch failures are noted from the run log for the completeness audit. The developer API documentation is out of scope by request. Site chrome and feedback prompts have been removed.

Analytics & reporting

Calendly analytics

Available to Owners and Admins on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button] #### Overview

Calendly’s in-app analytics provide detailed insights into your organization’s scheduling trends, helping owners and admins track data up to one year.

Easily keep track of:

  • Created events
  • Completed events and trends
  • Rescheduled events
  • Canceled events
  • Event distribution by duration
  • Popular events
  • Popular times #### Access and customize your dashboard

To open the Analytics dashboard, select Analytics from the left sidebar. Your dashboard shows organization-wide event data and individual user data.

  • Hover and click on data in widgets like Popular Times to explore more insights.
  • Select the [Image: Info] icon on any widget for a detailed explanation.
  • Use the [Image: Verticle menu] three dots in the top-right corner of a widget to see more options.

To customize the dashboard, select Customize at the top and choose which widgets you want to display. #### Filter your analytics data

Use the date range and filters at the top of the dashboard to view data by:

  • Date
  • User
  • Team
  • Group
  • Event type

Looking for data on shared event types? Filter by the event host’s name.

If you’re a user (not an admin or owner), you’ll only see your own event data. Admins can view their own data by filtering for their name. #### Routing Form analytics

If your organization is on our Teams plan or higher, owners and admins can access Routing Form analytics.

Go to the Routing tab to track how form submissions turn into booked meetings. You can track submissions from:

  • Calendly
  • Marketo
  • Pardot
  • HubSpot #### Export data

You can export your organization’s analytics to a CSV file for detailed reporting. Select Export at the top of the dashboard and choose Event Data or Employee (user) Data.

Tracking and reporting

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans #### Tracking conversions

You can track conversions in Calendly using Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, or by redirecting invitees to an external page after they book.

To track conversions directly in Calendly, add UTM parameters to your scheduling links. These tags help you see which campaigns bring in the most scheduling traffic.

For example, you could set up a summer campaign with this link:

javascript

calendly.com/YOURLINK?utm_campaign=summer&utm_source=facebook

When someone books through this custom link, Calendly records the UTM data. You can filter your Meetings page to view results.

Note

Calendly doesn’t provide IP address data for past meetings. For additional tracking, you can connect tools like Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, or Zapier. #### Custom tracking on the Calendly embed

If you’ve embedded Calendly on your site, you can trigger custom actions using JavaScript. Calendly’s embed sends message events to the parent window during the booking flow. #### Export meeting data

You can view and export your organization’s meeting data in a CSV file for detailed reporting. The export includes:

  • Invitee name, contact details, and time zone
  • Event type, date, and location
  • UTM parameters and Salesforce data
  • Marketing email consent status (for GDPR)
  • Payment details from Stripe and PayPal integrations

To export:

  1. Go to the Meetings page.
  2. Filter the meetings you want in your report based on date, team member, etc.
  3. In the top right corner, select Export.
  4. A CSV file will download automatically, or you’ll receive an email with the file.

Availability

Availability overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Your availability in Calendly is a mix of your schedules, holidays, and busy times from connected calendars. You can manage everything from your Availability page.

For example, you can:

  • Create and apply multiple schedules: Build different schedules for different types of availability. Assign them to the Event Types that need them.
  • Observe holidays: Select holidays to automatically block time on all scheduling links.
  • Manage connected calendars: Choose which calendars Calendly checks for conflicts and where new events are added. #### Before you begin

Set your time zone and location in your Account settings under the Profile section. #### How availability works with your connected calendar

Availability controls when people can book time with you. Your connected calendar prevents double-booking and stores your scheduled meetings.

Here’s how they work together:

  • You set the days and times you are available.

  • Calendly checks your connected calendar for events marked as busy.

  • Busy events block those times from being booked.

  • When someone books a meeting, Calendly adds it to your connected calendar. #### Best practices for users

  • Apply schedules by Event Type: On the Availability page, use the Active on dropdown to assign schedules to your Event Types.

  • Observe holidays: Toggle on the holidays you want to observe. Calendly will block off those days automatically.

  • Manage calendar connections: Choose which calendars Calendly should check when looking for conflicts and where to save new meetings. #### Best practices for owners and admins

  • Connect team calendars: Every team member should connect their own calendars.

  • Check calendar connections: View calendar status for each user on the Users page in the Admin Center or from their individual profiles.

  • Set Event Type permissions: Let others edit availability for specific Event Types, even if they’re not the host. Learn more about event type permissions. #### Setting up availability

Ready to set up your availability? These Help Center articles will walk you through the steps.

  • How to set your availability
  • Connect your calendar to Calendly
  • How to edit holidays within Calendly
  • How to fine-tune your availability settings

Free/busy rules overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Calendly’s Free/busy rules help you open up more time in your calendar. You can use them to book over certain meetings, giving you more control over your availability. #### Before you begin

Make sure to:

  • Connect your calendar on the Calendar settings page.
  • Set it as a calendar to check for conflicts.
  • This feature doesn’t work with the Outlook plug-in. You’ll need an online calendar connection.
  • You don’t need a calendar to add events to, but if you do, make sure it’s also set to check for conflicts.

Need help? Read more here. #### What you can do with free/busy rules

Use free/busy rules to:

  • Book over future events.

  • Book over personal events or Calendly meetings on your connected calendar.

  • Note: You can’t book over full Group meetings, even if their titles are listed as exceptions. #### Set up free/busy rules

You’ll set these up in the event editor. Here’s how:

  1. Go to your Scheduling page.
  2. Choose the event type you want to update.
  3. Scroll down and select More options.
  4. Expand the Free/busy rules section.
  5. Click + Add meeting exception.
  6. In the dropdown, choose:
  • Includes – to match part of an event title.
  • Matches exactly – to match the full event title.
  1. Type the event title in the search bar.
  2. Press Enter.
  3. Click Save changes.

Now, Calendly will allow those calendar events to be booked over. #### Booking over Calendly meetings

If you book over a Calendly meeting:

  • You’ll get an alert in your New Event email.
  • Click View in Calendly to go to your Meetings page.
  • From there, you can choose to reschedule the original meeting, if needed. #### Frequently asked questions

You can book over:

  • Calendly meetings on calendars marked for conflict checks
  • Events on your connected online calendar
  • Focus time or break blocks on your calendar

Note: This doesn’t work with Outlook plug-in connections. Use an online calendar instead.

No. You’ll get a conflict alert in your email. Select View in Calendly and choose to reschedule or keep the original meeting. [Image: 22685547026199]

  1. Go to your home page.
  2. Select the event type.
  3. Click More options.
  4. Expand the Free/busy rules section.
  5. Review the meeting exceptions listed.

There are a few reasons:

  • The meeting wasn’t added to a calendar set to check for conflicts.
  • The scheduled meeting title doesn’t match your event type title.
  • You’re using the Outlook plug-in, which isn’t supported.

To fix this:

  1. In your Availability page, go to your calendar settings.
  2. Make sure your Calendar to add events to is also marked as a Calendar to check for conflicts.
  3. If you use calendar invitations, go to your event type settings to make sure the event title is included in the invite.
  4. You can switch to email confirmations instead. Learn how here.

No. When you reschedule a meeting, Calendly still follows your event type’s availability and calendar conflict rules.

If a time is blocked, you will not be able to select it during rescheduling.

If you need to book during a blocked time, update your event type settings first.

For a one-time change:

  1. Go to your event type.
  2. Update your availability or calendar conflict settings.
  3. Reschedule the meeting.
  4. Change your settings back if needed.

This lets you book a high-priority meeting without creating a one-off event.

How to edit holidays within Calendly

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly can block off your availability for holidays based on your country. This helps you take time off without needing to adjust your schedule manually. #### Customize your holiday settings

You can edit the list of holidays you observe to match your personal or cultural needs. These settings apply to all your event types.

Calendly supports holiday settings in several countries. You can view the full list below.

  • Australia
  • Brazil
  • Canada
  • France
  • Germany
  • Mexico
  • Netherlands
  • Spain
  • United Kingdom
  • United States

If you want to be available for one event type on a holiday, but not others:

  1. Go to the Availability page.
  2. Turn off the holiday block for that day.
  3. Add Date-specific hours of unavailability to any event types you want to keep unavailable.

Note

You must turn off a holiday block before adding availability for that day. Date-specific hours cannot override an active holiday. #### Manage your holiday settings

  1. Open the Availability page from the left-hand menu.
  2. Click the Holidays tab.
  3. Confirm your country setting.
  4. Use the On/Off toggle next to each holiday:
  • [Image: 16084353553175] On = you’re unavailable for scheduling.
  • [Image: 16084370139543] Off = you’re available for scheduling. #### Need to add a missing holiday?

If a holiday you observe isn’t listed:

  • Add Date-specific hours to your availability.
  • Or, add an all-day busy event to your connected calendar.

For help creating events:

  • Google Calendar Support
  • Microsoft 365 Support

How to fine-tune your availability settings

Quick answer

Here’s how to fine-tune your availability:

  1. Go to your Scheduling page and select the event type you want to update.
  2. Select More options and open the section you want to edit. * Limits and buffers: Set meeting limits and buffer times * Free/busy rules: Choose what this meeting takes priority over * Booking page options: Set start time increments

When you’re done, select Save changes. Then check your booking page to make sure it looks right.

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

In addition to basics like calendar connections, event durations, and buffers, Calendly gives you more ways to control when people can book time with you. #### Adjust start time increments

Start time increments control how often available time slots appear on your booking page. For example, a 30-minute increment displays times like 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, and so on.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and select the event type you want to edit.
  2. Select More options at the bottom of the editor.
  3. Expand the Booking page options section.
  4. Under Start time increments, choose how often start times should appear.
  5. Select Save changes. #### Limit bookings per day, week, or month

Calendly allows you to set meeting limits across event types and hosts to better manage availability and prevent overbooking. Learn how to set meeting limits. #### Prevent last-minute bookings

Minimum scheduling notice lets you require a set amount of time between when someone books and when the meeting starts. For example, setting a 4-hour notice prevents invitees from booking a meeting that begins in less than 4 hours.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and select the event type you want to edit.
  2. Expand the Availability section.
  3. Under Date-range, open the notice dropdown (for example, “4 hours”) and set how much notice is required before a meeting.
  4. Select Save changes. #### Lock the invitee’s time zone

By default, Calendly detects your time zone and your invitee’s time zone. For in-person events, we recommend locking the time zone to the event location. Learn how to lock the invitee’s time zone. #### Hide an event type from your scheduling page

You can hide an event type so it does not appear on your public scheduling page. Invitees can still book it using a direct link. This setting is available on desktop only.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and find the event type you want to update.
  2. Select the [Image: 33336335169431] three dots in the top-right corner of the event type card.
  3. Choose Make secret.

A [Image: 33336377563927] slashed-eye icon appears next to the event name when the event is hidden. To make it public again, open the same menu and select Make public. #### Set your booking date range

Your booking date range controls when invitees can schedule meetings. For example, you can allow bookings for the next 60 days, within a specific date range, or indefinitely.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and select the event type you want to edit.
  2. Expand the Availability section.
  3. Under Date-range, open the range dropdown (for example, “60 days”).
  4. Choose one of the following options:
  • Number of days into the future – set how far ahead invitees can book. Choose calendar days or week days.
  • Within a date range – pick a specific time window for booking.
  • Indefinitely into the future – allow invitees to book anytime.
  1. Select Save changes.

How to manage ‘Busy’ vs. ‘Free’ calendar settings

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Manage your calendar visibility to control when you’re available for scheduling. By setting events on your connected calendar to ‘Busy’ or ‘Free,’ you tell Calendly whether those times should be shown as available to others.

For example, you can:

  • Mark all-day calendar events like holidays as ‘Free’ so they don’t block availability.
  • Set focus time as ‘Busy’ so guests can’t schedule over it.

This setting gives you more control over your availability without editing Calendly directly. It’s helpful if you rely on synced work calendars.

Learn more about managing general availability in Calendly. #### Before you begin

  • Connect your calendar to Calendly.
  • This setting is managed in your external calendar (not in Calendly).
  • Changes made in your calendar will sync to Calendly automatically.
  • All-day events show at the top of your calendar. If set to ‘Busy,’ they can block your whole day. Change them to ‘Free’ if you want to stay available. #### Set an event to ‘Busy’ or ‘Free’ in Google Calendar
  1. Find your event in Google Calendar.
  2. Select the pencil icon to Edit event.
  3. Select the Busy or Free dropdown and choose your status.
  • Calendly marks you as unavailable for events marked as Busy.
  1. Select Save.

[Image: 32483818815255] #### Set an event to ‘Busy’ or ‘Free’ in Outlook or Exchange

  1. Find your calendar event in Outlook.
  2. Select Edit andMore options.
  3. Select the Busy, Free, Working elsewhere, Tentative, or Away/Out of office dropdown and choose your status.
  • By default, Calendly marks Outlook calendars as unavailable for events marked as Busy, Tentative, Away/Out of office, and Working elsewhere.
  • In an Exchange Calendar, if your event status is set to Working elsewhere, Calendly will read you as available.
  • In the What’s considered unavailable? dropdown in your Calendar settings, you can choose how you’d like Calendly to read the statuses you set in your calendar.
  1. Select Save.

[Image: 32483844819223]

How to manage multiple calendars and email addresses

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Learn how to connect more calendars and email accounts in Calendly to save time and avoid double bookings. #### Connect more than one calendar

Calendly checks all your connected calendars to help you avoid being double booked. Depending on your plan, you can connect between one and six calendar accounts per user. Check our Pricing page to see what your plan includes.

If your plan allows more than one calendar, follow the steps in this article to add another.

Only allowed to connect one calendar? You can still see events from other calendars by sharing them with the one you’ve connected. Be sure to share with read and write access so Calendly can view them.

Need help? Use these guides to share your calendar:

  • Google Calendar
  • Office 365/Outlook.com

Note

You can’t link specific event types to different calendars. Calendar connections apply to all event types. If you need more control, consider adding another user to your Calendly organization. #### Check multiple users’ calendars

Calendly supports several ways to schedule with teams. Choose what works best for your setup:

  • Assign events by availability using Round Robin or priority order
  • Let invitees choose who they want to meet with
  • Pool availability so invitees can only book when all hosts are free
  • Schedule with groups of hosts

See more in our multi-user scheduling guide. #### Send notifications to more email addresses

By default, Calendly sends notifications to the email address you use to log in. If you’re on the Standard plan or higher, you can use a Workflow to send notifications to others using the Email someone else option.

If you’re not using Workflows, you can forward notifications using your email settings. #### For Gmail users:

  1. Add a forwarding address in Gmail settings.
  2. Create a filter.
  3. Filter by sender: notifications@calendly.com and no-reply@calendly.com.
  4. (Optional) Filter by event title in the subject line. #### For Outlook users:

Set up a forwarding rule in Outlook Web App. If you’re using Outlook on your desktop, the steps may be different depending on your version.

How to set meeting limits

Quick answer

Here’s how to set up meeting limits:

  1. Go to your Scheduling page and open the Event Type you want to edit.
  2. Select More options, then find Limits and buffers.
  3. Turn on Meeting limits and choose how many times this Event Type can be booked per day, week, or month.
  4. Save your changes so the limits apply.

The next time someone books this Event Type, Calendly will enforce the limits you set.

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

You can use meeting limits to control how many meetings can be booked with you in a set time frame. Calendly offers two types of meeting limits:

  • Limits for an Event Type - control how many times a specific Event Type can be booked.
  • Limits across all of your Event Types - control how many total meetings can be booked through your account, across all event types.

Meeting limits help you prevent overbooking and protect time for other priorities. #### Before you begin

  • You can set up both types of meeting limits. Whichever limit is reached first will make you unavailable to invitees.
  • Admins can view host limits in the Event Type editor, user profile, and Troubleshoot Tool, but they can’t create or edit them. Users must manage their own limits. #### Set meeting limits for an Event Type

Limit how many times a specific Event Type can be booked per day, week, or month.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. Find the event type and select it to open the editor.
  3. Select More options and open the Limits and buffers section.
  4. Under Meeting limits, select + Set limit.
  5. Set the maximum number of meetings that can be booked per day, week, or month.
  6. When you’re done, select Save changes. #### Set meeting limits across all of your Event Types

Limit the total number of meetings booked through your account per day, week, or month.

  1. Go to the Availability page > Advanced settings tab.
  2. Under Meeting limits, select + Add a meeting limit.
  3. Set your maximum number of meetings that can be booked per day, week, or month.
  4. Your settings will be saved automatically. #### Troubleshooting meeting limits

If your availability disappears unexpectedly, it may be due to a meeting limit being reached.

You can use the Troubleshoot Tool to check for possible causes. If a meeting limit is blocking availability, you’ll see an error code.

Limits for an Event Type

  • DAILY MAX
  • WEEKLY MAX
  • MONTHLY MAX

To fix it, go to the Event Type settings and increase or remove the limit.

Limits for a host

  • MEETING LIMIT

To fix it, go to your Availability page and increase or remove the limit. Admins are unable to edit these limits.

How to set your availability

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

This article shows you how to set your availability in Calendly. You’ll learn how to edit or create a schedule, add custom hours, and set date-specific hours for certain days.

With Schedules, you can make different sets of hours for different event types. You can use the same schedule for many events, or make custom hours for just one.

Calendly also checks your connected calendar(s) to avoid double bookings. #### Create a schedule

  1. Go to your Availability page.

  2. Expand the Schedule dropdown menu.

  3. Select + Create schedule.

  4. Name the new schedule.

  5. Select Create. #### Edit a schedule

  6. Go to your Availability page.

  7. Expand the Schedule dropdown menu.

  8. Select + Create schedule.

  9. Name the new schedule.

  10. Select Create. #### List view – for schedules that repeat weekly

Set your Weekly hours in List view for availability that will repeat each week.

  1. Go to your Availability page.
  2. Open your schedule in List view.
  3. Under Weekly hours:
  • Select the + to Add the days you want to be available each week.
  • Select the x to Remove any days you want to be unavailable each week.
  1. Set your start and end times for each time block.
  • To add another time block (like after lunch), select the +.
  • To remove a time block, select the x.

When you’re done, assign this schedule to your event types using the Active on dropdown. #### Calendar view – for non-weekly schedules

Set a non-weekly schedule in Calendar view for availability that does not repeat weekly.

  1. Go to your Availability page.
  2. Open your schedule in List view and locate your Weekly hours.
  3. Select the x next each time block to remove weekly hours.
  4. Switch to Calendar view.
  5. Select the first date you want to update or select and drag over multiple dates.

  • If selecting one day, choose to either:

  • Edit date, or

  • Edit all [day of the week]

  1. Set your start and end times for each time block.
  • To add another time block (like after lunch), select the +.
  • To remove a time block, select the x.
  1. Select Apply.

When you’re done, assign this schedule to your event types using the Active on dropdown. #### Set date-specific hours

Use date-specific hours to change your availability on certain days.

  1. Go to your Availability page.
  2. In List view, locate Date-specific hours and select + Hours.
  3. Pick the date(s) you want to change.
  4. Add or remove time blocks.
  5. Select Apply. #### Assign a schedule to your event types

After you make a schedule, you need to apply it to your event types.

From the Availability page:

  1. Go to your Availability page.
  2. From the Schedule dropdown menu, select your schedule.
  3. Open the Active on dropdown.
  4. Select the event types you want to assign to this schedule.
  5. Select Apply.

From the event type editor:

  1. Open the event.
  2. Go to Availability.
  3. Locate and expand the Schedule: dropdown.
  4. Select the schedule you want to apply.
  5. Select Save changes. #### Set custom hours for an event type

Use a custom schedule to set different availability for one event type. These changes only apply to this event and won’t affect your other schedules.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and select your event type.
  2. Expand the Availability section.
  3. Locate and expand the Schedule: dropdown.
  4. Select Custom schedule.
  5. Edit your schedule.
  6. Select Save changes. #### Copy hours between events

You can copy your Custom schedules from one event to another.

To do this:

  1. Open the event you want to update.
  2. Go to Availability.
  3. Select the [Image: 31489132846487] Apply to/from event types icon.
  4. Choose if you want to Apply to or Copy from.
  5. Select your event type(s).
  6. Select Apply.

Note

For Collective or Round Robin event types, you can only apply or copy hours when you’ve set available hours by individual host. You will not be able to apply or copy hours to Collective or Round Robin event types where all hosts are set to share the same availability. #### What’s Next?

Now that you’ve set up your availability, here are some other resources to check out!

  • How to troubleshoot unavailable times that should be available: This guide helps walk through troubleshooting your availability when you should be available.
  • How to troubleshoot available times that should be unavailable: This guide helps walk through troubleshooting your availability when you should be unavailable.
  • How to fine-tune your availability settings: Explore more ways to control when people can book time with you.

How to troubleshoot available times that should be unavailable

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Appearing available when you should be busy? Here’s how to fix it.

Note

Are you appearing unavailable when you should be free? Learn how to resolve this. #### Step 1 – Review your calendar connection

Make sure Calendly is checking the right calendar for conflicts:

  1. Go to the Calendar settings in your Availability page.
  2. Check that the calendar or sub-calendar with your events is selected as a calendar to check for conflicts.
  3. Confirm your events are marked as “Busy” in your connected calendar. #### Step 2 – Check your availability setup

Discrepancies between your availability and scheduling link might be due to availability settings on your Availability page or in the Event Type editor.

If using your Availability page:

  • Make sure the schedule is assigned to the event type.
  • Use the Active On dropdown to confirm it’s applied to the right events.

If using the Event Type editor:

  • Adjust hours directly in the Availability section of the editor for that event type.
  • Note: Date-specific hours here only apply to that one event type.

How to troubleshoot unavailable times that should be available

Quick answer

To troubleshoot unavailable times that should be available:

  1. Open the event type you want to review from your Scheduling page.
  2. Select Preview.
  3. Click Troubleshoot at the bottom of the preview page.
  4. Choose the date and time that appear unavailable but should be open.
  5. Review the list of reasons explaining why the time is not available.

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Are times showing as unavailable when they should be free? The Troubleshoot Tool can help you see why invitees can’t book with you and how to fix it.

Note

Are invitees scheduling time with you when you’re busy? Learn how to resolve this. #### Step 1 – Find and open the Troubleshoot Tool

To access the tool:

  1. Log in to your Calendly account.

  2. Open the live scheduling page or preview of your event type.

  3. Scroll down and select Troubleshoot. #### Step 2 – Check what’s blocking your time

  4. Choose the date you’re investigating.

  5. Review the time and corresponding troubleshoot code.

If no dates or times appear, go to the Availability of your event type and review your settings. #### Step 3 – What each code means and how to fix it

Each code shows why a time isn’t available. Use these tables to find the reason and learn how to fix it. #### Calendar sync

These codes mean something in your connected calendar is blocking a time. You may need to change an event or reconnect your calendar.

  • Code: CALENDAR; What it means: A “Busy” calendar event is blocking the time.; How to fix it: Change the event to “Free”or remove it from your connected calendar.
  • Code: NOCAL; What it means: Calendly can’t access your calendar.; How to fix it: Reconnect your calendar from Calendar settings.

Event Type settings

These codes come from your event’s rules. You might need to change limits, time ranges, or notice settings so invitees can book again.

  • Code: DAILY MAX; What it means: You’ve hit the daily meeting limit for that event type.; How to fix it: Adjust limits under Limits and buffers in the event editor.
  • Code: DURATION; What it means: Not enough time for your event.; How to fix it: Shorten the event or extend your availability.
  • Code: MONTHLY MAX; What it means: You’ve hit the monthly meeting limit for that event type.; How to fix it: Adjust limits under Limits and buffers in the event editor.
  • Code: RANGE; What it means: The date is outside your availability window.; How to fix it: Adjust the date range in the Availability section of your event type settings.
  • Code: TOOSOON; What it means: The time is too soon based on your minimum notice rules.; How to fix it: Adjust your minimum scheduling notice.
  • Code: WEEKLY MAX; What it means: You’ve hit the weekly meeting limit for that event type.; How to fix it: Adjust limits under Limits and buffers in the event editor.

Calendly meetings

These codes show that another Calendly meeting is blocking the time. You can fix this by rescheduling or adjusting meeting rules.

  • Code: EVENT; What it means: Another Calendly event of this event type is booked.; How to fix it: Reschedule from your Meetings page or use Free/busy rules to allow overlapping.
  • Code: GROUP; What it means: Group event has max attendees.; How to fix it: Increase the max invitee number from the Meetings page.
  • Code: OVERLAP; What it means: Another Calendly event is booked.; How to fix it: Reschedule from your Meetings page or enable Free/busy rules.

Availability settings

These codes mean something in your general availability is blocking bookings, like a holiday or meeting limit.

  • Code: HOLIDAY; What it means: This date is marked as a holiday.; How to fix it: Edit holidays from your Availability page.
  • Code: MEETING LIMIT; What it means: A meeting limit has been reached for this host.; How to fix it: The host must adjust the meeting limit in their own account.

Team scheduling

These codes appear for team events, like Collective or Round Robin. They tell you when a host isn’t available or when scheduling rules need an update.

  • Code: HOST; What it means: One or more hosts are unavailable for a Collective event type.; How to fix it: Make sure all hosts are free at the desired time.
  • Code: ROUNDROBIN; What it means: No host is available based on the distribution rules.; How to fix it: Update Round Robin host availability or distribution settings.
  • Code: UNFAIR; What it means: Scheduling at this time would distribute meetings unfairly between assigned hosts.; How to fix it: Adjust distribution settings for Round Robin events.

Edge conditions / System exceptions

These codes show special cases that stop scheduling, like buffers, past times, or reserved spots.

  • Code: BUFFER; What it means: A buffer is blocking this time.; How to fix it: Edit or remove the buffer from the Meetings page.
  • Code: PAST; What it means: The selected time is in the past.; How to fix it: Choose a future date.
  • Code: RESERVED; What it means: A poll or pending meeting is holding this time.; How to fix it: Clear reserved times from the Single-use Links or Meeting polls tab of the Scheduling page.

Frequently asked questions

Calendly continues to block times for events it created—even if marked “free” in your connected calendar. Cancel or reschedule the event in Calendly, or enable Free/busy rules to allow booking over these events.

Check for all-day events marked as “Busy”. Still not sure? Review your calendars for conflicts, including Calendar setting for extra calendars. Learn more about managing ‘Busy’ vs. ‘Free’ calendar statuses.

Calendly adjusts automatically. Times remain accurate, though time zone labels may not reflect the change right away.

You can manage schedules for your teammates or create different availability for multiple event types.

Set date specific hours to adjust your availability on the days you’re traveling. Each schedule is set in one time zone. Enter your hours according to when you’ll be available locally, and Calendly will display the right times to your invitees.

How to use buffers

Quick answer

Here’s how to add time before or after meetings using buffers:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and select the event type you want to edit.
  2. Select More options, then Limits and buffers.
  3. Select + Set buffer time.
  4. Add your preferred buffer time before and/or after the meeting.
  5. Select Save changes.

Your buffer changes will apply to new bookings and help prevent back-to-back meetings.

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Buffers add extra time before or after your meetings. They help you prep, travel, or wrap up without feeling rushed. #### What are buffers?

Buffers are short breaks before or after a Calendly meeting. Use them to:

  • Prepare before a meeting
  • Travel between meetings
  • Take notes or reset after a call

Each event type can have its own buffer settings. #### Add a buffer to an event type

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. Click More options.
  4. Open the Limits and buffers section.
  5. Click + Set buffer time.
  6. Add your preferred buffer time before and/or after the meeting.
  7. Click Save changes. #### Remove a buffer

For meetings not yet scheduled:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.

  2. Open the [Image: 33458179544471] three dots menu and select Edit.

  3. Click More options.

  4. Open the Limits and buffers section.

  5. Set the buffer time to 0 minutes.

  6. Click Save changes. #### For meetings already scheduled:

  7. Go to your Meetings page.

  8. Make sure Show buffers is turned on.

  9. Find the meeting and click the pencil icon next to the buffer.

  10. Edit or delete the buffer. #### Show or delete buffers on your calendar

You can choose to display buffers on your connected calendar.

To turn this on:

  1. Go to your Availability page.
  2. Open Calendar settings.
  3. Under Sync settings, check Include buffers on this calendar.

When this is enabled, deleting a buffer from your connected calendar will also remove it from Calendly. #### How buffer logic works

  • Buffers apply only to meetings booked through Calendly.
  • Calendly avoids overlaps by checking your entire calendar — including non-Calendly events.

[Image: 16767019958551]

Example: A 30-minute meeting with 15-minute buffers before and after needs 60 minutes of free time. The meeting stays 30 minutes long, but the buffer time protects your availability.

[Image: 16767004069143] #### Multi-user meetings and buffers

Buffer settings from one user can impact the availability of multi-user meetings.

  • Round robin: Buffers on other event types can cause uneven meeting distribution.
  • Collective events: Buffers on someone’s other events might block available time slots. #### Troubleshooting: BUFFER message

Calendly’s troubleshooting tool may show a BUFFER message. This means buffer settings are blocking a time slot.

You may see it if:

  • A buffer overlaps with a meeting
  • The total time (meeting + buffer) doesn’t fit in your calendar
  • Old buffer settings are still attached to a scheduled meeting #### Troubleshooting other buffer issues

A non-Calendly event may be blocking time. Try one of these:

  • Delete the conflicting event or set its calendar status to free (Remember to check your all day events!)
  • Change the buffer time to 0 minutes for the event type you’re trying to schedule

Buffers on scheduled meetings don’t update automatically when you change your event type settings. If a meeting was booked before you changed the settings, it will still follow the old rules.

To check or remove these:

  1. Go to your Meetings page
  2. Use the Show buffers toggle
  3. Edit the buffer directly

This might be caused by double buffers — using both a before and after buffer. When stacked, these buffers can block more time than you expect.

[Image: 26280084699031]

To fix it:

  • Edit the event type to use only a before or after buffer, not both
  • For already booked meetings, adjust or remove buffers from your Meetings page

Connect your calendar to Calendly

Quick answer

Here’s how to connect your calendar to Calendly so your availability stays in sync and avoids double bookings:

  1. In Calendly, go to Availability → Calendar settings.
  2. Select + Connect calendar account and choose your calendar type (for example, Google, Outlook/Office 365, or Exchange).
  3. Sign in to your calendar account and allow access.
  4. Select the calendar(s) Calendly should check for conflicts, and choose where new bookings go.
  5. Save your settings and make sure your calendar shows as connected.

Once connected, Calendly checks your calendar for busy times and adds new meetings to it. If you connect more than one calendar, choose one as your main calendar for bookings.

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Connecting your calendar to Calendly helps you manage availability and keep your meetings in sync.

For example, you can:

  • Check for conflicts and avoid double-booking
  • Automatically add Calendly meetings to your calendar
  • Coordinate team availability using features like Collective and Round Robin #### Before you begin

Supported calendars

You can connect any of these calendar platforms to Calendly:

Ready to set up your calendar account? These Help Center articles show you how to connect each calendar.

Some calendar types include extra options, like canceling and rescheduling a Calendly meeting from your calendar. To see what’s available, check the setup article for your calendar type above. #### FAQs

Connected calendars apply to all event types in your account. You can’t assign different calendars to individual events. To keep things separate, add another user to your organization.

Calendly events are added to one calendar only. If you’ve connected multiple calendars, you’ll choose a primary calendar where all scheduled events are created.

Check that your Add to calendar setting matches the calendar you want to use. Make sure your calendar connection is active and up to date.

If you see a calendar error, try reconnecting your calendar.

How Calendly uses your calendar data

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Beta

This functionality is currently in beta for select users.

When you connect your calendar to Calendly, we use limited scheduling data to personalize your setup. This helps you get started faster with tips, integrations, and features that match your workflow. #### What this means

Calendly may use your calendar to:

  • Suggest teammates you meet with often, so you can invite them to your team.
  • Recommend integrations or setup steps that match how you already work.
  • Highlight tips and features based on how you use your calendar.

We only use basic scheduling info—like who you meet with and how often—to personalize your experience. #### How to turn off calendar-based personalization

You can disable this at any time by disconnecting your calendar:

  1. Go to Account Settings >Calendar Connections.
  2. Locate your connected calendar.
  3. Select the X to Disconnect.

Once disconnected, Calendly stops using your calendar data to customize onboarding. You can reconnect at any time.

Note

Disconnecting your calendar also turns off availability syncing. This may lead to double-bookings, and your availability won’t reflect real-time updates until you reconnect your calendar. #### Your privacy and security

Calendly uses limited calendar data only to enhance your experience. Any suggestions based on your calendar are visible only to you.

How to allow Google Calendar invitations from unknown senders

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Google Calendar has a built-in setting to prevent spam. By default, events are only added to your calendar automatically if you’ve interacted with the sender before. This affects all scheduling tools, including Calendly.

If you’re using Calendly and a first-time invitee books with you, they may need to confirm the event before it appears on their calendar. This article shows how to update your Google Calendar settings so events from all senders are added automatically. #### Default behavior

If your invitees haven’t interacted with you before, they’ll see a grey banner that says: Unknown sender: not added to calendar yet

They’ll need to click I know the sender, then respond Yes to the invite for it to appear on their calendar. #### Change your Google Calendar settings

To allow all invitations to be added to your Google Calendar:

  1. Open Google Calendar.
  2. Click the gear icon in the top right corner and select Settings.
  3. In the left-hand menu, select Event settings under General.
  4. Find Add invitations to my calendar.
  5. From the dropdown, select From everyone. #### Tips to reduce no-shows

Here are a few ways to keep invitees informed and improve attendance:

  • Use reminders: If you’re on a Standard, Teams, or Enterprise plan, set up email or SMS reminders using Workflows.

  • Link to Google Calendar instructions: Add a link to your confirmation page to guide invitees on updating their settings.

After connecting, you can choose which calendars Calendly checks for conflicts and which calendar new meetings are added to.

Connect your Google Calendar to Calendly to check your availability, prevent double bookings, and automatically add scheduled meetings. #### Connect your Google Calendar

Step 1 – Go to your calendar settings

From your Calendly home page:

  • Select Availability from the sidebar.
  • At the top of the page, select the Calendar settings tab. #### Step 2 – Connect your Google account

In your Calendar settings, connect your calendar account.

  • If you signed up using a Google email address, your calendar may already be connected. If it’s listed here, you’re all set.

Sign in to your Google account when the sign-in window opens. Once you’re signed in, you’ll return to the Calendar settings page. #### Customize how Calendly uses your Google Calendar

After you connect your Google Calendar, you can manage how Calendly checks your availability, adds new meetings, and handles changes. #### Calendars to check for conflicts

Choose the calendars you want Calendly to check for availability. You’ll be marked as unavailable during any busy events on those calendars. #### Calendar to add events to

Choose the calendar where Calendly should add new meetings. Calendly won’t add events to any other calendar. #### Sync settings

Control how Calendly and Google Calendar stay in sync with these optional settings:

  • Include buffers on this calendar: Calendly adds buffer time before and after your scheduled meetings as separate events in your Google Calendar. When you delete a buffer event in Google Calendar, it’ll also be removed from Calendly.

  • Automatically sync cancellations and reschedules from this calendar to Calendly:

  • When you decline or delete a Calendly meeting in Google Calendar, it’ll also be canceled in Calendly.

  • When you update the date or time of a Calendly meeting in Google Calendar, it’ll also be rescheduled in Calendly.

  • If invitees change or delete the event in their own calendars, it won’t affect the meeting. #### Turn off Google’s automatic video links

By default, Google Calendar may automatically add a video conferencing link, like Google Meet, to all new events you create.

To update this setting, see Google’s article on turning off automatic video links. If you’re using a managed Google Workspace account, your admin may need to make this change by following these instructions.

How to connect your Microsoft Exchange calendar

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Connect your Exchange calendar to let Calendly check for busy times and add events automatically. Learn how to set up your Exchange connection. #### Before you begin

Version & Server Information:

  • Calendly supports Exchange versions 2013, 2016, and 2019.
  • Your Exchange account must utilize an EWS connection. ActiveSync connections are not currently supported.
  • If you are using Exchange via Amazon WorkMail, this endpoint acts on a version of Exchange that is not supported at this time.
  • Exchange IMAP/POP connections are currently unsupported.
  • If your Exchange calendar connection has a 2FA/MFA set up enabled, you will need to utilize our Microsoft Outlook Plug-In (for Windows users) instead. #### Connect an Exchange calendar to Calendly

Step 1 – Visit your Calendar settings page

  1. On your home page, go to the left-side navigation panel and select Availability.
  2. At the top of the page, select Calendar settings. #### Step 2 – Select the calendar you’d like to connect

  • If you haven’t connected a calendar yet:

  • Next to Exchange Calendar, select Connect.

  • If you’ve already connected a calendar:

  • You can add additional calendar accounts by selecting + Connect Calendar Account.

  • Select Exchange calendar. #### Step 3 – Sign in to your Exchange account

Enter your Exchange email address and password. Calendly will try to automatically detect your Exchange server.

If we can’t automatically detect your Exchange server, we’ll ask you to enter your Exchange server and your Domain and/or Username.

If you are unsure about your Server, Domain, or Username, ask your IT department or check the following Outlook settings:

  • iPhone Mail App: In Settings, select Accounts, then Exchange. Find the Server field which contains the Exchange server URL.

  • Mac Outlook: Select Preferences, then Accounts. Select your work account and click on Advanced. In the Microsoft Exchange section, copy the address in the Server field.

  • Windows Outlook: Select File, then Account settings. Double-click the email account from the list. Copy the address in the Server field.

  • Check Windows Lock Screen: If using a company PC, the domain name may be visible on the lock screen in the format Domain/Username.

  • iPhone Mail App: In Settings, select Mail Accounts, then choose the Exchange account.

  • Mac Outlook: Open Preferences Accounts, and check the server information under the account settings.

  • Windows Outlook: Go to File Account Settings, then double-click the email account to see the server information.

  • Check Windows Lock Screen: If using a company PC, the domain name may be visible on the lock screen in the format Domain/Username.

  • iPhone Mail App: Go to Settings and select Mail. Select Accounts, then choose the Exchange account. The username may be listed in the account details.

  • Mac Outlook: Go to Preferences Accounts. For your work account, click on Advanced. The username may be displayed in the settings.

  • Windows Outlook: Go to File Account Settings, then double-click the email account to see the server information.

Once authenticated, you’ll be redirected back to the Calendar settings page. #### Specify which calendar Calendly checks for conflicts

Note: Calendly can only check your primary Exchange calendar for conflicts. Calendly cannot check sub-calendars or shared calendars on your Exchange calendar.

  1. From left-side navigation panel, select Availability.

  2. At the top of the page, select Calendar settings.

  3. In the Calendars to check for conflicts section, select your Exchange calendar connection, and select your desired calendar(s).

  4. Select Update. #### Change the calendar Calendly adds events to

  5. From the left-side navigation panel, select Availability.

  6. At the top of the page, select Calendar settings.

  7. In the Calendar to add events to section, expand the dropdown.

  8. Select the calendar you want to add new events to. #### Working elsewhere status

In your Exchange Calendar, if your event status is set to “Working elsewhere”, Calendly will read you as available.

The “Working elsewhere” status is only available on Outlook on the Web. If you view a “Working elsewhere” event on Outlook for desktop, the event status will show as busy, but Calendly will still read you as available from the Exchange server. #### What to do if Calendly can’t connect to your Exchange server

If Calendly can’t connect to your Exchange server with only an email address and password, try the following options:

  1. Add your “Exchange server” in EWS URL format and leave Domain and Username empty.

  • EWS URL format: **mail.example.com where “mail.example.com” is replaced with your unique server information.

    Note: This URL is different than the one you normally use to access your email in the browser. How to find your Exchange Server.

  1. If that doesn’t work, try adding your Domain and/or Username. How to find your Exchange Domain and Username.

Need Help?

If your Exchange version meets the requirements mentioned above and you are still running into issues, we recommend reaching out to our support team for assistance or utilizing our Microsoft Outlook Plug-In connection (for Windows only). #### How Calendly stores your Exchange credentials

We take securing your credentials extremely seriously. Here’s how.

  1. When you provide your login credentials to connect your Exchange calendar to Calendly, we send your email and password to our servers through an encrypted SSL connection.
  2. Once your credentials reach our servers, we encrypt them before storing them in our database. We store the encryption key as an environment variable on our servers, ensuring even more security.
  3. When we need to access your Exchange calendar, we decrypt your credentials in memory. We never store your decrypted credentials anywhere.

All of this ensures that your Exchange calendar credentials are safely stored using industry best practices.

Connect your Microsoft Office 365 or Outlook.com Calendar to check your availability, prevent double bookings, and automatically add scheduled meetings. #### Connect your Outlook calendar

Choose the calendar where Calendly should add new meetings. Calendly won’t add events to any other calendar. #### Sync settings

Control how Calendly and Outlook Calendar stay in sync with these optional settings:

  • Include buffers on this calendar: Calendly adds buffer time before and after your scheduled meetings as separate events in your Outlook Calendar. When you delete a buffer event in Outlook Calendar, it’ll also be removed from Calendly.

  • Deleting or declining an event in your calendar will also cancel it in Calendly:

  • When you decline or delete a Calendly meeting in Outlook Calendar, it’ll also be canceled in Calendly.

  • If invitees change or delete the event in their own calendars, it won’t affect the meeting. #### Consent and admin approval

How to install or uninstall the Outlook plug-in

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

The Outlook plug-in is a tool designed to connect Calendly to your desktop Outlook calendar if you are unable to use the Office 365/Outlook.com connection. #### Before you begin

Compatible versions

  • The Outlook plug-in is available for Windows only and is not available on Mac.

  • To use the plug-in, you’ll need:

  • Outlook 2007 or later

  • Windows XP or newer

  • The plug-in doesn’t work with Outlook versions downloaded from the Microsoft Store. You’ll need the version from your O365 account.

  • Each Calendly account supports one plug-in connection only. #### Outlook plug-in vs. Outlook add-in

The Outlook plug-in connects your Outlook calendar to Calendly to check for conflicts and add events. It is separate from the Outlook add-in, which allows you to share your scheduling links and availability from your Outlook toolbar. #### Install the Outlook plug-in

To get started, contact our support team. They’ll send you a link to download the plug-in. You must be logged in to Calendly to access the link.

  1. Download the plug-in and save the file.
  • If you see a security pop-up, be sure to allow permissions to begin installing. Depending on your browser, you may need to locate and open the downloaded file to run the installation.
  1. Calendly will generate a unique key for you to copy and paste into your plug-in settings. Enter your plug-in key. [Image: 26278112440343]
  2. Choose which calendar accounts you want to check for conflicts.
  • Busy events on these calendars will be marked as unavailable.
  1. Select the calendar where you’d like new meetings to be added.
  2. Select Save. #### Sync the Outlook plug-in

The plug-in will only sync when it is running in the background and your computer is connected to the internet.

To manually sync your meetings:

  • Open the plug-in.
  • Click Sync Now in the bottom-left corner.

You’ll see the date and time of the last sync between Outlook and Calendly. #### Uninstall the Outlook plug-in

If you’re experiencing an issue with the plug-in, you can troubleshoot common issues with the help of Troubleshooting the Outlook plug-in.

  1. From the Windows Settings menu, select System.
  2. Under System on the left-hand side, select Apps & features and locate the Calendly Plugin for Outlook on the right-hand side.
  3. Select Uninstall.
  4. At “Do you want to view troubleshooting help before uninstalling?”:
  • Selecting Yes will direct you to our Help Center.
  • Selecting No will allow you to continue the uninstall process.
  1. Select Uninstall to uninstall the plug-in.
  2. Select Ok.

Note

If you plan to reinstall the plug-in later, first disconnect your calendar integration:

  1. Log into your Calendly account.
  2. Navigate to your Integrations page.
  3. Find your Outlook Plug-in connection and select the X to disconnect. #### Frequently asked questions

To choose how you’d like Calendly to read the Tentative, Away/Out of Office, and Working Elsewhere statuses you set in your calendar, set your preferences using the What’s considered unavailable? dropdown in the Calendars to check for conflicts section of your Calendar settings.

Need help? Check out our troubleshooting article.

Outlook plug-in overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

The Outlook plug-in, sometimes called the Calendly plug-in for Outlook or the Outlook desktop plug-in, is a tool designed to connect Calendly to your desktop Outlook calendar if you are unable to use the Office 365/Outlook.com connection.

  • Important settings requirements:

The Outlook plug-in connects your Outlook calendar to Calendly to check for conflicts and add events. It is separate from the Outlook add-in, which allows you to share your scheduling links and availability from your Outlook toolbar. #### Setting up the Outlook plug-in

Important

If you have a firewall, ensure that calendly.exe is added to the allowlist for successful synchronization.

Communication tools

How to use and manage Recommended Follow-ups

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users. Release notes

Learn how to send follow-ups, manage your recommended contacts, and adjust your preferences for Recommended Follow-ups. #### Before you begin

  • Connect the Gmail for Workflows integration #### Access your Recommended Follow-ups

View contacts who haven’t booked yet after you’ve shared availability with them.

From Contacts

  1. Go to Contacts.
  2. Select View [X] recommended follow-ups to see all your recommended follow-ups.

Note

The View [X] recommended follow-ups link only appears if you have contacts in Calendly.

From the weekly email

Calendly sends you a weekly email with up to five recommended follow-ups.

  1. Open the weekly Recommended follow-ups email in your inbox.
  2. Select Review follow-up emails. #### Follow-up from the Recommended Follow-ups page

You can send follow-ups directly from Calendly.

  1. Go to Contacts.
  2. Select View [X] recommended follow-ups to access your Recommended follow-ups page.
  3. Find the contact you want to follow up with.
  4. Review the suggested follow-up message. It will appear below the contact’s name.
  5. Edit the message if needed.
  6. Select Send.

The contact will receive your follow-up email right away. #### Manage contacts on your list

You can control which contacts appear on your Recommended Follow-ups page.

Remove a contact from the list permanently

  1. Go to Contacts.
  2. Select View [X] recommended follow-ups to access your Recommended follow-ups list.
  3. Find the contact.
  4. Select Dismiss (the X icon).

The contact is removed from your list and future emails.

View the most recent email thread

Each contact row shows the last email between you and them. Select the message to expand it and see the full conversation. #### Adjust your notification preferences

You can manage when and how often you get Recommended Follow-ups emails from Settings → → Notifications.

Unsubscribe from weekly emails

  1. Open any Recommended follow-ups email.
  2. Select Unsubscribe at the bottom of the email.
  3. You’ll no longer receive weekly follow-up emails.

Re-enable emails

  1. Go to Settings → Notifications.
  2. Find Recommended follow-ups.
  3. Toggle the setting on to start receiving emails again. #### Understand when contacts appear and disappear

Contacts only show up on your list if they meet certain conditions.

Contacts appear when:

  • You shared your availability from Calendly with them in the last 3 days
  • They haven’t booked a meeting yet
  • They haven’t already received a follow-up from you

Contacts disappear when they:

  • Book a meeting
  • Just received a follow-up from you
  • Are dismissed by you
  • Fall outside the three-day window

Recommended Follow-ups overview

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users. Release notes

Recommended follow-ups automatically identifies contacts who haven’t booked after you shared availability. Get weekly emails with follow-up suggestions and send messages directly from Calendly.

For example, you can:

  • Review a weekly email showing the top contacts who need follow-up, along with when you sent them your scheduling link
  • Easily send a personalized follow-up message
  • Use prefilled templates to save time writing follow-up emails
  • Manage all follow-ups in one organized page inside Calendly #### Before you begin

Recommended follow-ups is available for users with the Gmail for Workflows integration enabled. You’ll receive a weekly email only if you have contacts who meet the follow-up criteria.

The feature sends emails to contacts you’ve shared availability with in the last three days who haven’t scheduled a meeting yet. If you previously followed up with someone, they won’t appear again. #### Setting up Recommended follow-ups

Recommended follow-ups turns on automatically once you connect the Gmail for Workflows integration. Here are the key resources to get started.

  • How to connect Gmail for Workflows integration
  • How to use and manage recommended follow-ups #### Best practices

For all users:

  • Review your weekly email to catch scheduling opportunities early. The sooner you follow up, the better your chances of booking a meeting.
  • Use the prefilled template as a starting point, but feel free to personalize your message. A personal touch increases response rates.
  • Check the Recommended follow-ups page regularly. New contacts appear here before they show up in the weekly email.
  • Dismiss contacts who’ve already booked or who aren’t good fits. This keeps your list focused on real opportunities. #### Frequently asked questions

You’ll get one email per week. The email includes up to five contacts who need follow-up, sorted by when you sent them your scheduling link.

Yes. You can unsubscribe from the emails at any time by selecting the unsubscribe link at the bottom of the email.

You can dismiss them from the Recommended follow-ups page. They won’t appear in future emails or on your list.

No. Recommended follow-ups emails look like regular emails from you. There’s nothing that shows it came from Calendly’s automated follow-up feature.

The contact gets your email right away. If they book a meeting, they’re removed from your Recommended follow-ups list. If they don’t book within the next week, you might see them again in a future email.

Embed options

Advanced Calendly embed for developers

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Control how Calendly works on your website. Use the advanced JavaScript embed to customize how and when Calendly appears. You can pre-fill invitee info, track events, hide details, and more. #### Set up the embed with JavaScript

Add Calendly to a specific element on your page:

javascript

Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK',parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed')});

Required setup:

  1. Include the Calendly script in your HTML:

html

<script src="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js" type="text/javascript"></script>
  1. Add a container element for the embed:

html

<div id="calendly-embed" style="min-width:320px;height:700px;"></div>

Include the 0 to control where the embed appears. Without it, Calendly will load at the bottom of your webpage. #### Pre-fill booking answers

Learn about pre-filling booking answers. #### Auto-resize the Calendly embed

By default, the embed has a fixed height. If the content is longer, it may scroll inside the widget. You can make the height adjust automatically. #### Use standard embed

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget"data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK"data-resize="true"style="min-width:320px;height:700px;"></div>

Use advanced JavaScript embed

javascript

Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK',parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed'),resize: true});

Important:

  • Only use one auto-resizing embed per page to prevent layout problems.
  • Avoid dropdowns in booking or routing forms when using auto-resize. #### Hide profile info or the cookie banner

Learn how to customize your embed to hide profile info or the cookie banner. #### Track actions with postMessage

Calendly sends events when someone interacts with the embed. You can listen for these to trigger actions or track behavior.

Events sent:

  • 0
  • 0
  • 0
  • 0

Example:

javascript

function isCalendlyEvent(e) {return e.origin === "https://calendly.com" && e.data.event?.startsWith("calendly.");}window.addEventListener("message", function(e) {if (isCalendlyEvent(e)) {console.log("Calendly Event:", e.data.event);console.log("Event Details:", e.data.payload);}});

Calendly uses 0 to send these events to the parent window. #### Use an iframe (alternative method)

Calendly loads in an iframe by default. If you prefer, you can embed Calendly using direct iframe code:

html

<iframe src="https://calendly.com/YOUR_SCHEDULING_LINK"style="width: 100%; min-width: 320px; height: 700px;" frameborder="0"></iframe>

Note: Iframes do not support auto-resize or event tracking via 0.

Calendly embed and the API

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly offers embed options and an API to help you add scheduling to your website or app. This article explains what each tool does — and when to use them. #### What you can do with the API

Calendly’s public API lets you:

  • Get your scheduling links
  • View users, event types, and scheduled events
  • Sync Calendly activity with other systems

With the API, you can:

  • List a user’s event types
  • Update an event type
  • Get the scheduling link for a user or team
  • See meeting details
  • And more #### What you can’t do with the API

The API doesn’t support:

  • Booking meetings
  • Showing the full booking flow

If you want visitors to book with you, use an embed instead. #### When to use an embed

Use embed options when you want to:

  • Show the booking flow inside your site or app
  • Match the scheduler’s look to your brand
  • Let visitors book without leaving your page
  • Pre-fill invitee details or use tracking codes
  • Track bookings with event listeners (like 0)

Embed types:

  • Inline embed: The scheduler shows on your page
  • Popup widget: A floating button opens the scheduler
  • Popup text: A text link opens the scheduler

See the Developer Guide to Calendly embeds to learn more. #### Example: Use API and Embed

You can combine the API and embed to customize scheduling:

  1. Use the API to get a scheduling link.
  2. Use JavaScript to place that link in your embed.
  3. Call 0 to load the scheduler.

This lets you update links without hardcoding them. #### Want to build more?

Our team is always working to add more features to the API.

Check for updates on the:

  • Calendly Developer Portal
  • Calendly Release Notes

How to add Calendly to a Shopify site

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Embed Calendly on your Shopify site so visitors can book time with you without leaving your store. Shopify supports inline embeds, popup text, and popup widgets.

This guide shows how to add each embed type and resolve common display issues. #### Before you begin

First, generate your Calendly embed code. You can embed:

  • A specific event type, or
  • Your booking page #### Supported embed types in Shopify

Shopify supports three Calendly embed options:

  • Inline embed – Displays your calendar directly on a page
  • Popup text – A text link that opens your calendar in a popup
  • Popup widget – A floating button that opens your calendar on any page #### Add an inline or popup text embed

To embed Calendly on a specific Shopify page:

  1. In Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Customize
  2. In the left menu, select Add section
  3. Choose Custom Liquid
  4. On the right, paste your Calendly embed code in the text box
  5. Select Save

This works for both inline and popup text embed codes. #### Display a popup widget across your entire site

To show a floating Calendly button on every page:

  1. In Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes
  2. Find your theme and select the … button
  3. Select Edit code
  4. In the left menu, choose theme.liquid
  5. Find the 0 tag
  6. Add a line break right after it
  7. Paste your Calendly popup widget code
  8. Select Save

To check if it’s working, select Preview store. #### Troubleshoot Shopify display issues

If your Calendly embed doesn’t appear on your Shopify site, follow these steps to troubleshoot.

Step 1 – Confirm your embed code and theme settings

  1. In Calendly, copy the Inline Embed code for your Event Type.
  2. In Shopify, go to Online Store > Themes.
  3. Find your active theme and select Actions > Edit Code.
  4. Choose one of the following options:
  • Add a new custom HTML block, or
  • Create a new Snippet file.
  1. If using a snippet, name it something easy to reference later (like 0).
  2. Paste the Calendly embed code into the snippet or HTML block and select Save.

Step 2 – Reference the embed in your page template

  1. Open the Shopify page template where you want to display your Calendly embed.
  2. Add the following code at the bottom of the file: 0 (Replace 0 with the name you used if it’s different.)
  3. Save your changes.

Some Shopify themes hide empty HTML elements, which can prevent the popup from closing.

Fix: Add this HTML after your embed code:

html

 .calendly-overlay .calendly-popup-close, .calendly-overlay .calendly-close-overlay {  display: block !important; }

If your calendar looks cut off:

  1. Increase the height in your embed code:

    html

    <div class="calendly-inline-widget"data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_EVENT"style="min-width:320px;height:1000px;"></div>

  2. If that doesn’t fix it, add this CSS to your Shopify theme:

  • Go to Online Store > Edit code > Assets > theme.scss.liquid

  • Add the following at the bottom:

    css

    iframe {height: 100vh !important;}

This forces the iframe to use the full height of the screen.

How to add Calendly to a Squarespace site

  6. Select Apply to save your changes.

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Let visitors schedule time with you without leaving your website. Follow these steps to embed Calendly on your Squarespace page. #### Before you begin

  • A Squarespace Business Plan is required.

This script helps Calendly load correctly on your site. #### Additional tips

Elementor works with both WordPress.org and WordPress.com. It gives you more control over page design.

  1. Open your page in the Elementor editor.
  2. Add a Shortcode widget to the canvas.

For a visual walkthrough, watch the Elementor video guide: Add Calendly with Elementor. #### Troubleshooting scrolling issue on Elementor

We have seen that Elementor will automatically overflow-y:auto add as an inline style. The addition of this style can create an extra scrolling element.

To correct this, make sure that the overflow or overflow-y is set to hidden. For example:

html

.calendly-inline-widget { overflow-y: hidden !important; }
