How to control your embed layout and sizing

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly adjusts the calendar layout to fit the size of its container. You can change the layout and size to better fit your website or app. #### Choose a layout based on width

Calendly’s inline embed has three layout styles. The style depends on the width of the container (called the “parent container”). #### Large window layout

Parent element width >= 1100px

[Image: 30970862026775] #### Example

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget"data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK"style="width:1100px;height:700px;"></div>

Medium window layout

Parent element width < 1100px and >= 650px

[Image: 30970902130583] #### Example

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget"data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK"style="width:700px;height:700px;"></div>

Small window layout

Parent element width < 650px

[Image: 30970862029207] #### Example

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget"data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK"style="width:600px;height:700px;"></div>

Remove scroll bars

If you see a scroll bar inside the embed:

  • Increase the height in the embed code style=“min-width:320px;height:750px;”
  • Use data-resize=“true” to enable auto-resize

Example:

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget" data-url="https://calendly.com/your-link" style="min-width:320px; height:750px;" data-resize="true"></div><script type="text/javascript" src="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js" async></script>

Minimum width for mobile

Calendly needs at least 320px of width to show correctly on mobile.

If the embed looks off-center or cut off:

  • Check for extra padding or margins on mobile.
  • Make sure the container is at least 320px wide. #### Test your embed layout

After adding the embed:

  • Check layout on both desktop and mobile
  • Use your browser’s inspect tool to preview different sizes
  • Adjust the container’s size or margins as needed

How to create a custom button to open Calendly

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Add a custom button that opens Calendly in a popup using HTML and JavaScript—no iframe needed. Full setup and styling guide included. #### Before you begin

To create a button that opens Calendly in a popup, you’ll need to:

  • Include Calendly’s embed script and CSS on your page
  • Add a button or other clickable element to your HTML
  • Use a JavaScript 0 function to launch the scheduler #### Step 1 – Add Calendly’s CSS and JavaScript

Add the following code to your site’s HTML, ideally just before the closing 0 tag or at the top of the body:

javascript

<!-- Calendly embed script and styles --><link href="https://calendly.com/assets/external/widget.css" rel="stylesheet">

These resources are required for the popup to work. #### Step 2 – Add your button

Create a button or link in your HTML. In the 0 attribute, call the Calendly popup function and include your scheduling link.

Example:

html

<button onclick="Calendly.initPopupWidget({ url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_SCHEDULING_LINK' }); return false;">  Schedule a time to meet</button>

Replace 0 with the full URL to your booking page or event type. You can use any clickable element — links, icons, or divs — as long as it includes the same 0 function. #### Optional – Customize the popup behavior

The popup appears in the center of the screen with an overlay. You can also pass parameters such as pre-filled invitee data or UTM tags if you’re using the advanced embed. For most cases, the example above is enough. #### Style your button

You can style your button with CSS. Here’s an example:

css

  .calendly-button {    background-color: #0069ff;    color: white;    border: none;    padding: 12px 24px;    font-size: 16px;    border-radius: 6px;    cursor: pointer;  }  .calendly-button:hover {    background-color: #0052cc;  }<button class="calendly-button" onclick="Calendly.initPopupWidget({ url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_SCHEDULING_LINK' }); return false;">  Book your appointment</button>

Update the colors, padding, fonts, and other styles to match your site. #### Troubleshooting tips

  • Make sure both the Calendly script and CSS file are included
  • Ensure your button uses 0 to prevent the page from refreshing
  • If the popup doesn’t appear, check for errors in the browser console
  • Avoid multiple 0 calls on the same page unless needed

How to customize your embed

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Customize your Calendly embed to match your site—hide event info, remove the cookie banner, change colors, and adjust widget placement. #### Hide event details

You can hide personal or event information so it doesn’t show twice on your site.

What’s hidden:

  • Your photo
  • Your name
  • Event duration
  • Event location
  • Event description

To hide event details when creating your embed:

  1. Before copying your embed code, select Hide Event Details
  • Works for both inline and pop-up embeds
  1. Select Copy Code.
  2. Paste the code into your website’s HTML.

If you already embedded Calendly: Add these query parameters to your Calendly link:

  • Link type: Event type; What to add: ?hide_event_type_details=1
  • Link type: Landing or team page; What to add: ?hide_landing_page_details=1

Note: If you use both, the event type description may still show.

Example:

0 #### Hide the cookie banner

Calendly shows a cookie banner by default. If you hide it, make sure your site manages cookie laws like GDPR or CCPA.

To hide the cookie banner:

  • Select Hide Cookie Banner before copying your embed code

If you already embedded Calendly:

  • Add 0 to your Calendly link

Example embed code:

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget"data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_EVENT?hide_event_type_details=1&hide_gdpr_banner=1"style="min-width:320px;height:630px;"></div><script src="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js"></script>

Change colors and button text

If you’re on a paid plan, you can update your embed’s look and feel by changing the background color, text color, button color, or button label (only available for Pop-Up embed). You can do this when copying your code or by editing your existing embed code.

Available options:

  • 0 — Sets the background behind the embed
  • 0 — Changes the color of the text
  • 0 — Updates the button and link color
  • 0 — Replaces the default “Schedule” button label

Tip

The “Schedule” button text automatically switches to black or white based on your selected button color. This improves color contrast for accessibility and readability.

Example:

html

<!-- Calendly badge widget begin --><link href="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.css" rel="stylesheet">window.onload = function() {Calendly.initBadgeWidget({url: 'https://calendly.com/<YOUR LINK>',text: 'Your Button Text Here',color: '#0069ff',textColor: '#ffffff'});}<!-- Calendly badge widget end -->

Need help picking colors? Try a contrast checker to make sure your choices are accessible. #### Change the position of the widget

When using our pop-up widget embed code, the default placement of the widget will be the bottom of the webpage aligned to the right corner. To change the alignment to either the left or center of your page, add one of the CSS codes below. Then, adjust the left and right inputs until you arrive at your desired spacing.

Left:

html

<!-- left align the badge widget --> .calendly-badge-widget { right: auto !important; left: 20px !important; }  <!-- end left align the badge widget -->

Center:

html

<!-- center align the badge widget-->.calendly-badge-widget { left: 50% !important; margin-left: -100px!important; }<!--end center align the badge widget-->

Preview and adjust your embed

  • Test both mobile and desktop layouts
  • Use your browser’s Inspect tool (right select > Inspect) to try changes
  • Adjust width and height until the embed fits your site

How to embed Calendly in a mobile app

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Add Calendly to your mobile app using our embed options. This lets users schedule with you directly—without leaving your app. #### Display Calendly using a WebView

Calendly embeds are designed to run in a browser. To use them in a mobile app, most developers load the embed code into a WebView.

A WebView is a browser window that opens inside your app. It shows Calendly’s scheduling page like a regular webpage, but within your app’s layout. #### Supported embed types

You can use any standard or advanced Calendly embed in a WebView:

  • Inline embed
  • Popup widget
  • Popup text

Calendly embeds use HTML and JavaScript. If your mobile framework supports WebView and those technologies, it will work. #### Select the right embed for your app

Calendly offers two levels of embed control:

  • Option: Standard; Best for: Simple setups; quick and easy
  • Option: Advanced; Best for: Custom styling, event tracking, pre-fill

Load Calendly in a WebView

Use your mobile framework’s WebView component to load Calendly. Here’s a basic example using an iframe:

html

<iframe src="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK"style="width: 100%; min-width: 320px; height: 700px;" frameborder="0"></iframe>

Or use the JavaScript API for more control:

html

Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK',parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed')});

Troubleshoot your embed

  • Test on real devices—behavior can differ from emulators
  • Start with a standard embed to check compatibility
  • Confirm JavaScript is enabled in your WebView for advanced features
  • For iOS, watch for content overflow and layout scaling in Safari-based WebViews
  • Use developer options to pre-fill forms or track booking events #### Unlock advanced features

With Calendly’s advanced embed options, you can:

  • Pre-fill the booking form with user data from your app
  • Track scheduling events using window.postMessage
  • Dynamically resize the embed based on user actions
  • Add campaign tracking with UTM parameters

To learn more, see Advanced Calendly embed for developers.

How to embed Calendly in a React app

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

If you’re building a React app, you can embed Calendly to let users book time without leaving your site. This guide covers your options and offers tips for smooth implementation. #### Use the react-calendly package

The easiest way to embed Calendly in React is to use the third-party react-calendly package. While not maintained by Calendly, many developers use it in production. #### To get started:

Install the package using npm or yarn:

bash

npm install react-calendly# oryarn add react-calendly

Then, import and use the component in your React code:

jsx

import { InlineWidget } from "react-calendly";function BookingPage() {return (<InlineWidget url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK" />);}

This adds an inline embed to your page. #### Other available components

The react-calendly package also supports:

  • PopupText – renders a text link that opens a popup
  • PopupButton – renders a button that opens the scheduler
  • PopupWidget – adds a floating widget to your app

Visit the react-calendly package for full examples and customization options. #### Customize your embed

You can pass props to tailor the widget. For example, you can:

  • Pre-fill the booking form with invitee details
  • Track UTM parameters
  • Control the height and style

Example with props:

jsx

<InlineWidgeturl="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK"styles={{ height: '700px' }}utm={{ utmSource: 'facebook', utmCampaign: 'spring_sale' }}prefill={{name: 'Jane Doe',email: 'jane@example.com'}}/>

Handling layout issues

Calendly embeds use iframes. Some React layouts—especially mobile-first designs—can cause sizing or scrolling issues.

If you notice scroll problems (common on iOS):

  • Ensure the container has at least 700px height
  • Avoid overflow: auto or fixed-height containers
  • Test layout using browser dev tools #### Use the standard embed script (no package)

If you prefer not to use react-calendly, you can embed Calendly with the standard JavaScript and a useEffecthook.

Example:

jsx

import { useEffect } from "react";function BookingPage() {useEffect(() => {const script = document.createElement("script");script.src = "https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js";script.async = true;document.body.appendChild(script);window.Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: "https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK",parentElement: document.getElementById("calendly-embed"),});}, []);return ;}

This gives you full control, similar to embedding Calendly in regular HTML.

How to embed Calendly in an Angular app

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

You can embed Calendly in any app that supports HTML and JavaScript—including Angular. This guide shows how to add Calendly to your Angular app using our embed code. #### Choose your embed method

Calendly uses JavaScript and an iframe to show scheduling options. Angular supports both. You can choose between two methods:

  • Inline embed: Simple HTML with the Calendly script
  • Advanced embed: Uses Calendly.initInlineWidget() for more control

You can place either one inside a component template. #### Embed using standard inline method

Use Calendly’s standard embed code in your component’s HTML template:

html

<!-- Inside your Angular component's template -->

Then add the Calendly script globally in your index.html file or angular.json:

html

<script src="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js" type="text/javascript"></script>

This script loads the Calendly widget when your component appears. #### Embed using advanced JavaScript method

Need more control? Use the advanced method to resize, pre-fill data, or track events.

Add this code to your component file (e.g., booking.component.ts):

ts

import { Component, AfterViewInit } from '@angular/core';declare const Calendly: any;@Component({selector: 'app-booking',template: 0,})export class BookingComponent implements AfterViewInit {ngAfterViewInit(): void {Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK',parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed'),});}}

Make sure the Calendly script is in your index.html:

html

<script src="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js" type="text/javascript"></script>

Best practices

  • Set a height of at least 700px to avoid scroll bars.
  • Only call Calendly.initInlineWidget() once per render.
  • Test for issues when using Angular routing.
  • Don’t reload the script between route changes. #### Need an example?

See a working example with an answer provided by a Calendly engineer.

How to embed Calendly in Joomla

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

You can embed Calendly in your Joomla site so visitors can schedule time with you right from your website. This guide shows you how to add the embed code using Joomla’s custom HTML options. #### Before you begin

  • Make sure you can add custom HTML to your Joomla site.

  • Next, copy your embed code from Calendly. #### Supported embed types

  • Embed type: Inline embed; What it does: Shows the calendar directly on the page

  • Embed type: Popup widget; What it does: Adds a floating button that opens the calendar

  • Embed type: Popup text; What it does: Creates a link that opens the calendar

Learn more about Calendly embed options. #### Add Calendly to Joomla

You can add Calendly using a Custom HTML module or directly in an article. Choose the option that works best for your site. #### Option 1 – Use a Custom HTML module

  1. In your Joomla admin panel, go to Extensions > Modules.
  2. Select New, then choose Custom.
  3. In the editor:
  • Set Show Title and Position as needed.
  • Select the Code or Tools button (may look like <>) to switch to HTML view.
  • Paste your embed code.

  1. Save and publish the module.

  2. Visit your site to make sure the embed displays correctly. #### Option 2 – Add Calendly to an article

  3. Go to Content > Articles.

  4. Edit the article where you want to add Calendly.

  5. Select the Code view button (<>) in the editor.

  6. Paste your embed code.

  7. Save and preview the article.

Tip: If Joomla removes 0 tags, go to Global Configuration > Text Filters to change your editor settings. #### Example embed code

Here’s an example of an inline embed:

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget"data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK"style="min-width:320px;height:700px;"></div><script src="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js" type="text/javascript"></script>

To embed a popup widget or popup text, copy the code directly from your Calendly account. #### Troubleshooting

  • If nothing shows up, check if your editor is removing scripts.
  • Test your embed on both desktop and mobile.
  • If you’re using a dynamic template or extension, make sure the Calendly script loads properly.

How to embed Calendly with an iframe

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly offers several embed options that use JavaScript to control layout and behavior. But if your platform doesn’t support JavaScript—or only allows iframe content—you can still embed Calendly using a basic iframe setup.

This guide explains when to use the iframe option, how to set it up, and what limitations to expect. #### When to use an iframe

Choose the iframe embed if:

  • Your website builder doesn’t support JavaScript
  • You’re embedding Calendly in a platform that blocks scripts (like some CMS tools or email previews)
  • You only need a simple booking experience without tracking or customization

Tip: For more features like layout control, invitee pre-fills, and event tracking, use Calendly’s JavaScript embed options instead. #### Set up an iframe embed

You can use any Calendly scheduling link inside an iframe. Here’s the basic format:

html

<iframe src="https://calendly.com/YOUR_SCHEDULING_LINK" style="width: 100%; min-width: 320px; height: 700px;" frameborder="0"></iframe>

Replace YOUR_SCHEDULING_LINK with your actual link.

Example:

html

<iframe src="https://calendly.com/jane-doe/30min" style="width: 100%; min-width: 320px; height: 700px;" frameborder="0"></iframe>

Layout tips

  • Set min-width: 320px to support mobile devices
  • Use at least height: 700px to avoid scrollbars
  • Adjust the width or max-width to match your layout #### What iframe-only embeds can’t do

Without JavaScript, the embed is more limited. You won’t be able to:

  • Pre-fill the invitee’s name or email
  • Track events like bookings
  • Resize the widget automatically
  • Hide profile pictures or the cookie banner

Some features require JavaScript support to work correctly. #### Need more control?

If your platform allows it, switch to Calendly’s advanced embed options. These let you:

  • Pre-fill invitee details
  • Automatically adjust widget height
  • Track events and UTM parameters
  • Customize colors, styles, and labels

Learn more about advanced Calendly embeds.

How to pre-fill invitee information in an embed

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

If your site already collects information like name or email, you can pass that data into your Calendly embed. This saves users time and creates a smoother booking experience by filling in the form automatically.

This guide shows how to use Calendly’s advanced embed to pre-fill invitee details. #### Details you can pre-fill

Calendly supports pre-filling these fields:

  • Full name, or first and last name (if collected separately)
  • Email address
  • Answers to up to 10 invitee questions
  • Custom fields (labeled a1–a10) used in your event questions #### Add prefill data to an advanced embed

To pre-fill invitee info, use the advanced JavaScript embed (0) and include the 1 field.

Example:

javascript

  Calendly.initInlineWidget({    url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_USERNAME',    parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed-element'),    prefill: {      name: 'John Doe',      email: 'john@example.com',      customAnswers: {        a1: 'Yes',        a2: 'At the office'      }    }  });

Replace 0 with your actual Calendly link. Update the fields with your invitee’s information. #### Pre-fill from a custom form or URL

If your site collects data from a form or URL, use JavaScript to grab that data and pass it into the embed.

Example: Get values from the URL

javascript

function getUrlVars() {  const vars = {};  window.location.href.replace(/[?&]+([^=&]+)=([^&]*)/gi, function(m,k,v) {    vars[k] = decodeURIComponent(v);  });  return vars;}const nameValue = getUrlVars()["name"];const emailValue = getUrlVars()["email"];Calendly.initInlineWidget({  url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_USERNAME',  parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed-element'),  prefill: {    name: nameValue,    email: emailValue  }});

Also include this script:

javascript

<script src="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js"></script>

Use first and last name separately

If your event collects first and last name as separate fields, use:

javascript

prefill: {  firstName: "Jane",  lastName: "Smith",  email: "jane@example.com"}

Pre-fill answers to custom questions

If your event includes invitee questions, they’ll be labeled 0 through 1. Use the 2 object to pass answers.

Example:

javascript

customAnswers: {  a1: "Yes",  a2: "Zoom",  a3: "No dietary restrictions"}

The order of your questions in Calendly determines which field maps to each label.

How to source track your Calendly embed with UTM parameters

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Use UTM parameters to track where your traffic comes from before someone books with you. This helps you measure the success of your ads, emails, or campaigns using tools like Google Analytics. #### What are UTM parameters?

UTM parameters are tags you add to a link. They tell you where your traffic comes from. Calendly supports these values:

  • utm_source — where the traffic comes from (e.g., 0, 1)
  • utm_medium — the type of channel (e.g., 0, 1)
  • utm_campaign — the name of your campaign (e.g., 0)
  • utm_content — extra details like 0 or 1
  • utm_term — for paid search keywords

Note: Each UTM value must be fewer than 255 characters. Longer values may not be tracked. #### Option 1 – Add UTM parameters to the embed URL

If you use a direct embed link, you can add UTM parameters to the URL.

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget" data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK/30min?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=ad&utm_campaign=spring_sale" style="min-width:320px;height:630px;"></div>

This method works for all embed types: inline, popup text, or popup widget. #### Option 2 – Pass UTM parameters using JavaScript (advanced)

If you use the advanced JavaScript embed, pass UTM values during setup.

javascript

Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK/30min',parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed'),utm: {utmCampaign: "spring_sale",utmSource: "facebook",utmMedium: "ad",utmContent: "shoes",utmTerm: "spring"}});

Option 3 – Pass UTM values from the page URL

You can reuse the same embed across multiple campaigns by pulling UTM values directly from the page URL.

javascript

function getUrlVars() {const vars = {};window.location.href.replace(/[?&]+([^=&]+)=([^&]*)/gi, function(m,k,v) {vars[k] = decodeURIComponent(v);});return vars;}const utms = getUrlVars();Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK/30min',parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed'),utm: {utmSource: utms["utm_source"],utmMedium: utms["utm_medium"],utmCampaign: utms["utm_campaign"],utmContent: utms["utm_content"],utmTerm: utms["utm_term"]}});

Option 4 – Hardcode UTM values for different sources

If you’re tracking multiple sources, create separate embed codes for each.

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget" data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK/30min?utm_source=facebook" style="min-width:320px;height:630px;"></div>

Create different embeds for traffic sources like Google Ads, email newsletters, or LinkedIn.

How to track embed activity in Google Analytics

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

You can track what visitors do in your Calendly embed using Google Analytics. This helps you understand how people find and interact with your booking page. #### Before you begin

What you’ll need:

  • A Google Analytics account (GA4 or UA)
  • Access to your website’s HTML or tag manager
  • A Calendly account with the embed code ready #### Step 1 – Set up Google Analytics

Make sure Google Analytics is installed and working on your site. You can add it using Google Tag Manager, a plugin, or by placing the code directly into your site.

  • Learn how to set up Google Analytics. #### Step 2 – Connect Calendly to Google Analytics

Follow these steps to connect Calendly to Google Analytics. #### Step 3 – Add your Calendly embed to your site

Paste your embed code into your website where you want the scheduling page to appear. This is where the tracking happens.

Example:

html

<div class="calendly-inline-widget"data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK"style="min-width:320px;height:700px;"></div><script src="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js"></script><strong data-start="1492" data-end="1504"></strong>

Step 4 – Track traffic sources with UTM parameters

UTM parameters are tags you add to your Calendly link. They help you track where visitors come from, such as ads, email campaigns, or social media.

Example with UTM tags:

html

data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=ad&utm_campaign=spring_sale"

Common UTM values:

  • utm_source: Where the traffic comes from (e.g., facebook, newsletter)
  • utm_medium: The channel type (e.g., ad, email, social)
  • utm_campaign: The campaign name (e.g., spring_sale)

Note: Each UTM value can be up to 255 characters long. #### Step 5 – View Calendly events in Google Analytics

Calendly automatically tracks key visitor actions inside the embed.

Tracked events include:

  • calendly.profile_page_viewed
  • calendly.event_type_viewed
  • calendly.date_and_time_selected
  • calendly.event_scheduled

To view them:

  1. Go to your Google Analytics dashboard

  2. Navigate to the Events section #### Step 6 – Test your setup

  3. Book a test event using the embedded Calendly link

  4. Open Google Analytics

  5. Go to Real-time view

  6. Look for event or page activity

Real-time data shows immediately, but full results may take 24–48 hours. #### Privacy notice for international visitors

Visitors from regions with strict privacy laws (like GDPR or CCPA) will see a cookie banner in the embed. If they reject cookies, some activity might not be tracked. #### Optional: Use JavaScript to control UTM values

If you’re using Calendly’s advanced JavaScript embed, you can pass UTM values directly in the script:

javascript

Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK',parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed'),utm: {utmCampaign: "spring_sale",utmSource: "facebook",utmMedium: "ad"}});

Or pull UTM values from the page URL automatically:

javascript

"function" geturlvars=""const vars = {};window.location.href.replace(/[?&]+([^=&]+)=([^&]*)/gi, function(m,k,v) {vars[k] = decodeURIComponent(v);});return vars;}const utms = getUrlVars();Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: 'https://calendly.com/YOUR_LINK',parentElement: document.getElementById('calendly-embed'),utm: {utmSource: utms["utm_source"],utmMedium: utms["utm_medium"],utmCampaign: utms["utm_campaign"]}});

Troubleshooting Calendly embeds

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

If your Calendly embed isn’t working as expected, this guide can help. Below are common issues and how to fix them. #### Fix scrolling and image loading issues

If your page won’t scroll or images don’t load, Calendly’s embed styles may be conflicting with your website’s layout.

Try this CSS fix:

css

body {overflow: unset !important;}

Using Squarespace? Also add:

css

.site-wrapper {height: auto;}

These changes allow your page to scroll normally and prevent layout conflicts, especially if your site template overrides Calendly’s height settings. #### Prevent ad blockers from hiding embeds

Browser extensions may block Calendly embeds. To help visitors:

  • Display a message like: “Please turn off your ad blocker to view this calendar.”
  • Add a fallback button that opens the scheduling page in a new tab. #### Fix dropdown menus on mobile

Dropdowns in embeds can open off-screen on mobile devices. Try these fixes:

  • Use a shorter embed height
  • Replace dropdowns with radio buttons (for short lists)
  • Switch to a pop-up embed, which fits better on mobile #### Adjust layout based on container width

Calendly’s layout responds to its container’s width.

  • To show side-by-side layout: Set width to 1000px or more
  • To switch to stacked layout: Reduce width below 650px

Learn how to control embed layout and sizing #### Center your embed on mobile

If your embed appears off-center on mobile:

  • Make sure the container is at least 320px wide
  • Remove extra padding or margins around the embed #### Fix embeds appearing at the bottom of the page

If you use HubSpot, Marketo, or similar tools and your embed appears in the wrong place, check that this stylesheet is included:

html

<link href="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.css" rel="stylesheet">

Without it, styles may break and push the embed to the bottom. #### Embed not working after you change your Calendly link

Seeing a “calendly.com refused to connect” error? Your embed may use an old or incorrect link. Fix it by:

  • Generating a new embed code in Calendly
  • Replacing the old code on your site

Or inspect the link using ⌥⌘I (Mac) or right-click > Inspect, then update it manually. #### Remove extra scroll bars

Check out this guide: Remove the embed scroll.

Tip: Use “Inspect” in your browser to test different embed heights. #### Website builder specific issues

If you’re having any issues with specific website builders, please see our linked resources.

  • Squarespace - Embed doesn’t appear in editor
  • Shopify - Popup close button doesn’t appear
  • Wordpress - Embed not working in Elementor

Event types

Event type editor overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

The event type editor is your tool for creating and updating Event Types. Use it to customize your meeting details, set availability, and manage automated notifications.

For example, you can:

  • Create an Event Type
  • Update settings and availability for any existing Event Type
  • Manage automated notifications for each Event Type #### Before you begin

Only owners, admins, and group admins can edit Event Types for other users. Others can edit if they’ve been given event type permissions. Learn more in the Event type permissions overview.

To create an Event Type, you’ll first need to set a few basics:

  • Event name
  • Duration
  • Location
  • Availability
  • Host(s)

After that, you can access more settings by selecting More options at the bottom of the editor. #### Best practices

  • To make an event secret or change the language, select the [Image: 33336204766999] three dots on an event type card from the Scheduling page.
  • To preview your booking page, open the Event Type editor and select Preview at the bottom. #### Setting up event types

Ready to set up an event type? These Help Center articles will walk you through the steps.

  • How to customize your event types - How to set up an event type, - Event types overview - Advanced invitee features

Event types overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Event types in Calendly are meeting templates you can reuse. They help you schedule different kinds of meetings — like product demos, customer calls, or office hours — with specific settings and details.

There are four types of event types:

  • One-on-one: Meet individually with one invitee.
  • Group: Host events with multiple invitees at once.
  • Collective: Schedule a meeting where several team members meet with one invitee.
  • Round robin: Rotate meetings among team members, one-on-one with invitees. #### One-on-one

A One-on-one event type is a meeting between one host and one invitee.

Common uses include:

  • Coffee chats or syncs with a client, colleague, or friend
  • Phone interviews with a candidate
  • Office hours with a student #### Group

On the Standard plan and above, a Group event type allows one host to meet with several invitees. You choose how many people can join each time slot. The slot stays open until all spots are filled.

Common uses include:

  • Webinars
  • Museum or campus tours
  • Group fitness classes
  • University admissions sessions

Learn more: Multi-person scheduling options for teams #### Collective

On the Standard plan and above, a Collective event type lets multiple hosts meet with one invitee. Calendly finds times when all hosts are available and shows those options to the invitee.

Common uses include:

  • Panel interviews
  • Product discovery calls
  • Client calls with both an account executive and a sales development rep
  • Support calls with a support agent and an engineer

If you’re on the Teams or Enterprise plan, you can schedule with multiple host groups.

Learn more: Multi-person scheduling options for teams #### Round Robin

On the Teams and Enterprise plans, a Round Robin event type rotates one-on-one meetings across team members based on their availability or assignment rules.

Common uses include:

  • Sales calls handled by any available rep
  • Onboarding sessions rotated across the client services team
  • Support calls assigned to the next available agent
  • Personal training sessions with rotating trainers

You can also schedule with multiple host groups on these plans.

Learn more: Multi-person scheduling options for teams

Group event type overview

Quick answer

Event types are reusable meeting templates that control how people book time with you. Each event type defines details like duration, location, and availability.

Calendly offers four types:

  1. One-on-one: One host, one invitee
  2. Group: One host, multiple invitees
  3. Collective: Multiple hosts meet one invitee when all are available
  4. Round robin: One-on-one meetings rotate across teammates

Available to all users on all paid plans.View plans

A group event type lets one host meet with many invitees at the same time. This is great for events like:

  • Webinars
  • Training sessions
  • Museum tours #### Set the number of invitees per time slot

You can choose how many people can book the same time slot. For example, if you set the limit to 50, up to 50 invitees can book your 1 p.m. webinar.

Want to show how many spots are left? Turn on Display remaining spots to let invitees see the count in real time.

[Image: 28417516373527] #### To set the max invitees:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your group event type.
  2. Open the [Image: 33352436903959] three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. Expand the Invitee limit section.
  4. Enter the number of invitees (minimum 2, maximum 9,999).
  5. (Optional) Check the box to Display remaining spots.
  6. Select Save changes.

Changes to the Invitee limit setting only apply to future bookings. If your group event is already scheduled, increasing the limit will not open more spots for that meeting.

To change the number of invitees for an existing meeting, follow the steps below. #### Update the invitee limit for a scheduled meeting

  1. Go to your Meetings page.
  2. Select the meeting you want to update.
  3. Under Invitees, click Edit invitee limit.
  4. Enter the new limit in the pop-up window.
  5. Select Apply to save. #### How email confirmations work

Group events use email confirmations, not calendar invites.

  • Invitees get their own .ics file.
  • This file won’t update for others if someone changes the event.

Most calendars add the event automatically. If not, invitees can download the file from their confirmation email or page.

Learn more about invitee notifications. #### Use Workflows with group events

You can use Workflows to send reminders or follow-ups for group events. The Event is canceled trigger isn’t currently supported for group events.

Updates to Workflows will only apply to future meetings. Meetings made before the changes will still use the old settings from when they were created. #### Manage event hosts and permissions

If you’re on the Standard plan or higher, you can choose who can view, edit, or share the event.

Learn how to set event permissions. #### Change the event language, location, or duration

Once someone books a group event, you can’t change its language, location, or duration. These settings are locked with a gray box.

To make changes:

  1. Duplicate the event and update the language or duration.
  2. Cancel the original meeting.
  3. Reschedule it using the new event type.

To cancel and reschedule:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. (Optional) Open the My Calendly dropdown to switch to another user or team page.
  3. Find the event type and select the [Image: 33352436903959] three dots on the event card.
  4. Choose Duplicate, then update the event.
  5. Go to your Meetings page and cancel the original event.
  6. Return to the new event type and select [Image: 33352444305687] Book meeting.
  7. Add each invitee’s info to reschedule the meeting.

How to change your event type language

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Use Calendly’s language options to localize the scheduling experience for people meeting with you. Your booking page and all event notifications can be automatically translated to:

  • French
  • Spanish
  • German
  • Dutch
  • Portuguese (Brazil)
  • Italian
  • Ukrainian

Note

Calendly booking pages can be read by in-browser translation software such as Google Translate. This opens up the language options beyond the seven above. However, as we have not natively created these translations, we cannot guarantee their accuracy. #### Change invitee language

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. (Optional) Open the My Calendly dropdown to switch to another user or team page.
  3. Find the event type and select the [Image: 33338963568663] three dots on the event card.
  4. Select Change invitee language.
  5. Choose a language.
  6. Select Yes to confirm.

Once a new language has been selected, Calendly will localize the invitee’s view and notifications moving forward.

Note

Any customizable text, such as the event type name, description or custom questions will not be translated, and must be translated manually.

How to create a One-off meeting

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Use a One-off Meeting to host a one-time, high-priority meeting that doesn’t fit your regular event types. You can choose a custom duration, location, and hosts.

For example, you can:

  • Set up a one-time meeting with one or more hosts

  • Offer times outside your usual availability

  • Prioritize a meeting over existing events #### Before you begin

  • If you’re using video conferencing for the meeting location, make sure to connect your account through the Integrations & apps page.

  • You can only select time slots that are no more than 3 months apart.

  • Buffers and meetings appear as one block. For example, if your event has a 30-minute buffer and a 30-minute duration, the time slot will appear as a 1-hour block. #### Create a One-off meeting

Choose times to offer

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. Select + Create, then choose More ways to meet > One-off Meeting.
  3. Set your time zone, meeting duration, and any additional hosts.
  • Invitees will see the times in their own time zone.
  1. Pick time slots from the calendar.
  • You can select time slots over non-Calendly meetings.
  • You can also choose slots outside your available hours.
  • To select all free times for a day, go to that day and select + Add times at the top.
  1. After choosing time slots, select Next.

Set up meeting details

  1. Enter the meeting name and location.
  2. Add an optional description or instructions.
  3. Adjust any of the Optional settings.
  4. Select Share meeting link. #### Share your One-off meeting link

Calendly generates a unique link for your meeting. You can edit the link ending or preview the booking page using View live page.

When you’re ready, select Copy Link and share it. You can also copy and paste times in an email with the Add times to email feature. #### Where to find your One-off meeting

After sharing your link, you’ll find the meeting under Scheduling > Single-use links. Once your invitee books it, the meeting can be viewed from the Meetings page. #### Reserve times

Turn on Reserve Times to temporarily hold the time slots you’ve offered. This blocks time on your calendar (and your co-hosts’ calendars) with placeholder events.

Once an invitee books, those placeholders clear automatically, and the meeting appears on your Meetings page. It may take a few minutes for reserved times to fully clear.

To clear reserved times manually:

  1. Go to Scheduling > Single-use links.
  2. Find the one-off meeting and select the [Image: 33339952372887] three dots.
  3. Select Clear reserved times.
  4. Select Clear reservations to confirm. #### Frequently asked questions

No. It expires after it’s booked and can’t be used again.

Not yet. Workflows only apply to regular event types.

Yes. Reserved slots won’t appear as open on your regular booking pages. Use the Troubleshoot tool to confirm.

No. When you clear reserved times, all placeholder events are removed at once.

No. One-off meetings can’t be rescheduled.

If you need to move the meeting to a different date or time, cancel the existing One-off Meeting and create a new one.

If you need the flexibility to reschedule a meeting after booking, consider using a regular event type instead.

How to create a single-use link

Available to all users on all plans.View plans #### Overview

Single-use links let you share one-time meeting availability based on an existing event type. The link expires once the meeting is booked, preventing invitees from sharing it or scheduling multiple meetings. #### What you can customize

With single-use links, you can add a contact and customize meeting details before sharing. Here’s what you can customize:

  • For one-on-one event types: Personalize the meeting name, contact information, duration, location, and availability.
  • For group, round robin, and collective event types: Personalize contact information.

Create a single-use link

  1. Go to Scheduling.
  2. Find the event type you want to share and hover over it to see more options.
  3. Select [Image: 33352398968087] Create single-use link.
  4. (Optional) Add a contact and customize meeting details.
  5. Select Save and copy link to copy it to your clipboard and send it in a message.

Users on paid plans will also see a Share button to send the link by email from Calendly using your connected Gmail or Outlook account. You can customize the message and add a reminder if your invitee hasn’t scheduled in 1, 3, or 7 days.

Single-use links are created one at a time and expire after one booking. If you need multiple links, create each link separately.

Managing single-use links

  • On the Scheduling page, go to the Single-use links tab to view, share, duplicate, edit, or delete your links.
  • Once a meeting is scheduled through a single-use link, it will appear on your Meetings page.

How to customize your event types

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

You can update your event type settings in Calendly to control how and when people can schedule time with you. #### Before you begin

  • Using managed event types? These include special settings and limits. Learn how to edit admin-managed event types.
  • Want to switch event types? You can’t change one type into another (for example, from a one-on-one to a group event). Instead, create a new event type.
  • Using the mobile app? See these mobile-specific instructions for editing your event on a phone or tablet. #### Edit your event type
  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. (Optional) Open the My Calendly dropdown to switch to another user or team.
  3. Select the event type you want to edit to open the editor. #### Customize your event settings

Each event type includes settings that affect how invitees schedule with you. #### Primary settings

  • Setting: Event name; What it controls: What invitees see as the title.
  • Setting: Event color; What it controls: The color used to identify the event type.
  • Setting: Duration; What it controls: How long the meeting lasts.
  • Setting: Location; What it controls: Where the meeting takes place (Zoom, phone, in person). Learn more.
  • Setting: Availability; What it controls: Set your date range, minimum notice, and available hours.
  • Setting: Host(s); What it controls: Choose who will host the event.

More options

Select More options to see these additional settings:

  • Setting: Description; What it controls: Add details for invitees before the meeting.
  • Setting: Limits and buffers; What it controls: Add buffer time or limit how often people can book.
  • Setting: Free/busy rules; What it controls: Let invitees book over events on connected calendars. Learn more.
  • Setting: Booking page options; What it controls: Customize your event link, start time increments, and time zone display.
  • Setting: Invitee form; What it controls: Ask invitees for info before the meeting. Learn more.
  • Setting: Payment; What it controls: Collect payments with Stripe or PayPal (Standard plan and above).
  • Setting: Notifications and workflows; What it controls: Set reminders and follow-ups.
  • Setting: Confirmation page; What it controls: Decide what invitees see after booking.

Additional settings

  • Event language – Pick the language for your event.
  • Event permissions – Choose who can view or edit the event.
  • Secret events – Hide the event from your main scheduling page.

After making your updates, your event is ready to share.

How to edit event type permissions

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

You can give others access to view or edit your personal event types. This makes it easier to collaborate and share scheduling links.

Note: Event type permissions are only available for personal and shared event types, not team event types. #### Edit permissions for an event type

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. (Optional) Open the My Calendly dropdown to switch to another user.
  3. Find the event type and select the [Image: 33339243986583] three dots on the event card.
  4. Choose Edit permissions.
  5. Search for the person you want to add. Then choose one of the following:
  • Can edit – lets the user change the event type settings.
  • Can view – lets the user see and share the event type, but not edit it.
  • Delete permission – removes their access.

  1. Select Apply to save your changes. #### Managed event permissions

Owners, admins, and group admins can update permissions for managed events using the same steps above.

  • You can grant view or edit access to an assignee.

How to organize and manage your event types

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Use the Event Types tab on the Scheduling page to organize your event types, share your scheduling links, and manage event type permissions.

This article walks you through using the Event Types tab and manage general event type settings. If you need to update availability, location, or questions for a specific event type, open its event type editor to make those changes.

You can also access and manage event types from the Home tab in the Calendly mobile app. For an overview of where to find event types and what actions are available on mobile, see Event types on the mobile app. #### How your event types are organized

In your My Calendly view (the default), event types are grouped into three sections:

  • Personal event types: These are event types tied to your personal scheduling page. They may have been created by you or assigned as managed events by an admin.

  • Shared: This section includes:

  • Event types you’re hosting that were shared with you by others.

  • Event types you have permission to view or edit, even if you’re not its owner.

  • Team event types: If you’re part of a team and listed as a host on a team event type, you’ll see that team and only the event types you’re hosting. #### Filter and search your event types

Use the tools at the top of the page to quickly find what you’re looking for:

  • My Calendly dropdown: Switch views between your personal page, team pages, or another user’s page (if you’re an admin).
  • Search bar: Look up event types by name or link.
  • Filter menu: Narrow results by host, owner, or access permissions. #### Reorder your event types

On a desktop browser, drag and drop your event types to reorder how they appear on both your Scheduling page and on your personal or team landing page. This helps prioritize which events your invitees see first. #### Quick actions on event type cards

Hover over an event type card to access these actions:

  • Book meeting: Instantly schedule a meeting on your calendar.
  • Offer time slots: Select and share specific times with invitees.
  • Share availability: Email your booking link directly from Calendly using your Gmail or Outlook account. Available for users on paid plans.
  • Create single-use link: Set up a one-time link that expires after it’s booked.

You can also use Copy link on each event type card to copy the standard booking link. #### Event type settings

To open the settings menu for an event type, select the [Image: 33352398946327] three dots in the top-right corner of its card.

  • Setting: View booking page; Description: Opens the scheduling page your invitees will see.
  • Setting: Edit; Description: Opens the event type editor to change availability and booking page preferences.
  • Setting: Edit permissions; Description: Manage who can view or edit the event type.
  • Setting: Add to website; Description: Embed your scheduling page on a website.
  • Setting: Add / edit internal note; Description: Add or edit a note visible only to your team.
  • Setting: Change invitee language; Description: Choose which language invitees see for your page and notifications.
  • Setting: Make secret; Description: Hide the event type from your landing page.
  • Setting: Make public; Description: Show the event type on your landing page.
  • Setting: Duplicate; Description: Create a copy of the event type.
  • Setting: Event statistics (team event types only); Description: Download a CSV file with recent meeting activity for each team member.
  • Setting: Delete; Description: Permanently remove the event type from your account. Scheduled meetings remain unaffected.
  • Setting: On/Off; Description: Control whether the event type is currently active.

Bulk edit your event types

To update multiple event types at once, check the boxes on the cards and use the bulk actions toolbar at the bottom of the page. You can:

  • Delete: Delete the selected event types.

How to require email verification for event types

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly has built-in spam protections to help prevent unwanted bookings. For added security, you can require email verification on your event types. This ensures that invitees have access to the email address they enter, helping reduce spam and confirming the use of valid email accounts.

This can be useful if you share your booking links on a website, social media, or in an email blast. This feature is available for all event types, including admin-managed event types. #### What invitees experience

  1. The invitee chooses a time, answers any questions, and selects Schedule Event.
  2. A verification step appears, and a 6-digit code is sent to the email they entered on the booking page.
  3. The invitee enters the code on the booking page to verify their email.

Once verified, the booking is confirmed, and they see the confirmation page. If the invitee does not complete verification, the event is not booked. #### Manage email verification from Account settings

  1. Select your profile picture, then go to All settings > Security.
  2. Select the checkbox next to each event type that you want to change email verification.
  3. Select Enable Verification to turn it on, or Disable Verification to turn it off.

The page will refresh and show your updated settings. #### Manage email verification from the Admin center

  1. Go to the Admin center.
  2. Select Security > Booking.
  3. Select the checkbox next to each event type that you want to change email verification.
  4. Select Enable Verification to turn it on, or Disable Verification to turn it off.

The page will refresh and show your updated settings. #### Frequently asked questions

Yes. Invitees must verify each time they book for event types with email verification enabled.

No. If verification isn’t completed, the meeting is not booked, and you won’t receive a notification.

No. Email verification settings apply immediately, but they don’t generate a notification.

Invitees can try:

  • Checking their spam or junk folder.
  • Confirming they entered the correct email address on the booking page.
  • Resending the code from the verification screen.

Use the Location section of your event type to choose where your meeting will take place. You can meet in person, by phone, over video, at a custom location, or let your invitee provide the location. #### Set the location

Calendly Meeting Polls help you quickly find a time that works for everyone. Invitees vote on the times they prefer, and once voting ends, you pick the best option. Calendly takes care of the scheduling and invites.

For example, you can:

Who can vote?

Anyone with the poll link can submit votes—even without a Calendly account. #### How to schedule the meeting

  1. Once voting ends, review results and select [Image: 33300825233815] Book next to the best time.
  2. (Optional) Select + Add Invitee to add any invitees who didn’t vote.

A poll closes when:

If deleted, the poll link becomes inactive and voting is disabled. #### Frequently asked questions

Round Robin distribution overview

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

Calendly’s Round Robin event type helps you share meetings between team members. There are two ways to do this:

  1. Maximize for availability Let invitees book with any team member who’s free. Use this setting if you want to book as many meetings as possible and don’t need to evenly share them across your team.
  2. Optimize for equal distribution Calendly will spread meetings fairly across your team. This can mean fewer bookings overall because availability is limited to keep things even.

Keep in mind, Round Robin event types can be booked multiple times during the same time frame, as long as there are available hosts. #### How “Maximize for Availability” Works

Calendly looks at your team’s calendars to find any time at least one host is free. If more than one person is available, Calendly uses priority stars to decide who gets the meeting.

Here’s how it works:

  • Calendly only schedules meetings with team members who are available.

  • Availability includes Calendly meetings and anything on connected calendars.

  • The teammate with the highest priority will be booked first.

  • If two teammates have the same priority and both are available:

  • The one who hasn’t had a recent meeting will be booked.

  • If it’s still a tie, Calendly will choose someone at random.

  • You can adjust priorities in the Hosts section of your event type settings. #### How “Optimize for Equal Distribution” Works

Calendly tracks how many Round Robin meetings each teammate has. It compares meeting counts to make sure no one is more than three meetings ahead.

If someone is ahead by 3 or more meetings:

  • Their availability is hidden until others catch up.
  • Once things are even again, their time slots will show up.

Example:

  • Jim has 3 meetings and Karen has 0.
  • Calendly hides Jim’s availability.
  • Once Karen gets a meeting, Jim is eligible again.
  • If Jim gets another, and the count goes back to 4–1, Calendly hides his availability again.

Note: If you add or remove a host from the event, the meeting count resets to zero for everyone. #### Frequently asked questions

Your new setting takes effect immediately with the next booking. Past settings or meeting counts won’t carry over.

If you or a teammate isn’t showing as available:

  • Use the Troubleshoot tool in your event type preview.
  • If you see the error “UNFAIR”, it means meeting counts are too uneven for someone to be scheduled.

Rescheduled Round Robin meetings reassign by default based on your distribution rules. You can change this setting to keep the original host instead.

  1. Go to Scheduling, then select your round robin event.
  2. Expand the Hosts section.
  3. Under Rescheduling preferences, choose to Reassign host(s) through the round robin or Use same hosts as original meeting.
  4. Select the Rescheduling preferences dropdown and change from Reassign host(s) through round robin to Use same hosts as original meeting.

  3. Under Extension integrations, toggle LinkedIn Messaging on or off. #### Share your meeting links

When composing a message, the Calendly icon appears in your LinkedIn toolbar. Click it to:

  • Share an event type:

  • Insert link - Adds your standard Calendly link to the message.

  • Insert single-use link - Create and add a one-time link that expires after it’s booked.

  • Create a one-off meeting or meeting poll, then share the link in your message. These options open in a pop-up window. #### Troubleshooting the Calendly for LinkedIn extension

I am unable to log in to LinkedIn with the extension.

If you’re having trouble logging in to LinkedIn or don’t see the Calendly prompt, try these steps:

  1. Make sure the LinkedIn integration is turned on.
  2. Confirm that you’re logged in to Calendly.
  3. Close any open LinkedIn tabs or sessions, then open a new one.
  4. On the new LinkedIn page, open the Calendly extension sidebar from your browser toolbar to allow access. #### I am experiencing browser issues with the extension.

If another extension is interfering with Calendly for LinkedIn, try these steps:

  1. Open your browser’s extensions menu.
  2. Turn off all extensions, including the Calendly extension.
  3. Turn the Calendly extension back on first, then re-enable your other extensions one at a time.
  4. Open a new window and try using Calendly for LinkedIn again.

How to troubleshoot the Outlook plug-in

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Follow these steps to fix issues with the Outlook Plug-In for desktops when encountering unexpected behaviors. #### Before you begin

Are you troubleshooting the Outlook plug-in or Outlook add-in ?

The Outlook plug-in connects Calendly directly to your Outlook calendar. It to check for conflicts and adds events. This is separate from the Outlook add-in, which allows you to access your scheduling links or create a customized invitation directly from your Outlook toolbar. It does need to be installed separately. For more information on the Outlook add-in, check out How to install the Calendly Outlook add-in. #### Troubleshooting the plug-in

Step 1 – Check your system requirements

You’ll need a PC with Outlook 2007 or later and Windows XP or newer.

If you use a web-based Microsoft calendar such as Outlook.com, Office 365, or Exchange, we recommend connecting that calendar directly from your Calendar settings page. For more information on how to connect your calendar with Calendly, check out Connecting your calendar. #### Step 2 – Check your calendar settings page

Check to make sure your plug-in is connected. If your Outlook plug-in is not connected, check out How to install the Outlook plug-in for instructions on how to install and connect your Outlook plug-in to Calendly. #### Step 3 – Check your plug-in version and last sync date

[Image: 26158619378327]

To fix most issues, make sure you are running the most up-to-date version of the Outlook plug-in (Version: 174). You can confirm this at any time by navigating to your Calendar settings page or by contacting our support team.

If you’re not running the most up to date version, check out How to install the Outlook plug-in for instructions on how to re-install and connect your Outlook plug-in to Calendly. #### Step 4 – Make sure you’re only running one version of the Outlook plug-in

In order for the Outlook plug-in to properly sync with Calendly, you should only run one instance of the Outlook plug-in per Calendly user. #### Step 5 – Check that your Outlook plug-in is your system tray icon

The Outlook plug-in will only sync when it is running in the background and your computer is connected to the internet. Any changes made while your computer is off and the plug-in is disconnected will only update once your device is back on. To check if your Outlook plug-in is running:

  1. Select the upwards-facing arrow in your Windows taskbar to Show hidden icons.
  2. From there, look for an item listed with the Calendly logo. [Image: 4617638354711]
  3. If you do not see an instance of the Outlook plug-in running in your taskbar, use your PC’s search bar to search for, and open the Calendly Plugin for Outlook. [Image: 4618345788695]
  4. If you do not see the Calendly Plugin for Outlook app within your search bar, the Outlook plug-in is not installed on your device. For more information on how to install the Outlook plug-in, check out How to install the Outlook plug-in. #### Step 6 – Check your Outlook plug-in advanced settings

Set your sync to “Realtime” so Calendly can update your Outlook calendar right away. To set your Outlook plug-in sync to realtime:

  1. Open the Outlook plug-in via the taskbar in Windows (or by searching for the Calendly Plugin for Outlook in your Windows search).

  2. Select Settings

  3. Select Advanced in the bottom left corner of the Settings window.

  4. Select Realtime under Auto-Sync within the Advanced Settings window.

  5. Select OK to confirm your changes within the Advanced Settings window.

  6. Select Save to save changes made within your Outlook plug-in Settings. [Image: 4631456651671]

  7. Open the Outlook plug-in via the taskbar in Windows (or by searching for the Calendly Plugin for Outlook in your Windows search).

  8. Select Settings

  9. Select Advanced in the bottom left corner of the Settings window.

  10. Check Reread Outlook and Reread Calendlyunder the section titled Logging.

  11. Select OK to confirm your changes within the Advanced Settings window.

  12. Select Save to save changes made within your Outlook plug-in Settings. [Image: 4639751328023]

  13. Open the Outlook plug-in via the taskbar in Windows (or by searching for the Calendly Plugin for Outlook in your Windows search).

  14. Press CTRL+SHIFT+U to open the Special Settings Screen.

  15. Check Disable MAPI to the right of Disable MAPI DLL for Outlook.

  16. Select OK to confirm your changes within the Advanced Settings window. [Image: 4640012450711]

Managed events & workflows

How to create a Managed Workflow

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans #### Overview

Managed Workflows are automated email and text messages. They work with Managed Events across your organization. Use these Workflows to create consistent messaging and a standard scheduling experience for everyone. #### Before you begin

  • Creating a Managed Workflow is just like making a regular Workflow. Follow this article for step-by-step instructions.
  • When a Managed Workflow is applied to a Managed Event, it applies to all assigned users and future scheduled events.
  • We recommend setting up your Managed Events first before deciding which ones should have Workflows.

Roles and permissions

Different roles have different permissions for Managed Workflows. For an overview of the different roles, check out this article.

Owners and admins:

  • Can create and apply Managed Workflows for all users.
  • Can lock the Notifications and Workflows section of the Managed Event. This stop users from adding personal Workflows.

Group admins:

  • Can create and apply Managed Workflows for their group.
  • Can lock the Notifications and Workflows section for group members.

Users:

  • Can view Managed Workflows in the Admin Managed Workflows tab or within each assigned Managed Event.
  • Cannot apply, edit, or remove Managed Workflows.
  • Can apply personal Workflows only if the Notifications and Workflows section is unlocked.
  • If an Admin locks the Notifications and Workflows section after a personal Workflow is applied, the personal Workflow will be removed.

Create a Managed Workflow

  1. From your Home page, select Admin Center.
  2. Under Templates, select Managed Workflows.
  3. Choose one of these options:

  • To use a template:

  • Choose a Workflow template from our library and click Use workflow.

  • To create a custom Workflow:

  • Select Create your own workflow.

  • In the When this happens section, choose a trigger and set the time.

  • In the Do this section, choose an action, then select Next.

  1. In the Workflow name section, enter a name for your Workflow.
  2. In the Which event types will this apply to? section, choose your event types for this Workflow, then select Apply.
  3. In the Do this section, select Edit and customize your email or text message, then select Done.

  • To insert variables that autofill meeting details:

  • Place your cursor in your message, click Variables in the toolbar, and choose a variable from the list.

  • It will automatically populate with the relevant information once the meeting is scheduled.

  1. (Optional) To include more actions in your Workflow, select Add Actions and repeat Step 3.
  2. After setting up your Workflow, select Save.

How to create and assign Managed Events

Available to Owners and Admins on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button] #### Overview

Managed Events are reusable event types designed to standardize meetings across your organization. Admins can edit, lock (Teams and Enterprise only), update, and assign them to users.

Create a Managed Event

  1. Go to the Admin center > Managed events.
  2. Select + Create.
  • To duplicate an existing managed event, select the three dots next to it and choose Duplicate.
  1. Choose either a One-on-one or Group event type. Learn more about different event types.
  2. Set up your event to meet your needs. Learn more about customizing your event types.
  3. Select Create.

Set editing permissions (lock and sync)

Editing permissions (available on Teams and Enterprise plans) let admins control whether assigned users can change event details. #### If editing is enabled for assignees

[Image: 29037586287639]

  • Assigned users can edit the selected fields.
  • Admin updates to the template do not sync to assignees. #### If editing is disabled

[Image: 29037599663639]

  • Assigned users cannot edit those fields.
  • Admin changes automatically sync for all assigned users.

Assign a Managed Event

Once you’ve created a Managed Event, assign it to users or groups:

  1. On the Managed events page, select the event you wish to assign to yours users or groups.
  2. Scroll down to expand the Assign section.
  3. Choose between Assign group(s) or Assign to people.
  4. Select + Add people or + Add groups.
  5. Search for and select the users or groups (active or pending).
  6. Select Assign.

The page refreshes with updated assignees. To unassign, select the X next to a user or group and confirm your choice.

Managed Events overview

Available to Owners and Admins on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Managed Events help your team stay aligned by using shared event templates. Admins can set up events, control which parts teammates can edit, and sync updates across all shared versions.

For example, you can:

  • Share a company-wide event type that updates in real time.

  • Let users personalize their booking links while locking the rest. #### Before you begin

  • You must be a Calendly owner or admin to create or manage them.

  • Each team member gets their own version, linked to the template.

  • Changes sync only for sections you’ve locked (editing turned off).

  • Teams and Enterprise plans: You can manage editing permissions for each section.

  • Professional plan: You can update events by un-assigning and reassigning them. This replaces the user’s version and removes any custom edits they made. #### Setting up Managed Events

Ready to set up Managed Events? These Help Center articles walk you through the steps.

  • How to create and assign Managed Events

  • How to customize your event types #### What else can you do with Managed Events?

  • Turn off editing for specific sections to sync updates automatically.

  • Let users adjust their own availability or reminders while keeping branding consistent.

  • Use templates for different teams, such as Sales, Success, or Recruiting. #### Best practices

For a user:

  • You’ll know an event type is a managed event by the [Image: 33336109077783] admin managed icon at the top of the event type card. [Image: 33336084630295]
  • You can manage the permissions of your managed events.

For an owner/admin:

  • Owners and admins can allow or disable editing for each section of a Managed Event.

  • If editing is disabled, the section is locked and stays synced with admin updates.

  • If editing is enabled, updates made by the admin won’t sync to users.

  • If you later disable editing, your next update will override any changes users made when editing was allowed.

  • Location is always editable.

  • Tip: Leave the Location field blank so users can add their preferred options. #### Troubleshooting

Changes didn’t sync to team members — why?

Check if editing is enabled for that section. Updates only sync when editing is disabled. #### Team members can’t see their events

Make sure the Managed Event was assigned to their account and they are in the correct team.

Workflows for admins

Available to Owners and Admins on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Help your team send the same emails and texts every time. Set up Workflows to reduce no-shows and keep meetings running smoothly.

As an admin, you can manage Workflows for all event types, including Managed Events. You can also control which members can create, edit, and delete Workflows in your organization. #### Workflows for Managed Events

Owners and admins on the Teams and Enterprise plans can create, update, and lock Managed Workflows for Managed Events that are assigned to users in the organization. To learn more, check out this article. #### Workflows for personal event types

Follow these steps to manage Workflows for a user:

[Image: 25627904946839]

Helpful resources:

  • How to create a Workflow
  • How to edit or delete Workflows #### Workflows for shared event types

Owners, admins, and shared event owners can manage Workflows for shared event types.

Follow these steps:

  2. Open the My Calendly dropdown and choose the event type owner.
  3. Create or edit the Workflow for the shared event type.

[Image: 25627904946839] #### Workflows for team event types

Owners, admins, and team managers can manage Workflows for team event types.

Follow these steps:

  2. Open the My Calendly dropdown menu and choose the team.
