Managing contacts

How to create a contact

Available to all users on all plans.View plans #### Overview

Easily add new contacts in Calendly to streamline scheduling and boost productivity. Follow these quick steps to get started.

Automatically created contacts

Calendly automatically creates contacts for each invitee who schedules with you from 2024 onward. Contacts are created or updated based on the type of event scheduled. Here’s how it works. #### New contacts

Newly created contacts will include:

  • Name
  • Email
  • Phone (if available)

For new invitees, here’s how contacts are created:

  • One-on-one and Group events: A new contact is created for the meeting host.
  • Collective events: A new contact is created for all hosts assigned to the event.
  • Round Robin events: A contact is created for the specific assigned host. #### Existing contacts

When an existing contact schedules a meeting, their contact card is automatically updated with the “next meeting” information in Calendly.

Create a contact

Want to add someone to your contacts? Just follow these steps:

  1. Go to the Contacts page.
  2. Select + Add contact in the upper right corner.
  3. Enter their details:
  • Required: Name and Email address.
  • Optional: Phone, Job title, Company, LinkedIn, Time zone, Country, City, and State.
  1. Select Save contact.

What’s next?

You’ve created a contact—great! Ready for what’s next? Here are a few ways to manage and schedule with your contacts:

  • Manage a contact: Edit or remove someone from your contact list.
  • Schedule with a contact: Book meetings quickly and efficiently.
  • Share availability: Send your open times directly from Calendly.

How to create and manage custom fields for contacts

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Create custom fields to track the details you need beyond standard contact info like name, email, or phone number. These fields appear in your Contacts table so you can view and manage that information in one place.

For example, you can:

  • Track responses to booking form questions using the invitee question field

  • Store contact details using text, currency, tags, date, or multi-select fields #### Before you begin

  • There is a limit of 10 custom attributes at one time

  • Custom fields pull data from booking form questions on your event types #### Create a custom field

  1. Go to Contacts

  2. Open the Columns dropdown

  3. Select + Create a custom field

  4. Choose a field type:

  5. Invitee question (from event types), or

  6. Text, number, currency, tag, date, multi-select

  7. If you chose Invitee question, select the event type and question

  8. Select Create

New responses appear in the contact’s record right away. You can also add or update values directly in the Contacts table. #### Edit or delete a custom field

  1. Go to Contacts
  2. Select the three vertical dots next to the custom field you want to update
  3. Select Edit custom field
  4. Make your changes and select Save changes, or choose Delete to remove the field.

How to delete a contact

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Delete contacts you no longer need from your Contacts page or from an individual contact’s detail page. #### Delete a contact

From the Contacts table

  1. Go to Contacts.
  2. Select one or more contacts.
  3. Select Delete.
  4. Confirm by selecting Delete again.

From the contact details page

  1. Go to Contacts.
  2. Select a contact to open the details page.
  3. Select the pencil icon next to the contact’s name.
  4. Select Delete.
  5. Confirm by selecting Delete again.

Note

Archiving contacts is not available at this time. #### What happens when you delete a contact?

When you delete a contact, Calendly stops auto-creating that contact in your system. If they schedule with you again in the future, you can manually add them as a new contact.

However, deleting a contact doesn’t remove their data from Calendly. To fully remove their data, submit a data deletion request.

How to import and export contacts

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Easily manage your contacts by importing new ones from CSV files and form integrations, or exporting your existing list. This helps you keep your scheduling data up to date and reuse contact details across tools. #### Before you begin

To import contacts, you’ll need:

  • A CSV file (for file imports) that includes at least name and email address, or
  • A connected form account (for Typeform)

For both import methods, you must have name and email as required fields. #### Import contacts from a CSV file

Note

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users.

Step 1 – Upload your CSV file

  1. Go to your Contacts page.
  2. Select + Add contact, then Import contacts from a file.
  3. Upload your CSV file.

Step 2 – Map your fields

Next, match each column in your file to a Calendly contact field. If you don’t want to import a column, leave it unmapped or select Exclude this field when mapping.

Each column from your file appears on the left. Use the dropdown to select a matching Calendly contact field on the right.

If a CSV column doesn’t match an existing Calendly field, you can create a new field. Choose from text, number, tag, currency, or date fields to add a custom field.

Required fields:

You must map:

  • Name
  • Email

Step 3 – Choose how to handle duplicates

  1. Select Continue.
  2. Choose how to handle duplicate contacts.
  • Merge with existing contact (default).
  • Overwrite with new information from the form.
  • Skip and don’t import this contact.
  1. Select Continue.

What happens next

After the import completes, you’ll see one of these outcomes:

  • All contacts imported successfully – Select View contacts to see your full list.
  • Some contacts imported, some skipped – Select Download skipped contacts to see which ones failed and why.
  • Contacts imported with field issues – Select View contacts with issues to check which fields didn’t import correctly. #### Import contacts from a form

Note

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users.

Connect Typeform to automatically turn form submissions into Calendly contacts. This saves you time and keeps your contact information organized without manual entry.

Step 1 – Connect your form account

If you’re already connected, skip to step 2.

  1. Go to your Contacts page.
  2. Select + Add contact, then choose Typeform
  3. Select Connect account.
  4. Sign in to your form account.
  5. Allow access when prompted.

Calendly will validate that you own the form before the connection is complete.

Tip

You can also connect by going to your Account settings → Contact settings and selecting your form type under Connect a form to add contacts.

Step 2 – Choose your form

If you’ve already connected your account, go to the Contacts page. Select + Add contact and choose where you want to import contacts from.

  1. Select the form you want to connect.
  2. Review the form name.
  • Give your form connection a clear, descriptive name so you’ll remember which form it’s connected to. You can’t change the name later.
  1. Select Continue.

You can connect up to 10 forms.

Step 3 – Map your form fields

Match each form field to a Calendly contact field so the right information gets captured.

  1. Select a Calendly contact field from the dropdown for each form field.
  • If a form field doesn’t match an existing contact field, you can Create a new field.
  • You can choose text, number, tag, currency, or date field types.
  1. Select the form fields you want to import (skip fields you don’t need).
  2. Select Continue.

Required fields:

You must map these fields:

  • Name
  • Email

Step 4 – Choose how to handle duplicates

  1. Choose how to handle duplicate contacts (contacts with the same email address).
  • Merge with existing contact (default).
  • Overwrite with new information from the form.
  • Skip and don’t import this contact.
  1. Select Continue.

Step 5 – Review and confirm

  1. Review your settings.
  2. Select Confirm connection.

Contacts will be created automatically from new form submissions going forward. Only new submissions create contacts. Previous submissions won’t be imported. #### Manage your form connections

Exclude email addresses or domains

You can exclude certain email addresses or entire domains from creating contacts automatically from the Contacts settings section of your Account settings. Form submissions from blocked addresses or domains won’t create new contacts.

Pause or resume a form

  1. Go to Account settings → Contacts settings.
  2. Find your form connection.
  3. Select the toggle to pause or resume.
  • Active: Contacts are being created from form submissions.
  • Paused: Form submissions won’t create new contacts.

When you resume a connection, it won’t import submissions from when it was paused.

Edit form connections

  1. Go to Account settings → Contacts settings.
  2. Find your form connection.
  3. Select the three dots menu.
  4. Select Edit form settings.
  5. Make your changes and select Save.

Disconnect a form

  1. Go to Account settings → Contacts settings.
  2. Find your form connection.
  3. Select the three dots menu.
  4. Select Remove form.
  5. Confirm by selecting Remove form again.

When you delete a form connection, any contacts already created stay in your contact list.

View contact source

You can see which contacts were created from a form. In your contact list, the Source column shows the form name. #### Export contacts

  1. Go to your Contacts page.
  2. Select the contact(s) you want to export.
  3. In the toolbar that appears at the bottom, choose Export.
  4. Your file downloads automatically.

You’ll also receive an email link to the file. The link expires in 24 hours.

Tip

To select all contacts at once, first select any contact to open the bottom toolbar. Then, choose Select all [x] contacts, where [x] is your total number of contacts.

Stay organized by editing contact details, managing communication preferences, reviewing meeting history, or removing contacts you no longer need.

Use this guide to manage your contacts in Calendly. #### Edit a contact

From the contact detail page

  1. Star the primary email you want to use for sending emails, sharing availability, booking meetings, and managing Workflows or reminders.

Important

Only the details you select will be saved, including email and meeting history. After you merge contacts, you can’t undo it.

How to add or remove users and seats

Available to Owners and Admins on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

With Calendly, you can easily manage users and seats. Each team member gets their own Calendly link and gains access to multi-user features, including centralized billing, collaborative scheduling, and reporting. Get started by inviting team members to join your Calendly account. #### Before you begin

Free plan users:

  • If you’re on Calendly’s Free plan, you’ll be prompted to upgrade to a paid plan and purchase seats before you can add team members.

Paid plan users:

  • Owners and Admins: Owners and Admins of Calendly organizations count as a paid user seat on your Calendly subscription. At this time, we do not have and ‘Admin’ role in a Calendly organization that does not take up a seat.
  • Paid plans with open sets: If you’re already on a paid plan with open seats, you can invite users without purchasing additional seats.
  • Paid plans with no open seats: If your account has no open seats, you will be prompted to purchase additional seats before sending invitations.

Permissions and limits for managing users and seats:

  • By default, both admins and group admins can invite users. You can adjust these permissions in the Permissions page under the Invitations tab.
  • A user can only be part of one organization at a time. If a user is already in another organization, their owner or admin must remove them before they can join your organization.
  • You can add up to 100 users at a time.
  • If your account is managed by Calendly (for example, Enterprise or customer success–managed plans), you can’t add or remove seats on your own. To make changes to your seat count, contact your Calendly account manager. #### Add users and paid seats

Adding users

When adding a new user, Calendly checks if there are available open seats. If there’s an open seat, it will be assigned to the new user. If not, you’ll need to purchase a new seat before sending the invitation.

  1. Go to your Users page in your Admin Center, then select Invite users.
  2. Enter the email addresses of the users you want to invite.
  3. (Optional for users on Teams and Enterprise plans) Assign the users to a group.
  4. Select Next.
  5. If you need to add seats, a popup will show the seat details and prorated costs. Confirm the changes to continue.
  6. Assign user or admin roles for each person and select Next.
  7. (Optional) Assign Managed Event types for each person.
  8. Select Send invitation.

Note

All users in a Calendly organization must be on the same plan. Individual users can’t have different plans within the same organization. #### Adding seats without inviting users

You can add seats without immediately inviting users. This allows you to expand your seat count for future use, even if you’re not ready to invite new users yet.

  1. Go to the Admin Center and select Billing.
  2. On your Billing page, select Add seats. [Image: 27176607916439]
  3. Enter the number of seats you’d like to purchase and confirm by selecting Add seats.

Note

This option isn’t available for Enterprise or CS-managed accounts. Contact your account manager to request additional seats. #### What’s next?

  • You can monitor pending invitations in the Pending tab on the Users page.

  • There is no expiration on user invitations.

  • If a user hasn’t accepted their Calendly invite after 7 days, Calendly automatically sends a one-time reminder email.

  • The user must be logged into Calendly with the same email the invite was sent to.

  • Once a user accepts the invite, new Calendly users will set up their account, while existing users will join with their personal events and settings intact.

  • If a user can’t accept the invitation, they may see an error like “You’re already in a different organization” and be prompted to contact Support to complete the change. #### Remove users and paid seats

Removing a user

When you remove a user from your organization, their paid seat remains available. This lets you invite a new user to fill the seat without needing to purchase an additional one.

  1. Go to your Users page in your Admin Center.
  2. Choose the user you want to remove and select Remove.

You’ll see two options:

  • Remove: Frees up the seat, but the user keeps their personal Calendly account.
  • Remove and delete: Also permanently deletes the user’s account. This option is available only if the user created their Calendly account while joining your organization.

Once removed, whether or not their account is deleted, the user receives a notification email. If not deleted, they’ll move to Calendly’s free Basic plan and can continue using their account independently. #### Removing a seat

If you don’t plan to invite another user to fill an open seat, you can remove the unused paid seat.

  1. Go to the Admin Center and select Billing.
  2. On your Billing page, select Remove seats. [Image: 27176607917335]
  3. Enter the number of seats you’d like to remove and confirm by selecting Remove seats.

Note

This option isn’t available for Enterprise or CS-managed accounts. Contact your account manager to reduce seats. #### Leaving your current organization for non-Admin users

If you are a part of a Calendly organization and want to leave it:

Ask an Owner or Admin of the organization to remove you:

  • They should go to their Admin Center, then select Users.
  • Find your name in the user list.
  • Select the 3 dots [Image: 37964570186519] next to your name and select Remove.
  • Confirm removal.

After you’re removed:

  • Your personal Calendly account will remain active.
  • You can continue using your Calendly account independently. #### Frequently asked questions

The Standard plan is unavailable if you are trying to assign the user to a group.

Groups are only supported on the Teams plan and higher. To use groups, you’ll need to upgrade your plan or add the user without assigning them to a group.

You can’t reduce your seat count below the number of users currently assigned.

Before lowering seats, remove or unassign users until the total number of assigned users matches (or is less than) your desired seat count.

To remove a user, go to the Admin center and select Users. Choose the user you want to remove, then select Remove. Learn more about removing users.

  • You’ll be charged a pro-rated amount based on your billing cycle.

  • If the user already paid for a subscription, we’ll refund the unused portion — no action needed.

  • Removing a user doesn’t remove their seat

  • Active seats stay on the account for easier replacements

Want to remove a seat? Follow these steps.

This error usually means you are logged into a different Calendly account.

Try these steps:

  1. Open the link in a private or incognito browser window.
  2. Make sure you are logged into the correct Calendly account.
  3. Log out of any extra Calendly accounts open in other tabs.

Then try the link again.

Only an organization admin or owner can remove users from an account.

If you want to leave the organization, contact your admin and ask them to remove you.

What if I can’t contact the admin?

If you no longer have contact with the admin or owner, contact us.

For security reasons, you may need to verify your account before changes can be made.

If your organization offers Calendly, you must be invited to join their account.

To join:

  1. Check your inbox for an invitation email.
  2. Look in your spam or junk folder if you don’t see it.
  3. Make sure you are logged in with the same email address that received the invite.
  4. Accept the invitation.

If you did not receive an invite, contact your organization’s Calendly admin. Only an admin can add you to the account.

How to merge or migrate organizations

Available to Owners and Admins on Standard, Professional, and Teams plans.View plans

Need to transfer team members from one Calendly organization to another? Follow these steps to make sure the process goes smoothly.

Note

If you’re on an Enterprise plan, reach out to your Calendly account representative for assistance with organization management. #### Step 1 – Add seats to the new organization

Before you move anyone, make sure your new organization has enough open seats. You’ll need one open seat per user you plan to invite.

Once seats are available, you’re ready to move users. #### Step 2 – Remove the user from their old organization

An admin from the user’s current organization must remove them first.

Removing a user from their organization does not delete any of their event types or settings. #### Step 3 – Invite the user to your new organization

After they’re removed from their previous organization, you can invite them to join yours.

Once they accept, Calendly automatically assigns them to an open seat in your organization. #### What information is migrated?

Expand the section below to see what information is and isn’t moved during account migration.

When users migrate to a new organization, Calendly brings over their key settings.

  • Attribute: Schedule Link; Transferred: ✅; Description: The user’s personal scheduling link is retained.
  • Attribute: Availability Settings; Transferred: ✅; Description: Their working hours and availability settings are transferred.
  • Attribute: Individual Event Types; Transferred: ✅; Description: All personal (non-team) event types are migrated.
  • Attribute: Routing Forms; Transferred: ❌; Description: Routing forms do not transfer between organizations.
  • Attribute: Team, Shared, & Managed Event Types; Transferred: ❌; Description: These event types are tied to the original org and are not moved.
  • Attribute: Managed Events; Transferred: ❌; Description: Managed Events must be recreated in the new organization.
  • Attribute: Connected Calendars; Transferred: ✅; Description: Any external calendars already connected are preserved.
  • Attribute: User-Level Integrations; Transferred: ✅; Description: Includes tools like Zoom, Google Meet, and calendar connections.
  • Attribute: Zapier & Payment Integrations; Transferred: ❌; Description: Zapier and payment integrations (PayPal and Stripe) are not migrated.
  • Attribute: User Profile Data; Transferred: ✅; Description: Name, profile picture, and contact info move with the user.
  • Attribute: Historical Data; Transferred: ❌; Description: Past activity, like analytics, is not included.
  • Attribute: Meetings; Transferred: ✅; Description: All scheduled meetings remain on the connected calendar.
  • Attribute: Billing Records; Transferred: ❌; Description: Billing history stays with the original organization for tax purposes.
  • Attribute: Org-Level Integrations; Transferred: ❌; Description: Integrations managed at the org level (e.g. Salesforce, HubSpot, and Google Analytics) are not moved.

What are the limitations of account migration?

Account migration comes with a few limitations:

  • Users can’t belong to two organizations at once: Users can only be added to a new organization after being removed from their current organization.
  • No historical data is moved: Past meetings and events won’t transfer. Future meetings will still appear in the Meetings page.
  • Billing records stay with the original organization: These are kept for tax and record-keeping purposes.
  • Polls aren’t moved: Any in-progress polls will be deleted during migration. #### FAQs

No. At this time, Calendly does not support merging accounts.

How to request bulk deletion of users

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

Customers on an Enterprise plan can request to delete multiple user accounts from their Calendly organization. This guide outlines how to securely submit a request for bulk user deletions. #### Before you begin

  • This bulk deletion process is only available for Enterprise plan customers.

  • Deleted user accounts are permanently removed and cannot be recovered.

  • The following users cannot be deleted:

  • Calendly account owner

  • Previously deleted users

  • Users deactivated via SCIM

  • Users currently being updated

  • For more information on data removal, review our User Data Deletion Policy.

  • After deletion, all personally identifiable information (PII) will be removed from Calendly, as outlined in our Privacy Policy. #### Submit the bulk deletion request

Download the template

  • Make a copy of this spreadsheet template.

  • The template includes a single column for entering email addresses. #### Prepare your list

  • Enter the email addresses of the users you want to delete into the spreadsheet.

  • Verify each email address is in its own row within the designated column.

  • Do not add any additional data or formatting to the spreadsheet. #### Submit your request

  • Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) to submit your bulk deletion request.

  • Attach the completed spreadsheet to your request.

  • Confirm that you understand the deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. #### What’s next?

We’ll review your request and delete the user accounts once it’s approved. You’ll receive a confirmation once the deletion process is complete.

If you have any questions or need help, please contact your Customer Success Manager.

User management

Available to Owners and Admins on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Admins and owners can manage users from the Users page in the Admin Center. This includes inviting new users, assigning roles, managing pending invites, and exporting user data. #### Add or remove users and seats

Owners and admins can manage users and seats across the organization. For detailed steps, check out this article. #### Change a user’s role

You can update a user’s role by making them a regular user, admin, or the organization owner. For more details about roles, check out this article.

  1. Go to the Users page.
  2. Find the user whose role you want to change.
  3. Select the [Image: Settings Menu] three dots at the end of the row.
  4. Select Change Role.
  5. Choose a new role: User, Admin, or Owner.
  6. Select Apply to confirm. #### Notes about transferring ownership:
  • Each organization can only have one owner.
  • Transferring ownership will make the current owner an Admin.
  • If your shared or team event types use a payment integration, such as Stripe or PayPal, the new owner will need to reconnect their account on the Integrations page. #### Make bulk changes to users

To make changes to multiple users at once, select the checkbox next to each user’s name. A bulk action toolbar will appear at the top of the page with the following options:

Bulk actions for active users:

  • Change role
  • Add to group
  • Remove members
  • Apply managed events

Bulk actions for pending users:

  • Remove
  • Resend invite #### Remove a pending user
  1. Go to the Users page.
  2. Open to the Pending tab.
  3. Find the user.
  4. Select the [Image: Settings Menu] three dots at the end of the row.
  5. Choose Remove.
  6. Select Yes to confirm. #### Resend a pending invite

Calendly will automatically resend a pending invite after 7 days, but you can resend it manually at any time.

  1. Go to the Users page.
  2. Open to the Pending tab.
  3. Find the user.
  4. Select the [Image: Settings Menu] three dots at the end of the row.
  5. Choose Resend invite. #### Export a list of organization members

Owners and admins can download a CSV report of organization members. The report includes:

  • Name
  • Login email
  • Role
  • Calendly link
  • Date added
  • Calendar connection status
  • Date of their last meeting (based on invitee booking)
  • Days since last event
  • Total events scheduled in the past 30 days (including canceled events)

To export:

  1. Go to the Users page.
  2. Select Export.
  3. Choose either Active or Pending users.
  4. A CSV file will download automatically, or you’ll receive an email with the file. #### Update Workflow permissions

Admins and owners can control Workflow permissions, setting which team members can create, edit, and delete Workflows.

  1. Go to the Admin Center.
  2. Select Permissions, then open the Workflowstab.
  3. Under Who can create, edit and delete workflows?, choose one:
  • All members of my organization
  • Only admins and the owner
  1. Select Save.

Note

If you select Only admins and the owner, Workflows can only be created for them. You won’t be able to create Workflows on behalf of others. #### Frequently asked questions

Only a current Owner or Admin can give Admin access in an organization.

If you need Admin access:

  1. Contact your organization’s current Owner or Admin.
  2. Ask them to update your role.

If no Owner or Admin is available, contact Calendly Support for help.

Support may need to verify your request before making any changes to the account.

No. User management features are only available on paid plans.

The Free plan does not support:

  • Adding users
  • Removing users

To manage users or change ownership, upgrade to a paid plan that includes user management features.

User roles and permissions

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Calendly offers 5 different roles:

  • Owner
  • Admin
  • Group admin
  • Team manager
  • User

The following table outlines some key permissions and use cases for each role:

  • Role: Owner; Available on: All plans; Amount: One per account; Best for…: Business owner, IT admin, or the person creating the Calendly account; Main permissions: - All permissions - Can transfer ownership to another user if in a multi-user organization
  • Role: Admin; Available on: All paid plans; Amount: Unlimited; Best for…: Company or IT admins; those who want full control over all Calendly users; Main permissions: - All permissions - Cannot change the owner of an account
  • Role: Group admin; Available on: - Teams - Enterprise; Amount: Unlimited; Best for…: Department managers; those who need to manage a subset of people in Calendly based on department, location, job function, etc. Added from the group page; Main permissions: - Can pull reporting and view meetings of group members - Can create teams - Can create routing forms - Can invite users to join an organization (with permissions enabled), invite users to existing groups - Can be members of multiple groups at once withouthaving to be a member
  • Role: Team manager; Available on: All paid plans; Amount: Unlimited; Best for…: Team leads; those who need to manage a set of team events or a team booking page, oftentimes for cross-departmental scheduling. Added from the team page; Main permissions: - Can create and manage event types that appear on a team booking page - Can add or remove users from their team
  • Role: User; Available on: All paid plans; Amount: Unlimited; Best for…: People who use Calendly, but don’t need to edit anything on behalf of others. Anyone you add to your account will default to the user role; Main permissions: - Have their personal scheduling page, (calendly.com/janedoe) - Can only edit their personal settings - Can be added to groups and teams, and included in team event types

Adding, removing, and deleting users

The following table outlines who can add, remove, and delete users from the Calendly account.

  • Remove users; Owner: ✔️; Admin: ✔️; Group Admin: 𝙓; Team Manager: 𝙓; User: 𝙓
  • Delete a user’s Calendly account; Owner: ✔️ Can only delete a user’s Calendly account if it was created when joining the organization; Admin: ✔️ Same as owner; Group Admin: 𝙓; Team Manager: 𝙓; User: 𝙓

Meeting data

AI at Calendly

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users. Release notes

Note

Calendly’s AI features are being gradually rolled out to eligible users.

Calendly uses AI to help you save time and get more value from every meeting. Our AI features reduce manual steps and make it easier to take action—before and after meetings.

With AI at Calendly, you can:

  • Turn meeting conversations into clear notes, summaries, and action items
  • Get quick answers about your events, availability, and scheduling activity
  • Use natural language to ask questions and take action in Calendly
  • Reduce time spent searching for event details or updating schedules
  • Stay organized with accurate, easy-to-share meeting insights

Some products that use AI at Calendly include:

  • Notetaker – Automatically records, summarizes, and highlights key moments from meetings
  • Ask Callie – Lets you use conversational prompts to discover meeting, contact, and recap details across Calendly
  • Callie AI Scheduling Assistant – Helps you schedule meetings through natural, conversational requests, handling availability, coordination, and booking on your behalf

This page gives an overview of how AI works at Calendly and explains how we protect your data and keep your information private and secure. #### Frequently asked questions

No. Calendly does not sell customer data or use it to train AI models.

Calendly securely stores AI-related logs to improve accuracy and your overall experience. These logs follow Calendly’s security policies and are protected with strict access controls. Access is limited to authorized personnel who require it to support or improve the product.

Calendly uses AI to make your work easier and more intuitive. When you use AI-powered features, AI providers receive only the minimum data needed for that feature to work.

Calendly currently uses large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI and may add other vetted providers over time. All providers must follow strict rules on how long data can be stored and how it can be used.

The data you submit and the responses you receive are used only to serve your experience. They are not used to train models across customers or shared between customers.

No. Calendly does not allow any third-party AI provider to use your data to train their models.

The data an AI feature can access depends on the feature.

  • Calendly Notetaker uses meeting recordings and transcripts to create summaries. In some cases, it may also access your calendar to identify attendees and match speakers to the transcript.
  • Calendly AI Assistant reviews your data in the Calendly app to give accurate answers and take actions based on your request.

Yes.

Similar to other cloud software companies, Calendly works with trusted sub-processors to run and support its service. Some of them use AI in their own systems.

For example, Calendly runs on Google Cloud. Google uses AI to help manage its cloud systems, data, and security.

This AI supports the tools that power Calendly. It does not change how your scheduling data is handled.

Calendly does not provide an opt out for its AI features. Instead, in most cases, users have the option to determine whether they want to use an AI feature.

Yes. AI can make mistakes, so always review AI-generated content before using or sharing it.

How to delete a Notetaker recap

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users. Release notes

Note

Notetaker is being gradually rolled out to eligible users. Join the waitlist.

Learn how to delete Notetaker recaps—like summaries, transcripts, and action items—for one meeting or all meetings recorded by Notetaker.. #### Before you begin

  • Enable Notetaker for your meetings.
  • Notetaker can record Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams meetings, regardless of whether you’re the host or if the meeting was scheduled through Calendly or your Google Calendar. #### Delete a recap from one meeting

From the Recaps page

  1. Go to your Recaps page.

  2. Select the recap.

  3. In the top right corner, select [Image: 29391678366487] More.

  4. Select Delete recap.

  5. Confirm by selecting Delete meeting recap. #### From the Meetings page

  6. Go to your Meetings page.

  7. Find and select the Past meeting with the recap.

  8. Select the [Image: 29391678366487] three dots next to the meeting title.

  9. Select Delete recap.

  10. Confirm by selecting Delete meeting recap. #### Delete all Notetaker data

From Account settings

  1. Go to the Notetaker settings page.
  2. At the bottom right, select Delete Calendly Notetaker data.
  3. Check the boxes to verify your intent.
  4. Reconfirm by selecting Delete Calendly Notetaker data.

Account FAQs

8 questions

When you add a new user, Calendly charges a pro-rated amount for their seat. The amount will depend on the time left on your current billing cycle.

If the added user already paid for an annual plan, Calendly refunds the unused part of their plan when they join your organization. You don’t need to take any extra steps.

When a user, Calendly creates a seat for them in your account. If you remove a user, the seat stays unless you remove it.

This helps teams switch out users without needing to change billing right away.

To remove a seat:

  • Go to yourBilling page.
  • Open the drop down menu.
  • Select Remove Users.

Owners and Admins can view and edit users’ event types and meetings. However, your Calendly home page will default to your personal event types.

To view another user:

  • Select the My Calendly drop down menu.
  • Choose the user you want to view.

Note: You can view your users’ calendar connections and video conferencing integrations from theirprofile. However, you can’t change their account settings - those must be set on their end.

Only the current organization owner can transfer ownership. Follow the steps inthis article to change user roles.

After ownership is transferred, your account becomes an admin. An admin or the new owner can then remove your account from the organization.

If the current owner isn’t available, contact our support team. We’ll ask for some account details to help complete the ownership transfer.

By default, Calendly will use the login email to send invoices to. You can, however, update the billing email address without changing your login email address in a couple of ways.

  • Add an additional billing contact to receive invoice and payment related emails. To do so, please contact our support team for assistance. Have the new contact’s email address and the last 4 digits of the card on file ready.
  • Change ownership of the Calendly organization. The owner is the primary billing contact by design. Changing ownership will also update the billing contact.

Calendly is committed to General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) compliance. We understand the importance of incorporating standards put forth by the GDPR into our data practices and making sure our customers feel secure and confident to continue using Calendly.

Calendly has designed its data privacy program to be compliant with GDPR and other applicable privacy laws, both now and in the future.

We have incorporated aData Processing Addendum into ourTerms of Use. There is nothing additional for you to sign or execute, and by accepting the Terms of Use, the DPA is already in place for you. Calendly’s DPA also includes both the SCCs and UK Addendum.

Please contact us and we will be happy to process your request.

Admins FAQs

10 questions

From the Users page in the Admin Center, owners and admins can invite and remove users, assign or change roles, manage pending invites, apply bulk actions, and export a CSV list of organization members. They can also transfer ownership, manage seats, assign users to groups or managed events, and track key user details like roles, calendar connection status, and recent scheduling activity.

When you open the Scheduling or Meetings page, you will see your own event types and meetings by default. At the top of the page, open the My Calendly dropdown next to the search bar and select the user or team you want to manage.

No. Each person must connect their own calendar from their Calendly account.

Admins may see whether a calendar is connected from the Users page, but they cannot connect, disconnect, or change another person’s calendar settings.

There is no shared or organization-wide calendar connection setting.

Groups in Calendly help admins organize users by department, team, or location so they can manage members, delegate permissions, and track meetings and activity at a group level. Owners and admins can manage all groups, while group admins can oversee users and reports for their assigned groups without needing full admin access. Enterprise customers can also use SCIM to automatically provision users into groups.

The Admin Center is where owners, admins, and group admins manage users, groups, and organization-wide settings in Calendly. From the Admin Center, you can view organization activity, manage users and roles, organize groups, control login and security settings, handle billing, and configure scheduling settings like permissions, branding, managed events, and workflows. Users without admin access will only see the organization directory.

Admins can manage Workflows across their organization to ensure consistent email and text communication and reduce no-shows. Owners and admins can create and manage Workflows for Managed Events, while admins can also manage Workflows for individual users’ personal event types. Shared event Workflows can be managed by owners, admins, and shared event owners, and team event Workflows can be managed by owners, admins, and team managers.

Currently, you can create One-on-One events or Group events as Managed Events.

Admins control this through editing permissions. You can allow or prevent editing by section. If disabled, those sections are locked and automatically sync with admin updates.

After a user is added through SCIM, Calendly sends them an email invitation. The user must accept the invite and sign in using SSO to complete setup. Once they sign in, they’ll take one of your available seats.

If the user doesn’t receive the invite, contact Calendly support and let us know whether the user is a new employee. Enabling SCIM doesn’t affect the user’s calendar or existing integrations, and admins can assign Managed Events or groups after the user is provisioned.

When SSO is enabled, all users are immediately signed out of Calendly and must log back in using their identity provider (IdP) credentials. From that point on, users can no longer sign in with a Calendly password and must use SSO to access their account.

Admins and owners still have the option to Log in using another method, which is useful for troubleshooting or disabling SSO if there’s an IdP issue. Enabling SSO doesn’t change users’ calendars or integrations, but users outside of your IdP won’t be able to log in—so be sure to notify your team before turning it on.

Calendly + PayPal

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Collect payments when invitees schedule a meeting by integrating PayPal with Calendly. Connect your account and choose which events will require payment upfront, helping you save time and reduce no-shows.

Note

A Business PayPal account is required to accept payments. #### Supported payment methods and currencies with PayPal

Payment methods

Calendly supports the following payment methods through PayPal:

  • PayPal wallet
  • Venmo (U.S. only)
  • Major credit and debit cards

For more details, review PayPal’s article on supported payment methods.

Note

If these payment methods aren’t available to your invitees during checkout, you may need to update your PayPal connection.

Visit your PayPal integrations page to learn more and update your connection. #### Currencies

Calendly currently supports payments in the following currencies through PayPal:

  • $ AUD - Australian Dollar
  • $ CAD - Canadian Dollar
  • € EUR - Euro
  • £ GBP - Pound Sterling
  • $ USD - United States Dollar #### How Calendly collects payments based on event types

The PayPal account used to collect payments depends on the event type’s setup:

  • For personal event types (one-on-one and group), Calendly uses the PayPal account connected by the host.
  • For shared or team event types (round robin, collective, and group), Calendly uses the PayPal account connected by the organization’s owner.

If you’re using a single PayPal account for your organization, you can either share those credentials with each user to connect it to their personal event types, or set up shared or team event types instead. #### Connect PayPal with your own Calendly account

Each user must connect their own PayPal account to collect payments for personal event types. Admins can’t connect PayPal on behalf of other users.

  1. Go to the Integrations & apps page.
  2. Find and select PayPal.
  3. Connect your account.
  • If you don’t have a PayPal account, you’ll be prompted to create one.

After connecting PayPal, you’ll need to turn on payments for each event type where you want to collect payments. #### Collect payments through PayPal for an event type

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. (Optional) Open the My Calendly dropdown to switch to another user or team.
  3. Choose the event type and select More options from the bottom of the editor.
  4. Expand the Payment section.
  5. Select Accept payments with PayPal.
  6. Specify the amount and currency to be collected when an event is scheduled.
  7. Customize your payment terms and cancellation policy with any information an invitee may need before confirming their payment.
  8. Select Save changes.

Note

Calendly does not calculate or collect VAT or sales tax. If needed, include tax in the event price or add tax details to your payment terms. #### Viewing payment details

Once an invitee schedules a meeting through your connected event type and completes a transaction via PayPal, you can view the transaction link directly from the event’s details on the Meetings page. #### Stop collecting payments from an event type

To change a paid event type back to free:

  1. Go to the More options section of the event type editor.
  2. Expand the Payment section.
  3. Select Do not collect payments for this event.
  4. Click Save changes.

Your event is now set as a free event. #### Disconnect PayPal from Calendly

To completely disconnect PayPal from your Calendly account:

  1. Go to the Integrations & apps page.
  2. Find and select PayPal.
  3. Select Disconnect.

Once PayPal is disconnected, any event types that were accepting payments will no longer require payment in order to book. #### Frequently asked questions

No, Calendly doesn’t currently support discount or promo codes with the PayPal integration. Use our Stripe integration if you want to offer coupon codes.

As another option, duplicate your event type, set a lower price, and make it a secret event. Then share the link directly with invitees who should receive the discount. See a full example in our Community post.

No, refunds must be processed manually by the account holder. Calendly support will direct invitees to contact you regarding any payments they submit through your scheduling page.

If you’re having trouble connecting your PayPal account to Calendly, try selecting United States as your country on the PayPal login screen, even if you’re located outside the US:

[Image: 25830426070551]

Selecting United States at this step will not affect your PayPal Business account settings. If the integration still doesn’t work, contact us for help.

If a meeting was booked without a successful PayPal payment, try reconnecting your PayPal account.

To fix this:

  1. Go to the Integrations & apps page.
  2. Find and select PayPal.
  3. Select Disconnect.
  4. Reconnect your PayPal account.
  5. Test with a new booking.

If the issue continues, contact us and share:

  • The event type name
  • The booking date and time
  • The PayPal transaction ID (if you have it)

Calendly + Stripe

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Collect payments when invitees schedule a meeting by integrating Stripe with Calendly. Connect your account and choose which events will require payment upfront, helping you save time and reduce no-shows. #### Supported payment methods and currencies with Stripe

Payment methods

Calendly supports the following payment methods through Stripe:

  • Most major credit and debit cards
  • Apple Pay
  • Google Pay
  • Instant Bank payments with Link
  • Buy now, pay later with Affirm and Klarna (subject to availability)

When you connect Stripe, all of the payment methods listed above are turned on by default. To turn one off, go to your Stripe payment method settings, open the Calendly configuration, and manage the payment options from there.

For more details, review Stripe’s article on supported payment methods.

Note

Apple Pay only appears at checkout when invitees use Safari, have Apple Wallet set up, and are viewing a direct Calendly link rather than an embedded scheduling page. #### Currencies

Calendly currently supports payments in the following currencies through Stripe:

  • $ AUD - Australian Dollar
  • $ CAD - Canadian Dollar
  • € EUR - Euro
  • £ GBP - Pound Sterling
  • $ USD - United States Dollar #### How Calendly collects payments based on event types

The Stripe account used to collect payments depends on the event type’s setup:

  • For personal event types (one-on-one and group), Calendly uses the Stripe account connected by the host.
  • For shared or team event types (round robin, collective, and group), Calendly uses the Stripe account connected by the organization’s owner.

If you’re using a single Stripe account for your organization, you can either share those credentials with each user to connect it to their personal event types, or set up shared or team event types instead. #### Connect Stripe with your own Calendly account

Each user must connect their own Stripe account to collect payments for personal event types. Admins can’t connect Stripe on behalf of other users.

  1. Log into Calendly and go to the Integrations page.
  2. Find and select Stripe.
  3. Connect your account.
  • If you don’t have a Stripe account, you’ll be prompted to create one.
  • Your Stripe account must be in live mode to accept real payments through Calendly.

After connecting Stripe, you’ll need to turn on payments for each event type where you want to collect payments. #### Collect payments through Stripe for an event type

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. (Optional) Open the My Calendly dropdown to switch to another user or team.
  3. Choose the event type and select More options from the bottom of the editor.
  4. Expand the Payment section.
  5. Toggle on Require payment to book this meeting.
  6. Make sure the Payment processor is set to Stripe.
  7. Enter the amount and currency to be collected.
  8. To set up a coupon, select + Create coupon code. See Create a coupon code below for details.
  9. Customize your payment terms and cancellation policy with any information an invitee may need before confirming their payment.
  10. Select Save changes.

Note

Calendly does not calculate or collect VAT or sales tax. If needed, include tax in the event price or add tax details to your payment terms. #### Create a coupon code for an event type with Stripe

Coupon codes (sometimes called discount or promo codes) let you offer discounts on paid events. They’re created and managed in the Payment section of an event type in Calendly.

Each event type has its own set of coupon codes. Code names must also be unique across your account, so you can’t reuse the same code name (for example, WELCOME10).

To create a coupon code:

  1. Select + Create coupon code.
  2. In the pop-up window, enter your details:
  • Code: what invitees will enter at checkout.
  • Coupon name: appears on receipts and invoices.
  • Type: choose percentage off or fixed amount off, then enter the discount value.
  • Options (optional): add restrictions such as first-time only, usage limits, or an expiration date.
  1. Select Create to save your code. #### Meeting packages and payment links

Beta

This feature is currently in private beta and available to a limited group of users.

With Calendly Payments, you can charge for bundled meetings or send payment links for extra services—all in one place.

With Payments, you can:

  • Create meeting packages to sell prepaid bundles of one-on-one sessions. Clients pay upfront and book their sessions over time using a unique link.
  • Create payment links to collect payments without scheduling a meeting, such as deposits, follow-up charges, or digital products.

This feature is currently in private beta and available to select users with Stripe connected. Learn more about meeting packages and payment links. #### Viewing payment details

Once an invitee schedules a meeting through your connected event type and completes a transaction via Stripe, you can view the transaction link directly from the event’s details on the Meetings page. #### Stop collecting payments from an event type

To change a paid event type back to free:

  1. Go to the More options section of the event type editor.
  2. Expand the Payment section.
  3. Select Do not collect payments for this event.
  4. Click Save changes.

Your event is now set as a free event. #### Disconnect Stripe from Calendly

To completely disconnect Stripe from your Calendly account:

  1. Log into Calendly and go to the Integrations page.
  2. Find and select Stripe.
  3. Select Disconnect.

Once Stripe is disconnected, any event types that were accepting payments will automatically become free. #### Frequently asked questions

No, refunds must be processed manually by the account holder. Calendly support will direct invitees to contact you regarding any payments they submit through your scheduling page.

When someone reaches the payment step but doesn’t finish booking, Stripe creates a temporary record labeled “Incomplete” or “Uncaptured.”

These aren’t failed charges. They show that someone opened the payment form but didn’t complete their booking in Calendly.

Confirmed bookings will still appear as “Successful” in Stripe, with full invitee details.

Yes, you can create coupon codes that give invitees a 100% discount, making their meeting free. If the coupon covers the full price, your invitee will skip the Stripe checkout process and no transaction will appear in Stripe.

Yes! Calendly has implemented the new 3D Secure to Stripe functionality to comply with the new larger second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) regulations implemented by the European Parliament.

If both you (the account owner) and your invitee are in the EU, the purchase of your event using our Stripe integration will result in a pop-up that will confirm authorization of payment from your invitee. Your invitee should receive a two-factor authentication message (however their bank chose to set it up) to authorize the payment. It will differ from bank to bank, but an example is below:

[Image: 16588146951063]

If a team member is seeing an error when trying to collect payments, check the following:

Stripe account connect

Each user must connect their own Stripe account to collect payments for personal event types. Admins cannot Stripe on behalf of other users.

Event type setup

Make sure the event type is set to require payment and that Stripe is selected as the payment processor in the event’s payment settings.

Currency and payment method support

Confirm that the currency and payment methods used for the event are supported by Stripe and enabled in the connected Stripe account. Availability may vary by country.

If the issue continues after checking these settings, disconnect and reconnect Stripe.

Contacts FAQs

Contacts help you keep track of people you schedule meetings with. You can use Contacts to view meeting history, see basic details, and schedule follow-up meetings.

When someone books a meeting with you, Calendly creates a contact using the name and email they enter during scheduling.

If you’ve deleted a contact, Calendly stops auto-creating that contact in your system. If they schedule with you again in the future, you can manually create a new contact for them.

Yes. You can manually create a contact even if that person has not booked a meeting with you yet.

A contact record includes details like name, email address, and meeting history. Some details come from bookings, and others can be added or updated by you.

You can open a contact to see their past and upcoming meetings. This helps you review previous meetings before scheduling again.

You can edit a contact from the Contacts page or from the Contact details view. Any updates you make are saved to that contact.

You can delete a contact from your Contacts list. This removes the contact from view, but it does not delete past meetings from your account.

When you delete a contact, Calendly stops auto-creating that contact in your system. If they schedule with you again in the future, you can manually create a new contact for them.

Saved contact lists let you save filtered views of your contacts. This helps you quickly return to the same group of contacts later.

You can hover over a contact’s name to open a quick view card. From the card, you can book a meeting, share your availability, or send an email without opening the full contact page.

When a contact books another meeting, the new meeting is added to their contact record.

Contact import is currently available to select users only. If you have access, you can import contacts via CSV file or by connecting a form like Typeform to automatically capture submissions. For detailed instructions, visit our import and export contacts guide.

If you don’t have access yet, Calendly automatically creates contacts when someone books with you. You can also manually create contacts in your account.

Contacts overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans #### Managing relationships with Contacts

Calendly’s Contacts feature helps you better manage and prepare for meetings with your most important business relationships. You can track key contact details, prepare for upcoming meetings, review meeting history, and schedule follow-ups all in one place.

Contacts make it easier to:

  • Show up prepared: View contact and meeting details — like invitee info and past meetings — all in one place.
  • Schedule follow-ups fast: Book a new meeting right from a contact’s profile or share your availability.
  • Keep details current: Calendly updates each contact’s profile when you schedule, so you always have the latest info.
  • Keep in touch fast: (Paid plans) Email your contacts directly with or without sending them a booking link.
  • Follow up on missed opportunities: (Limited Availability) Calendly automatically identifies contacts who received your scheduling link but haven’t booked yet, making it easy to send personalized follow-ups.

Quick view with hover cards

When you hover over a contact’s name, a small card appears with their email, phone number, LinkedIn, and time zone. From the card, you can also book a meeting, share availability, or send an email. View details faster and take action at a glance. #### Setting up contacts

Ready to set up contacts? These Help Center articles walk you through the steps.

  • How to create a contact
  • How to manage a contact
  • How to book meetings in real time
  • How to share availability with Gmail or Outlook in Calendly
