To learn more about our privacy policy and how Calendly for Slack uses your app data, visit the Permissions page.

Calendly + Zapier

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Zapier connects Calendly to hundreds of apps—like Google Sheets, Redtail CRM, and RingCentral—without any coding. Use it to automate actions after meetings are scheduled, contacts are updated, or Notetaker activity occurs.

For example, you can:

  • Send Calendly contacts to your CRM automatically.
  • Trigger a Slack message when someone books time with you.
  • Send Notetaker meeting recaps to your CRM automatically.
  • Build workflows based on meeting activity, contacts, or Notetaker updates.

Explore Zapier’s Calendly integrations or get inspired by our automation ideas. #### Before you begin

Make sure you have:

  • A Calendly Standard plan or higher.
  • A Zapier account (free or paid).
  • Admin or owner access if using group or organization triggers.

Use Zapier when the app you need doesn’t offer a direct Calendly integration. To check for available apps in Calendly, go to Integrations & apps. #### How it works

Zapier uses triggers and actions to automate workflows when something happens in Calendly.

You can create zaps for:

  • Meetings and event activity
  • Contacts
  • Notetaker activity #### Available triggers

Event triggers

  • Invitee Created — Fires when someone books a meeting.
  • Invitee Canceled — Fires when a meeting is canceled.
  • Invitee No Show Created — Fires when a user is marked as a no-show.
  • New Routing Form Submission — Fires when a routing form is submitted.
  • Event Canceled — Fires when an event is canceled by the host or invitee.
  • Meeting Recap Created — Fires when a meeting recap becomes available.

Contact triggers

  • New Contact Created — Fires when a new contact is added to Calendly.
  • Contact Updated — Fires when a contact record changes.
  • Contact Deleted — Fires when a contact is deleted.

Contact triggers support contacts created from booking forms, manual entry, or Notetaker activity. #### Trigger scope

  • Scope: Organization; Applies to: All meetings in your organization
  • Scope: Group; Applies to: Meetings in a selected group
  • Scope: User; Applies to: Meetings booked with the specific user

Note

Only admins or owners can use group or organization triggers. “No show” triggers aren’t available for group scope. #### Connect Calendly to Zapier

Follow the steps in Zapier’s support article. #### Set up your first zap

Step 1 – Create test data

Before testing your zap, create sample activity in Calendly. Depending on your workflow you can:

  • Schedule a test meeting
  • Create or update a contact
  • Use Notetaker in a meeting

Zapier uses this data to test your zap setup.

Step 2 – Create your zap

  1. In Zapier, select Create a new Zap.
  2. Choose Calendly as the app.
  3. Select a trigger, such as:
  • Invitee Created
  • Invitee Canceled
  • New Contact Created
  • Contact Updated
  1. Select Sign in to connect Calendly.
  2. Choose your trigger scope: user or organization.
  3. Select Test trigger. Zapier will use the most recent matching activity.

Tip

You can view a sample Webhook Payload here. #### Use filters and paths (paid Zapier plans)

Filters

Continue the zap only when certain conditions are met:

  • If invitee is “John”
  • If event is “Coffee Chat”
  • If UTM source is “email”
  • If invitee answered “yes” or “maybe”
  • If contact timezone is “PST”
  • If company name matches a CRM account #### Paths

Create custom actions based on:

  • Invitee responses
  • Meeting details
  • Contact attributes
  • Notetaker activity #### Disconnect Zapier

You can disconnect Calendly from Zapier by going to your connected apps page in Zapier and deleting the connection. #### Troubleshooting

The Zapier integration is built and supported by Zapier.

If your zap isn’t working, try the following:

  1. Check your Zap History in Zapier.
  2. Confirm your Calendly connection is active.
  3. Verify that recent test activity matches your selected trigger.

For additional troubleshooting or feature requests, please contact Zapier support.

Calendly API overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly’s API connects your software systems with our scheduling platform. You can automate tasks, sync data, and improve scheduling.

This guide covers the basics to help you get started. Check out the Developer Portal and the Developer Community for advanced help. #### How the Calendly API works

API Request

All Calendly users can send a request to get information or complete a task using our API. You’ll include what kind of data or action you need in the request.

Each request is secured with a personal access token (PAT), which lets the API know what you’re allowed to do. Our reference pages in the portal explain how to format your request and include all the details you need. #### API Processing

When a request is sent, our servers collect data, process calculations, or complete tasks based on your input. The server then sends a response that matches your request.

Request example: [Image: 26628689296919] #### Response

Once your request is processed, a response is sent to you. It will either include the data you asked for or confirm that the action was completed. All responses follow standard API formats.

Response example: [Image: 26628689299735] #### Error Handling

If an error happens, it’s handled with preset messages and codes. These help with troubleshooting or when you need support from the Calendly team.

Error example: [Image: 26628627756823]

Webhooks

Info

Available on the Professional, Standard, Teams, and Enterprise plans

Webhooks provide real-time updates to your systems when events occur in Calendly. Once set up, Calendly will notify you instantly if a meeting is scheduled, rescheduled, or canceled. This lets you automate tasks or trigger actions based on these updates. For more details, review our article on webhooks. #### API access by subscription plan

Developers can make GET and POST requests to API endpoints on behalf of a Calendly user on any subscription plan, including the Basic plan.

However, certain endpoints are available only to the Enterprise plan:

  • List activity entry logs
  • Delete invitee data
  • Delete scheduled event data

For webhooks and Scheduling API endpoints, the Calendly user must have a paid subscription on the Professional, Standard, Teams, or Enterprise plan. Explore each plan’s features on our pricing page. #### User vs admin/owner scopes

When generating tokens to authenticate Calendly’s API, the level of access depends on the user’s role. The scope of available data depends on whether the token is generated by a user or an admin/owner:

  • User role: A token generated by a user only allows access to data linked to that specific user. This includes webhooks that trigger for events like scheduled or canceled meetings related to the individual user.
  • Admin/Owner role: Tokens generated by an admin or owner provide broader access. These tokens allow API calls to manage data across the entire organization or within groups. #### Create a personal access token

Verify that you are generating the token from the correct account (user or admin/owner) to set the appropriate scope of access.

  1. Visit your Integrations page and select API and webhooks.
  2. Select Get a token now.
  3. Under Choose a name for this token, add a name.
  4. Select Create token.
  5. You’ll be prompted to enter an authentication code. Check your email for the code, then enter it to complete the verification.
  6. Once the personal access token is generated, select Copy token.

After you generate your personal access token, check out our guide on API capabilities and creating integrations in our Getting Started Guide on the Developer Portal.

Note

Keep your personal access tokens private and secure, just like a password. #### Security and compliance

The security of your integration is our top priority. Our API adheres to the best practices for security and data compliance, ensuring that your information stays safe. For more details, see our Calendly Platform Security and Compliance article.

Through the API, you can make manage organization users by:

  • Inviting users to join your organization
  • Revoking invitations
  • Removing users from your organization

You can also integrate your app using OAuth 2.0 for secure authorization.

Connect Calendly to your AI tools

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

You can connect Calendly to AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT to manage scheduling directly from your conversation. The steps to connect may vary depending on the AI tool.

MCP powers this connection behind the scenes, so your AI tool can take actions in your Calendly account.

Note

Want to learn more about how this works? Read our blog post. #### What you can do

After connecting Calendly to your AI tools, you can take actions such as:

  • Find open time or view busy slots
  • Book or cancel meetings
  • Create single-use links
  • Update availability settings
  • Create or manage event types #### Subscription requirements

You do not need a paid Calendly plan to connect Calendly to your AI tools using MCP. However, availability of some actions may vary depending on your Calendly plan.

Calendly is available on all Claude and ChatGPT plans. #### Connect Calendly to Claude

Use the Calendly connector for Claude. These steps apply to Claude on the web and desktop.

  1. From the sidebar in Claude, select Customize.
  2. Select Connect your tools and search Calendly.
  3. Select Connect.
  4. In the Calendly window that opens, sign in if prompted.
  5. Select Approve to grant access.

You’ll be taken back to Claude once the connection is complete. #### Use Calendly in Claude

After connecting, enable Calendly in a chat to start using it.

  1. Start a new chat in Claude.
  2. Select + in the chat box.
  3. Select Connectors, then turn on Calendly.

You can now ask Claude about your schedule and take actions directly in the conversation. #### Connect Calendly to ChatGPT

Use the Calendly plugin for ChatGPT. These steps apply to ChatGPT on the web, desktop, and Codex.

  1. From the sidebar in ChatGPT, select Plugins.
  2. Search for and select Calendly.
  3. Select Connect.
  4. (Optional) Turn on Reference memories and chats to personalize responses using relevant conversations and memories.
  5. Select Sign in with Calendly.
  6. In the Calendly window that opens, sign in if prompted.
  7. Select Approve to grant access.

You’ll be taken back to ChatGPT once the connection is complete. #### Use Calendly in ChatGPT

After connecting, enable Calendly in a chat to start using it.

  1. Start a new chat in ChatGPT.
  2. Select + in the chat box.
  3. Select Calendly.

You can now ask ChatGPT about your schedule and take actions directly in the conversation. #### Connect Calendly to other AI tools

If your AI tool supports Model Context Protocol (MCP), you can connect it to Calendly using the MCP server URL: mcp.calendly.com

In your AI tool, look for an option to add an MCP server or custom connector, then paste this URL. Follow your AI tool’s instructions to complete setup. #### Example prompts

Try these prompts with your connected AI tool:

  • “List my event types.”
  • “Find open time next week for my 30-minute meeting.”
  • “Create a single-use link for my 1:1 meeting.”
  • “What is my scheduling link?”
  • “Book a 30-minute meeting with Sarah this Thursday at 2 PM.”
  • “Cancel my 2 PM meeting with Alex.”
  • “Remove Fridays as available days for my 30-minute meeting.”

You can also ask, “What can you help me with in Calendly?” to explore available actions.

For full technical details and a complete list of supported actions, see the Developer Integration Guide.

How to sync meeting data to Marketo

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

Calendly syncs meeting data to Marketo, updating lead records automatically and enabling triggers for Smart Lists, re-targeting, and new campaigns. To learn more about syncing meeting data to Marketo, check out this article. #### Before you begin

To sync Calendly event data to Marketo, you must meet the following requirements:

  • Marketo API user with read and write permissions.
  • Marketo account with no more than 8 custom activity types.
  • Syncing meeting data to Marketo is only available for organizations on our Teams and Enterprise plans. Check out our Pricing and plans page for more information.
  • Only organization owners and admins can enable syncing meeting data to Marketo from the Integrations page. #### Connect Calendly and Marketo
  1. Go to the Integrations page.
  2. Select the Marketo integration.
  3. Enter your Marketo credentials (Client ID, Client Secret, and Munchkin ID#).
  • Review this article if you need help finding them.
  1. Select Save.

When you’re ready to start syncing data to Marketo, turn on Syncing data.

[Image: 31322250832279] #### Custom Activities in Marketo

When Syncing data is enabled in Calendly, two Custom Activities are created in Marketo:

  • Calendly Submit Routing Form
  • Calendly Schedule Event

To view the activities:

  1. In Marketo, go to the Admin panel.
  2. Under Database Management, select Marketo Custom Activities.
  3. You’ll see the two Calendly activities listed in the sidebar. #### Lead matching in Marketo

When a Marketo form linked to Calendly is submitted or a Calendly event is scheduled, the data is sent to Marketo and logged as an activity under the lead. Calendly searches for the lead in Marketo using the provided email address.

  • If a match is found, the lead’s record is updated with the form submission and/or meeting.
  • If no match is found, Calendly does not create a new lead, and no activity is logged.

To view the data:

  1. In Marketo, go to the Database panel.
  2. Under System Smart Lists, select All People.
  3. From the People tab, select a person.
  4. Open the Person Actions menu and select View Person Details. [Image: 16031403791767]
  5. Go to the Activity Log tab to view Calendly activity. [Image: 16031403794839]

Syncing meeting data to Marketo FAQs

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

This article contains frequently asked questions related to syncing Calendly meeting data to Marketo. #### What field data is included in event details for each custom activity?

  1. Routing Form Name
  2. Submission URI
  3. Routing Form URL
  4. Routing Form UUID
  5. Route Result Type
  • Event Type, Custom Message, or External URL
  1. Route Result Value
  • (i.e. If Result Type is Event Type, the value will be Event Type Name)
  1. Event Name
  2. Invitee URI
  3. Event Type URL
  4. Event UUID
  5. UTM Parameters
  6. The date the event was booked
  7. The date the event will occur #### What can I do with this integration?

You can create Smart Lists, Campaigns, and Programs in Marketo using Calendly triggers for form submissions or event scheduling. Use activity fields to set filters or constraints in your criteria. #### Will Calendly create people/leads in Marketo when routing forms are submitted and/or events are scheduled?

No, Calendly will only update activity on people records if the email used in the routing form and/or the meeting matches a people record that already exists in your Marketo account. #### What makes this integration better than others?

If you’re syncing Calendly event data to Salesforce first and then to Marketo, it can take 7 minutes to an hour. With this integration, Calendly event data flows directly to Marketo instantly after a form submission or event scheduling, so your campaigns can run right away. #### Do I have to use routing to take advantage of this integration?

No, you can still take advantage of syncing meeting data to Marketo regardless of if you’re using Calendly routing. Because Calendly Submit Routing Form and Calendly Schedule Event are two separate activities, Calendly will send activity to Marketo any time one of these actions are taken. #### How does this impact API calls to Marketo?

Calendly makes two API calls for each activity. When a routing form is submitted, one call checks if the person exists, and the other logs the form submission. For event scheduling, one call checks the email used, and the other logs the scheduled event. #### How are Calendly Schedule Event activities logged when multiple people schedule the same group event?

Calendly treats each person scheduling a group event as an individual action, so activities are logged separately. If Person A and Person B book the same group event, one activity is logged for each person. #### How are Calendly Schedule Event activities logged when a person schedules a Collective event with multiple Calendly hosts?

A single activity will be logged and the event details will include the name of the Collective event and the host will be the name of the Calendly user’s whose calendar was used to send the invitation.

Webhooks overview

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Calendly supports webhooks through our open API, allowing you to receive real-time updates when key events occur in your account. Use the v2 API to send event data to a specified URL when someone schedules or cancels a meeting, or submits a routing form.

For example, you can:

  • Trigger actions when a new meeting is booked

  • Update systems when an event is canceled

  • Capture data when someone submits a routing form (even if no event is booked) #### Before you begin

  • You’ll need access to either a personal access token or an OAuth application for authentication.

  • Make sure your endpoint is ready to receive and process webhook data.

  • View the Calendly API Use Cases for more ideas and examples. #### Webhook event types

Calendly supports the following webhook subscriptions:

  • Invitee Created Events — when a new event is scheduled
  • Invitee Canceled Events — when an existing event is canceled
  • Routing Form Submissions — when someone submits a routing form (with or without booking) #### Create a webhook

Follow the steps shown in our Developer Portal.

Once you create a webhook subscription, Calendly sends event data to the endpoint you specify when new activity occurs.

To test your webhook, trigger a new event (such as a booking, cancellation, or reschedule). Webhooks are not triggered by past events.

View sample data in our Webhook Payload documentation.Delete a webhook

To remove a webhook, visit our Delete Webhook Subscription guide. #### Best practices

For developers:

  • Use secure, HTTPS URLs for your webhook endpoints.
  • Validate incoming webhook signatures for added security.
  • Handle retries and avoid duplicate processing by checking event IDs.

For admins:

  • Monitor who has created webhook subscriptions.
  • If a user who created webhooks is removed from your organization, their webhooks remain active until manually deleted.

Plans & billing

Billing overview

Available to Owners and Admins on all plans.View plans

Adjust seats, change plans, and view subscription details from the Billing page in the Admin Center with this quick guide to Calendly billing. #### What happens after your trial

Note

New Calendly users start with a free two-week trial of the Teams plan. After that, you’ll move to the Free plan automatically.

No action is needed to move from the Teams trial to a free plan.

Once the trial ends, paid features like adding users or creating Workflows will be turned off.

To keep using those features, you can upgrade your plan anytime. Or, you can stick with the Free plan—no charge.

Want to delete your account and remove all your data? Follow these steps. #### Billing words to know

  • Organization: Your Calendly account. If you’re on the Free plan, it’s just you. If you invite others, they become part of your organization.

  • Seat: Also called a license. It represents one spot for a person in your organization. You’re billed for the number of seats, whether they’re filled or not.

  • Example: If you have 10 seats and 6 users, 4 seats are still available.

  • User: Someone who joins your organization and takes a seat. Users can schedule events, create links, and have different roles.

  • Upgrade: Move to a higher plan (e.g., from Free to Teams).

  • Downgrade: Move to a lower plan (e.g., from Teams to Free). #### How you’re charged

Calendly offers monthly and yearly plans. Your plan renews at the end of each billing cycle. You can change your plan or seat count anytime.

  • Upgrades and added seats take effect right away.
  • Downgrades and removed seats start at the end of your current billing cycle.

If you’re on a Teams annual plan, you’ll get a discount when you have over 30 seats. You can add seats or upgrade your plan from the Billing page. A clear cost breakdown will appear before you confirm changes.

Need help with invoice billing? Reach out to your Customer Success Manager or get in touch with our billing team by contacting support. #### Seat Charges

You pay for every seat, even if it’s not filled.

  • Example: If you have 5 seats and only 4 users, you’ll still pay for 5.

Want to manage seats and users? Check out this article. #### Joining an organization

When you accept an invitation to join an organization, your account becomes part of that organization and is managed by its admins.

If you have an existing paid subscription, it will be canceled when you join.

If the organization is on a trial, you may lose access to some paid features when the trial ends.

Before joining, you’ll see information about the organization and confirm to continue. #### Billing resources

If the error continues, wait a few minutes and try again later. Temporary billing errors usually resolve on their own.

Calendly and the RBI e-mandate

Available to Owners and Admins on all plans.View plans #### What is the RBI e-mandate?

On October 1, 2021, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced an e-mandate for recurring payments using India-based bank cards. To stay compliant, Calendly has updated its billing process for customers in India. #### Who is affected

Customers with a billing address in India are affected by this change. #### What Calendly is doing

Each billing cycle, Calendly will email you an e-mandate compliant payment link. You’ll need to confirm your payment manually to keep your subscription active. You’ll have 10 days to complete the payment. #### What this means for existing customers

Each billing period, you’ll receive an email titled “Important your invoice is due for payment.” Click Pay Now to open the payment portal and complete your transaction.

Note

Be sure to pay within 10 days to avoid account cancellation.

If your payment fails or you need to update your plan or seat count, contact our support team. #### What this means for new customers

If your card payment fails, contact our support team. We’ll guide you through authorization to complete your subscription.

Choose the right Calendly plan

Available to Owners and Admins on all plans.View plans

Calendly offers four plans to fit different scheduling needs:

  • Free — Basic tools for individuals
  • Standard — Advanced scheduling for individuals and small teams
  • Teams — Team scheduling, lead routing, and admin controls
  • Enterprise — Security, compliance, and dedicated support for large organizations

Each Calendly plan builds on the one before it: the Standard plan includes Free features, the Teams plan includes Standard features, and the Enterprise plan includes Teams features. Visit our pricing page to compare all features. #### What’s included in the Free plan?

The Free plan is best for individuals with simple scheduling needs. With the Free plan, you can:

  • Create one event type and schedule unlimited meetings
  • Connect one calendar and use basic integrations
  • Customize your booking page
  • Send confirmation emails
  • Embed your calendar on your website
  • Use the mobile app and browser extension

Choose the Free plan if you only need to schedule one type of meeting and don’t require integrations beyond your calendar. #### What’s included in the Standard plan?

The Standard plan is best for individuals or small teams who need advanced scheduling options. With the Standard plan, you can:

  • Create unlimited event types
  • Connect up to six calendars to be checked for conflicts
  • Use integrations like HubSpot, PayPal, and Stripe
  • Offer group (one host : many invitees) and collective (many hosts : one invitee) events
  • Automate reminders and follow-ups with Workflows
  • Customize your emails, booking page, and website embed
  • Get 24/7 live chat support

Choose the Standard plan if you need multiple event types, calendar integrations, or workflow automation but don’t yet need team-level lead routing or admin controls. #### What’s included in the Teams plan?

The Teams plan is built for teams or individuals who want powerful automation, lead routing, and admin controls. With the Teams plan, you can:

  • Sync meeting data to Salesforce
  • Use round robin scheduling — automatically distribute meetings across team members
  • Route leads with Calendly, Marketo, Pardot, or HubSpot forms
  • Match known leads to the right rep using HubSpot lookup
  • Manage events and permissions with admin tools
  • Add Single Sign-On (SSO) as an optional add-on
  • Get 24/7 live chat support

Choose the Teams plan if you or your team need to route leads, distribute meetings across reps, or manage scheduling at the team level. #### Teams plan tiered pricing (annual plans)

The Teams plan offers tiered pricing on annual subscriptions: as your team grows beyond 30 seats, the average price per seat automatically goes down. The first 30 seats remain at the same price.

  • Seat number: 31-50; Price per seat/month (billed annually): $14.50
  • Seat number: 51-100; Price per seat/month (billed annually): $14.00
  • Seat number: 101-200; Price per seat/month (billed annually): $13.50
  • Seat number: 201-300; Price per seat/month (billed annually): $13.00
  • Seat number: 301+; Price per seat/month (billed annually): $12.00

For example, if your team has 40 seats: seats 1–30 cost $16 each per month, and seats 31–40 cost $14.50 each per month.

You can add seats and view your total cost anytime from your Calendly Billing page. Discounts apply automatically. #### What’s included in the Enterprise plan?

The Enterprise plan is best for large organizations with advanced security, compliance, and support needs. With the Enterprise plan, you can:

  • Use Single Sign-On (SSO) and advanced user provisioning — automatic user account creation and management through your identity provider
  • Claim your domain and manage all users in one account
  • Access the full Salesforce routing suite
  • Stay compliant with an audit log and data deletion API
  • Get priority support, onboarding, and implementation help
  • Connect to Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Automate

Choose the Enterprise plan if your organization requires SSO, audit logging, dedicated implementation support, or the full Salesforce routing suite.

Profile settings

Account settings overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Your Calendly account settings let you control personal preferences like your profile, login, calendar connections, and communication settings. These options help you customize your scheduling experience and stay organized.

For example, you can:

  • Upload a photo and set a welcome message for your scheduling page
  • Adjust your time zone, date, and time format
  • Connect your calendar to avoid double-booking
  • Set branding and communication preferences #### Before you begin

To access your account settings, log in to Calendly and select your photo or icon in the top-right corner. Then select Profile.

Only account owners and admins can manage settings that affect an entire organization. #### Profile settings

In the Profile tab, you can edit:

  • Profile picture – Upload or update your profile picture

  • Name – Set the name shown on your Calendly page and in email invites

  • Welcome Message – Add a message to your scheduling page (265-character limit)

  • Language – Choose a language for your Calendly view (English, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese [Brazil])

  • Note: This doesn’t change the language for event types.

  • Date Format – Choose MM/DD/YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY

  • Time Format – Choose 12-hour (am/pm) or 24-hour

  • Country – Set your location

  • Time Zone – Choose your default time zone #### Branding

In the Branding section, you can:

  • Upload a logo – Add a logo to your personal scheduling pages

  • Apply branding to others – Owners and admins can apply the logo across all users in their organization

  • Disable Calendly branding – Owners and admins can disable the “Powered by Calendly” banner on scheduling pages for themselves or their organization #### My link

Customize how your scheduling link appears and is shared with invitees. You can do this from the event editor. #### Communication settings

Manage how you receive notifications and which phone numbers are used in SMS Workflows.

  • Phone numbers for SMS – Add phone numbers for text messages from host Workflows

  • Note: Available on paid plans only

  • Email notifications – Choose whether to get an email when added to shared or managed event types #### Login preferences

Update how you log in and which email address is linked to your Calendly account.

Control which cookies Calendly can use on your account. #### Calendar settings

Connecting a calendar helps you avoid scheduling conflicts. Calendly blocks out times you’re busy and adds all scheduled events to your calendar.

Calendar settings aren’t in your Account settings. You’ll find them on the Availability page. Learn how to connect and manage your calendar.

How to add a phone number to your account

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Using Workflows, you can send text messages to yourself as the meeting host. These messages help you stay up to date on your meetings and receive reminders. To set up those host text messages, add and verify your phone number. #### Add a phone number

  1. Select your profile picture in the top-right corner and choose All settings.
  2. Go to the Communication settings page.
  3. Enter your phone number and select Send verification code.
  4. Check your phone for a text message with a numeric code.
  5. Enter the verification code into the boxes.

After the code is confirmed, the page will refresh with your phone number saved. You can now select it when creating a Workflow to send a text to yourself as the host.

If you have another phone number, select Add another number and repeat these steps. #### Remove a phone number

  1. Select your profile picture in the top-right corner and choose All settings.
  2. Go to the Communication settings page.
  3. Next to the phone number you want to remove, select the X.
  4. Confirm by selecting Yes, delete it.

How to delete your account

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Note

If you’re new to Calendly, you’ll start with a two-week trial of our Teams plan. At the end of your trial, your account will automatically switch to our Free plan. No action is needed to make this change. #### Options to cancel or downgrade your subscription

If you’re thinking about canceling your Calendly subscription, you have three options:

  1. Switch to a different plan: Choose a new subscription plan (for example, from Teams to Standard).
  • You’ll keep your current plan’s features until the billing cycle ends.
  • This action can be reversed anytime.
  1. Cancel your paid plan: At the end of your billing cycle, you’ll move to Calendly’s Free plan.
  • You won’t be billed again, but you can still schedule meetings.
  • This action can be reversed anytime.
  1. Delete your account: This will permanently remove your account and all associated data.
  • You won’t be billed again, but this action cannot be undone. #### Delete your Calendly account

Deleting your account removes all your information and access. Deleting your account is permanent and cannot be undone. If you may return in the future, consider downgrading to the Free plan instead. #### Steps to delete your account

  1. In Calendly, go to Account > Account Settings.
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the Profile page.
  3. Select Delete Account.
  4. Choose one of these options:
  • Transfer ownership and delete my account: If you’re an owner, you’ll assign another user as the team owner before deleting your account.
  • Keep my account and leave organization: If you’re in an organization, you’ll keep your account, but leave the team.
  • Delete my account and disband the organization: If you’re an owner, you’ll delete your account and close the organization.
  1. Check your email for a verification code. Enter it when prompted.
  2. (Optional for owners) If you chose to transfer ownership or leave the organization, pick the new owner.
  3. Choose a reason for deleting your account from the drop-down menu.
  4. Select Delete to finish.

Note

If you’re the organization owner and delete your account:

  • All booked meetings from your event types—even those scheduled by others in your team—may be removed from the Meetings page.
  • These events can’t be recovered in Calendly.
  • However, they may still appear on your connected calendar as “Canceled” events.

How Calendly works with existing routing tools

Available to all users on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

To get the most from Calendly Routing, match the rules you use in your current routing tools. This helps ensure that both Calendly and your existing tool assign the same person to a new lead.

Many companies use tools like LeanData, Distribution Engine, or Salesforce to route leads. Follow these best practices to connect Calendly with those tools and keep your lead process running smoothly.

Note: Need help setting up Calendly Routing? Learn how to set up routing forms. #### Before you begin

Make sure you’ve connected Calendly with Salesforce using our native integration. This connection sends Calendly data into Salesforce, which helps trigger the right flows and updates.

Once set up, you can take these actions: #### Create a routing exclusion

If your leads come from different sources and go through an existing tool, but you want Calendly to take over routing, you’ll need to exclude those leads from your old tool.

By default, Calendly sends meeting info to Salesforce and creates a 0 record. This triggers a Salesforce flow called 1, which marks the lead or event with an attribute called 2. Tip: Update your routing rules to skip leads where 0 is present. #### Exclude already-assigned leads

Most routing tools won’t act on leads that are already assigned. When someone books a meeting through Calendly, our Salesforce integration automatically assigns the lead to the person they booked with.

This means your routing tool can skip the lead, since it already knows who to assign it to. #### Add a wait step

To avoid issues, insert a short delay before your routing tool runs. This gives Calendly enough time to update the lead’s info and assignment in Salesforce.

Steps to add a wait:

  1. Choose a wait time — 5 to 10 minutes usually works well.
  2. Add the wait to your Salesforce flow before the routing rules run.
  3. Test the setup to make sure the wait and exclusions work as expected. #### Final tips

Following these steps helps you connect Calendly to your routing tool without breaking your lead flow. You’ll keep your assignments accurate and your systems in sync.

How to create a Routing Form

Available to Owners and Admins on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

With Routing Forms, you can direct visitors to specific people or destinations based on factors like industry, company size, and interests.

Once your form and routing logic are built, Calendly gathers visitor details and automatically routes them to the right person or team based on the conditions set in your routing rules.

This article will cover instructions for creating a form from scratch. For integrating a form from another source, check out this article. #### Before you begin

  • Only owners, admins, and group admins can create Routing Forms.
  • From the Routing Forms page, all users can view and share Routing Forms.
  • For a user to edit a form, owners or admins must grant them editing permissions.

How to set up a Routing Form

Step 1 - Create your form

  1. From your Home page, select Routing from the navigation panel on the left-hand side.
  2. Select New routing form, then choose Create a new form.
  3. Enter a name for your form, and select Create form. #### Step 2 - Edit form settings and add questions

In your form, you can choose to include a headline and/or a description. You can also customize the text on the submission button.

  1. To add a question, select Add a question and choose your preferred format.
  2. Complete the question settings, then select Save.
  3. Continue adding form questions, as needed.
  4. When you’re finished, select Next. #### Step 3 - Set up routing logic

Create a route

  1. From the Routing logic tab, select Create.
  2. Choose Use form answers to use answers from your Calendly form.
  • For other options, review these articles on Salesforce lookup and HubSpot lookup.
  1. Fill out the settings for your condition by selecting a question, qualifier, and answer.
  • To add another qualifier and answer for a condition, choose or or and.
  1. To include more questions, select Add another question.
  2. Once your conditions are complete, select a Destination from the list:
  • Event Type: Route qualified visitors to an event type.
  • Custom message: Route disqualified visitors to a message.
  • External URL: Route visitors to another page.
  1. When you’re finished, select Save.

Fallback route

  • Your form includes a fallback route that applies to visitors whose responses don’t match any of the existing routes.

  • By default, this route displays a custom message. To edit the message or change the destination, select the route information. #### Step 4 - Preview and publish your form

  • We recommend previewing and testing your form before publishing by selecting Preview form.

  • In the popup window, you can test the routing logic by filling out and submitting the form. Your responses won’t be recorded during preview.

  • Once your form is ready, select Publish form. #### Step 5 - Share your form

After publishing the form, a popup window will display the following sharing options:

  • Share a link: Copy the link to share in a message.
  • Add to website: Embed the form directly on your website.

Note

Deleted routing logic cannot be recovered or restored.

What’s next?

Now that you’ve learned how to create Routing Forms, explore more ways to manage and utilize them with these resources:

  • How to manage a Routing Form: Learn how to edit permissions, view responses, and export results to manage your Routing Forms.
  • Routing Forms best practices: Discover best practices when creating your Routing Forms.
  • Routing Form analytics: Understand how to track and analyze Routing Form data to gain insights.

How to manage Routing Forms

Available to Owners and Admins on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

This article covers how to manage Routing Forms by editing permissions, viewing responses, and exporting results to stay on top of important form data. #### Editing Routing Form permissions

  1. Navigate to your Routing page and open the form you want to edit.

  2. At the bottom of the page, select Edit permissions.

  3. Enter the name or email of the user you want to add.

  4. Once you’ve added those users, select Apply to save your changes. #### Viewing Routing Form responses

  5. Open your Routing page.

  6. Locate your form, and select the three dots next to it.

  7. Select Responses.

Alternatively, you can access the Responses tab inside the form.

You’ll be able to view the response date, destination result, questions, and answers. You can also use filters, such as result type, event type, and date range to narrow down the responses. #### Exporting Routing Form responses

Once your Routing Form is live and has collected responses, you can export the results as a CSV file.

  1. Open your Routing page.
  2. Locate your form, and select the three dots next to it.
  3. Select Export results.

Alternatively, you can export responses from the Responses tab inside the form.

Note

Exporting a large number of responses may show a “Queued” message, and the results can take up to 24 hours to be delivered by email.

How to pre-populate invitee answers in routing forms

Available to Owners and Admins on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Improve your invitees’ experience by using Calendly routing forms to pre-fill info like name and company, saving them time and personalizing the process.

Routing also helps reduce mistakes and ensures invitees finish the form quickly. Overall, pre-filled forms make the scheduling experience faster and more enjoyable for everyone. #### Pre-populating Calendly routing forms

  1. Go to the Routing page.
  2. Find the form you want to share, then select Share.
  3. Select Copy link.
  4. Paste the link into an email, text message, or text editor.
  5. At the end of the link, add a “?” to start the section where you’ll add answers.
  6. Add a question number (“a1”, “a2”, etc.) followed by an “=”, and then the answer.
  • For example, to pre-fill the invitee’s name as the first question: “…/yourform?a1=InviteeName”
  1. Use “%20” to add space between words.
  • Example: “a1=John%20Smith”
  1. To include more answers, type “&”, followed by the next question and answer.

  • Example: “a1=John&a2=English” #### Routing form URL syntax

  • Term: a1, a2, a3; Use: Refers to specific question numbers on your routing form

  • Term: autofill=true; Use: Add to the end of the URL to auto-submit the form and route the invitee based on their answers

All answers are case sensitive. Make sure your URL answers match the exact text in your routing form. #### Example: Full pre-filled routing form

Pre-filled URL:

01

This URL auto-fills the form with:

  • a1 = Susan Smith
  • a2 = School
  • a3 = 9 or less
  • a4 = Chemistry

How to prevent scheduling with non-business or unwanted email domains

Available to Owners and Admins on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

This article walks you through how to use Routing Forms to let you control who can book time with your team by qualifying invitees before they reach a scheduling page. You can use routing logic to block personal or unwanted email domains (like Gmail or Yahoo) and ensure only qualified leads can schedule. #### Prevent scheduling with non-business or unwanted email domains

To block personal email addresses like Gmail or Yahoo, set up routing logic that screens for business domains:

  1. Go to the Routing Forms page.
  2. Select the form to edit or create a new one.
  3. Add an Email Address question and make it required.
  • Label it “Business Email” if helpful.
  1. From the Logic tab, select + Create.
  2. In IF, select your Business Email question.
  3. In the next dropdown box, choose includes domain, then list domains to block (i.e. gmail.com, yahoo.com, outlook.com). Remember to include .com, .net, or .org.
  4. In THEN, select Custom message to show unqualified invitees a custom message. [Image: 26242243102231]
  5. Select Save.
  6. Drag the Business Email route at the top of your logic list. #### Customize your fallback page

Unqualified visitors will reach the fallback page with the default “Thank you for your interest” message. You can personalize the page, and add helpful content or a contact email to keep those visitors engaged.

How to set up routing from HubSpot forms

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

Connect your HubSpot forms to Calendly’s routing logic to send leads to the right booking page based on their form responses.

For example, you can:

  • Route clients using specific fields on your HubSpot forms.
  • Embed Calendly routing with your HubSpot forms on your website.

Note

Calendly currently supports HubSpot forms built on the legacy form editor, as well as the new form builder (including multi-step forms). #### Before you begin

  • You’ll need HubSpot admin privileges.
  • Only organization owners and admins can set up HubSpot routing integrations.
  • Owners and admins can grant edit access to specific users for individual forms.
  • Make sure your HubSpot CRM is connected. Follow the steps in Calendly + HubSpot. #### Connect a HubSpot form to routing
  1. In Calendly, go to Routing.
  2. Select + New Routing form.
  3. Choose Import an existing form.
  4. Select Connect to link a HubSpot form.
  5. Sign in with your HubSpot credentials (skip if already connected):
  • Enter your Username and Password.
  • Select Log in.
  • Enter the verification code sent to your email.
  • Select Verify.
  1. Choose the HubSpot form you want to import.
  2. Calendly creates a “mirror form” and maps it to your original HubSpot form.
  3. In Form Preview, build your routing logic using radio buttons, dropdown fields, or the email domain.

For help building routing logic, see Getting started with Routing Forms.

Note: Routes can only be built off of responses to radio button and dropdown questions, as well as the email domain for an email field. #### Share your embedded form

  1. In Calendly, go to Routing.
  2. Next to your form, select Share.
  3. Customize your booking page (colors, visibility of event details, cookie banner).
  4. Select Copy code in the form panel.
  5. Paste the copied code after your HubSpot form code on your website.

When someone completes your HubSpot form, they’ll be automatically redirected to the correct Calendly booking page.

How to set up routing from Pardot forms

How to set up routing with HubSpot lookup

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

This article explains how to set up routing with HubSpot lookup in Calendly.

You can connect forms to your Calendly event types in two ways:

  • Calendly’s native routing logic: Used fixed answers for basic routing. Learn more in How to create a Routing Form.
  • HubSpot lookup with Calendly routing: Use data in HubSpot for more advanced routing.

HubSpot lookup lets you:

  • Route by Contacts or Company objects in HubSpot.
  • Use standard or custom fields like company size or contact stage.
  • Send people to Managed events, custom messages, or external links.

HubSpot lookup logic works with Calendly forms or imported forms like Marketo, HubSpot, or Pardot. #### Before you begin

Calendly Requirements

  • You must be an organization owner or admin.

  • Owners and admins can grant edit permission on each individual form to specific users.

  • HubSpot lookup requires Managed Events. #### HubSpot Requirements

  • You’ll need HubSpot free or paid plan.

  • You’ll need HubSpot admin privileges.

  • The Calendly user must exist in HubSpot and have the ability to own the HubSpot objects described above (Contact, Company).

  • Your Calendly and HubSpot emails must match. #### Managed Events

Routing with HubSpot lookup uses Managed Events. This allows you to apply a single event template across your organization for a consistent scheduling experience. This setup removes the need to create multiple routes for each team member, making the process easier.

For help setting up managed event types, see How to create and assign Managed Events. #### Adding HubSpot lookup logic to a routing form

Step 1 – Set up your routing form

You have two options when setting up your routing form:

  • Creating a Calendly routing form
  • Importing a HubSpot, Marketo, or Pardot form.

For more information on setting up your routing form, check out these articles:

  • How to set up routing forms - Set up routing from an existing HubSpot form, - Set up routing from an existing Marketo form - Set up routing from an existing Pardot form

Step 2 – Configure your routing logic

  1. Navigate to the Logic tab of your Routing form.
  2. Select + Create.
  3. Configure your routing logic.
  • For routing with HubSpot lookup, select Use HubSpot lookup. Since each HubSpot setup is different, we recommend the following configuration for beginners.
  1. Choose your HubSpot object: Contact
  2. WHEN: Contact record is found…
  • Find record by: Using full email address
  • Full email address matching field: Email
  1. Optional: Select + Add condition to add an IF condition for more nuanced and advanced routes.
  2. THEN: Go to a Managed Event
  • Ownership field: Contact owner
  • Managed Event: Select the Managed Event of your choice.
  1. Select Save
  2. Select Publish form

For more information on how to embed your routing form, check out these resources:

  • How to embed a routing form - How to embed routing from Marketo forms, - How to embed routing from HubSpot forms - How to embed routing from Pardot forms

Frequently asked questions

Calendly can find an owner from Contacts and Companies.

Your Calendly login email must match your HubSpot account email. This allows Calendly to access your HubSpot data.

To route by Contact Owner or Company Owner:

  1. Add a condition like Contact Owner is {owner ID}
  2. Turn off Use ownership
  3. Select the owner’s Event Type

This routes meetings based on the owner in HubSpot.

In HubSpot:

  1. Select Settings
  2. Go to Data Management > Properties
  3. Search for Contact owner
  4. Open the property and copy the Internal value

Calendly matches the primary email domain in HubSpot to the contact or company to keep routing accurate.

Yes. Place the HubSpot ownership route first so Calendly checks CRM ownership before other routes.

A Managed Event lets all owners share one Event Type. This avoids creating a route for each team member.

Yes. Admins control Managed Events to keep the meeting experience consistent.

Yes. Use a neutral title and description that work for any account, such as: Account check-in: Meet to touch base and answer questions.

How to set up routing with Salesforce lookup

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

This article provides instructions on how to set up routing with Salesforce (SFDC) lookup. #### Before you begin

Calendly Requirements

  • Only organization owners and admins can establish a SFDC form integration.
  • Owners and admins can grant edit permission on each individual form to specific users.

Salesforce Requirements

  • You’ll need Salesforce Enterprise or higher edition.

  • You’ll need Salesforce admin privileges.

  • The Calendly user:

  • Needs to exist in Salesforce

  • Be able to own the SFDC objects described above (Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity).

  • Calendly matches user by email. To match correctly, make sure each user’s email in Salesforce matches their Calendly email. #### Choose your method

When connecting forms to event types in Calendly, you have two options:

  1. Calendly’s Native Routing Logic: Use fixed answers for simple routing. Learn more in Getting started with Routing Forms.
  2. Salesforce Lookup with Calendly Routing Logic: Use Salesforce data for more flexible routing.

  • Salesforce Objects:

  • Account: Route visitors based on their account owner and conditions like “account type.”

  • Contact: Route visitors by their contact owner.

  • Lead: Route visitors by their lead owner.

  • Opportunity: Route based on the opportunity owner, using fields like “stage” for detailed routing.

  • Filtering/Routing Criteria: Use standard or custom Salesforce fields, such as “stage” or “account type,” for routing conditions.

  • Destinations: Based on Salesforce data, direct leads or contacts to different Event Types, Custom Messages, or External URLs.

You can use Salesforce lookup with Calendly forms or other tools like Marketo, HubSpot, or Pardot. #### Add SFDC lookup logic to a routing form

Step 1 – Set up your routing form

You have two options when setting up your routing form:

  • Creating a Calendly routing form
  • Importing a HubSpot, Marketo, or Pardot form.

For more information on setting up your routing form, check out these articles:

  • How to set up routing forms - Set up routing from an existing HubSpot form, - Set up routing from an existing Marketo form - Set up routing from an existing Pardot form

Step 2 – Configure your routing logic

  1. Navigate to the Logic tab of your Routing form.
  2. Select + Create.
  3. Configure your routing logic.
  • For routing with SFDC lookup, select Use Salesforce lookup. While every SFDC instance is unique, we recommend users new to SFDC routing use this configuration when getting started:
  1. IF: SFDC Lead
  • Find record by: Using full email address
  • Full email address matching field: Email
  1. Ownership Field: Lead Owner
  2. GO TO: Select the preferred destination (i.e., Managed Event, Event Type, External URL, or Custom Message)
  3. Select Save
  4. Select Publish form

For more information on how to embed your routing form, check out these resources:

  • How to embed a routing form - How to embed routing from Marketo forms, - How to embed routing from HubSpot forms - How to embed routing from Pardot forms

Routing with Salesforce lookup examples

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

Use this guide to configure Salesforce (SFDC) lookups in Calendly routing forms.

For initial setup steps, see How to set up routing with Salesforce lookup. #### Route leads to their Salesforce owner

Send known visitors to their assigned rep.

  1. Go to Calendly Home > Routing.
  2. Select + New routing form.
  3. Choose Create a new form, name it, and add questions (e.g., First Name, Email).
  4. Go to Routing Logic > Add a Route.
  5. Set logic:
  • IF: SFDC Lead
  • Match: Full email address
  • Field: Email
  • Owner Field: Lead Owner
  • GO TO: Choose destination (e.g., Managed Event)
  1. Select Save, then Publish form. #### Add conditions for ownership routing

Route only if Opportunity is Open

  1. Make sure your form includes an Email address.
  2. In Routing Logic, select Create route.
  3. Choose Salesforce lookup > Opportunity.
  4. In WHEN, select a lookup field.
  5. In IF:
  • Field: Stage
  • Condition: is
  • Value: Open
  1. In THEN:
  • Toggle Ownership lookup on
  • Owner Field: Owner ID
  • Managed Event: Select event type

  1. Select Save. #### Route only if account is in a certain division

  2. In WHEN, use a field like Account Domain.

  3. In IF:

  • Field: Business Tags
  • Condition: is
  • Value: e.g., Education
  1. In THEN, toggle Ownership lookup on.
  • Owner Field: Owner ID
  • Managed Event: Select event type
  1. Select Save. #### Route to a specific AE or team

Send to an AE not listed as the owner

  1. In IF:
  • Field: Owner ID
  • Condition: is
  • Value: Salesforce User ID
  1. In THEN, keep Ownership lookup off.
  2. Choose a destination and event type (e.g., One-on-one).
  3. Select Save.

Note: For multiple SDR–AE pairs, create separate routes. #### Skip bot owners

Calendly skips bot owners and follows your fallback route (e.g., round robin). #### Route based on Salesforce fields

Route leads by score

Send leads with a score over 50 to a high-priority team.

  1. Use Salesforce lookup on the Lead object.
  2. In IF:
  • Field: Behavior Score
  • Condition: is greater than
  • Value: 50
  1. In THEN, keep Ownership lookup off.
  2. Route to Round Robin event.
  3. Select Save.

Note: Use “is less than” to send low-score leads to a message or URL. #### Route leads by Zip Code

Option 1: Use a Salesforce field

  1. In WHEN, select your object such as Account.
  2. In IF:
  • Select the Account field that holds the Zip Code (e.g., Billing Zip)
  • Zip is greater than 30000
  • AND Zip is less than 40000
  1. Route to event.
  2. Select Save.

Option 2: Use form response

  1. Add a Zip Code question to the form.
  2. In IF:
  • Zip is greater than 30000
  • AND Zip is less than 40000
  1. Route to event.
  2. Select Save. #### Route to different destinations

Route partners to a different site

  1. Use Salesforce lookup on Contact.
  2. In IF:
  • Field: Partnership Reason
  • Condition: is
  • Value: Active

  1. In THEN, send to an external URL (e.g., Partners page).

  2. Select Save. #### Route known customers to support

  3. Use Salesforce lookup on Account.

  4. In IF:

  • Field: Active Users
  • Condition: is not empty

  1. In THEN, route to support (e.g., Team event or external site).

  2. Select Save. #### Route to a CSM, not the account owner

  3. Lookup the Account.

  4. In THEN, enable Ownership lookup.

  • Owner Field: CSM
  • Managed Event: Choose event type
  1. Select Save.

Routing with Salesforce lookup FAQs

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

This article contains common questions and answers related to Calendly routing with Salesforce lookup. #### What types of records can I look up in Salesforce?

Calendly can look up owners for these Salesforce records:

  • Leads
  • Contacts
  • Accounts
  • Opportunities
  • Custom objects #### Can I do lookups on custom objects in Salesforce?

Yes, Calendly supports custom object lookups. #### Can I do lookups on custom fields in Salesforce?

Yes, you can look up any standard or custom field. #### How do I route leads to the right rep in email campaigns?

Use a Calendly routing form instead of a direct event link.

  • The form should collect the email address.
  • Add a Salesforce ownership route to the form.
  • When someone opens the link and enters their email, Calendly finds their rep and shows the rep’s booking page. #### Can I assign a lead to someone other than the usual record owner?

Yes. Use a custom field on the Account, Lead, Contact, or Opportunity object. For example: “Account Rep” or “CSM”. #### How are leads added to Salesforce from Calendly?

  • If a meeting is booked, Calendly adds the record to Salesforce.
  • If no meeting is booked, the lead can be added through a Marketo or Pardot integration. #### Does routing work with Salesforce Shield Platform Encryption?

It depends on the type of encryption:

Probabilistic encryption

  • Calendly routing does not work with this type.
  • Fields with this encryption can’t be used in WHERE, GROUP BY, or ORDER BY queries.
  • Learn more: General Shield Platform Encryption Considerations

Deterministic encryption

  • Routing can work, but only for exact, case-sensitive matches.
  • Example: You can match an email address, but not just the domain part.
  • LIKE and STARTS WITH queries are not supported.
  • Learn more: Considerations for Using Deterministic Encryption

Troubleshooting routing from HubSpot Forms

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

Having trouble with Calendly routing and HubSpot forms? This guide shows common issues and how to fix them. #### HubSpot form redirects to a “Thank you” page instead of the booking page

If your HubSpot form doesn’t take invitees to the Calendly page, check which type of form editor you’re using in HubSpot. #### Troubleshooting HubSpot forms and Wix

Calendly routing script doesn’t work on Wix

If nothing happens after pasting the routing script on your Wix site, check the following:

  1. Make sure you’re using the paid version of Wix. The free version doesn’t allow custom code outside an iframe.
  2. Paste the following code in the Custom Code/Body-start section in Settings:

html

<!-- Calendly inline widget begin --><link href="https://assets-staging.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.css" rel="stylesheet"><!-- Calendly inline widget end →

Invitees close the popup and don’t return to the form

If someone closes the Calendly popup before booking, you can redirect them back to a page of your choice.

  1. Add this redirect snippet to your page:

html

constcallback = (mutationList, observer) => {for (constmutationofmutationList) {if (mutation.type === 'childList') {mutation.removedNodes.forEach((removedNode) => {if (removedNode.className === 'calendly-overlay') {window.open('https://calendly.com', '_self')      }    })  }}};constobserver = newMutationObserver(callback);observer.observe(document.getElementsByTagName('body')[0], { childList:true });
  1. Replace the Calendly URL with your preferred redirect page.
  2. Find the line Calendly.Calendly.initHubSpotForm({ url: … }) and add this code:

html

<!-- Calendly routing form code begin --><linkhref="https://calendly.com/assets/external/widget.css"rel="stylesheet"><scriptsrc="https://calendly.com/assets/external/forms.js"type="text/javascript"async><scripttype="text/javascript">window.addEventListener('load', () => {Calendly.initHubSpotForm({ url:"..." })<Add the code snippet here> });<!-- Calendly routing form code end -->

Troubleshooting routing from Pardot forms

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

Having trouble importing your Pardot form into Calendly? This guide covers common issues and how to fix them. #### I’m not seeing any forms to import

If you’ve connected Pardot but don’t see any forms to import, here are a few possible reasons:

  • You’re using Pardot form handlers, not Pardot native forms.
  • The Salesforce user you connected isn’t a Pardot user.
  • You have a Pardot account, but your role doesn’t allow creating or editing form templates.
  • Your Pardot account isn’t hosted on a custom domain (for example, 0 is not a custom domain, but 1 is). #### I’m not seeing my form’s fields

You were able to select a form to import, but your form fields aren’t showing in Calendly.

This often happens if your Pardot domain is connected to Cloudflare.

To fix this:

  • Whitelist the Pardot domain in your Cloudflare settings.

Note: Cloudflare requires a higher-tier plan to enable domain whitelisting. #### I’m receiving a ‘403’ error in Chrome

Seeing a 403 error when importing a Pardot form into Calendly?

This usually means you’re using a demo Pardot form, which has limitations.

For more information, see this article on demo Pardot form limitations.

Troubleshooting when routing with Salesforce lookup

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

This article contains common troubleshooting steps related to Calendly’s routing with Salesforce (SFDC) lookup. #### My route is being skipped

Here are some common reasons why a route may be skipped:

  • There’s no owner for the full email address or domain submitted in the form.
  • There’s an owner, but they’re not a Calendly user.
  • The user exists in Calendly but isn’t assigned to the managed event type linked to the route.
  • The user is assigned to the managed event type, but their Salesforce email doesn’t match their Calendly email.

Other reasons include:

  • YourSalesforce account hit its API limit. Learn more about Salesforce API limits.

  • Salesforce timed out or returned an error during the routing process. #### I’m seeing duplicate events on my calendar

  • You may have multiple calendar connections in Salesforce.

  • Tools like Einstein Activity Capture or Lightening Sync may be creating duplicates. Visit these Salesforce articles for more info:

  • Einstein Activity Capture

  • Lightning Sync

  • You may have multiple flows that create events. #### I want to route by the Salesforce email field, but it’s not showing in the menu

If your field is missing from the dropdown, you may need to update your Salesforce field permissions.

  1. In Salesforce, select Contact from the Object Manager tab.

  2. Select Fields & Relationships in the sidebar menu.

  3. Select the specific field that is currently missing from the routing form drop-down menu in Calendly. (e.g. Email)

  4. Select Set Field-Level Security.

    [Image: 26357826283415]

  5. Scroll down to System Administrator.

  6. Make sure the profile associated with your connected Salesforce account has access/permissions to the field in question by checking the Visible check box.

  7. Select Save.

    [Image: 14846953106455]

  8. In Calendly, open your routing form.

  9. Refresh the page.

If the field doesn’t show:

  1. Go to the Salesforce integration page in Calendly.
  2. Disconnect and reconnect Salesforce.
  3. Go back to your Calendly routing form.
  4. The field should now appear in the drop-down menu.

Salesforce

Calendly + Salesforce

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

This article serves as a central hub for the Calendly + Salesforce integration. It’s designed to help you navigate and maximize the Calendly integration. Explore how to get started, customize Calendly’s Salesforce flow, and much more, transforming your approach to CRM. #### What you can do with Calendly + Salesforce

  • Create events – Automatically create events or tasks on Salesforce records when a meeting is scheduled.
  • Map to custom objects – Send booking information to Salesforce custom objects to help qualify leads faster.
  • Route by Salesforce ownership – Automatically look up, match, and schedule known leads and customers without manual reassignment.
  • Never leave Salesforce – Schedule meetings from Salesforce and view upcoming and past meetings in your activity records. #### Integrating Calendly with Salesforce

Calendly Salesforce package v2 post-install steps

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

Once you have installed the Calendly Salesforce package (version 2.3 or higher) from the Salesforce integrations page, we recommend taking the steps detailed in this article so that you can begin testing and customizing the integration behavior. #### Flow templates deactivated by default

Usability updates to our managed package (v2 or higher) now sets flow templates to be deactivated by default. This follows Salesforce’s best practice guidelines, allowing admins to intentionally apply flow updates instead of having them auto-applied. Therefore, we recommend creating copies of the deactivated default flow templates and activating the copies of the flow templates.

Note

With the update in version 2.5, we recommend keeping the original subflow templates (Get Event Attendee Template and Create Event Attendee Template) in the CreateEventTemplate active, and avoid creating a copy unless you’re making changes directly within the subflow itself.

However, if you do create a copy and make changes to these subflows, ensure you replace these modified subflows with the original versions within the CreateEventTemplate. #### Create a copy of a flow template

[Image: 10794981486999]

  1. From your Salesforce Flows list, select the flow template you wish to duplicate (i.e. MapCalendlyLinkTemplate).
  2. Select Save As in the top right-hand corner.
  3. Name the flow by creating a Flow Label.
  4. Select Save.
  5. Navigate back to the Salesforce Flows list
  6. Select the newly saved/created flow.
  7. Activate the flow by selecting Activate in the top-right hand corner.

Once a copy of the flow templates has been created and activated, we recommend creating a test booking in Calendly to verify the flow is functioning properly.
