Troubleshooting Salesforce integration

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

Having trouble syncing events between Calendly and Salesforce? Use this guide to fix common issues and get your integration working again. #### Events aren’t syncing to Salesforce

If no events are showing up in Salesforce, follow these steps: #### Step 1 – Check your integration status

  1. Open your Salesforce Integration Page in Calendly.
  2. Look at the Status:
  • If it says Broken, check your email for a Salesforce flow error message.
  • If it says Good, move to the next step. #### Step 2 – Turn on “Push New Events to Salesforce”

  1. Stay on the Salesforce Integration Page.

  2. Make sure Push New Events to Salesforce is switched on.

  3. If it’s off, turn it on and try booking a new event. #### Step 3 – Make sure your Salesforce flows are active

  4. In Salesforce, go to Setup > Flows.

  5. Switch the view to All Flows.

  6. Filter by Package Name = Calendly.

  7. Make sure these flows are active:

  • CreateEventTemplate
  • CancelEventTemplate
  • Get Event Attendee Template (v2.5+)
  • Create Event Attendee Template (v2.5+)

Using custom flows? Be sure to turn off the original ones and turn on your custom versions. #### Step 4 – Test with a booking

Book a test event using your team’s Salesforce training process. Then check if it syncs to Salesforce. #### Step 5 – Look for CalendlyAction records

  1. In Salesforce, open the CalendlyAction tab.
  2. Sort by Created Date (descending).
  3. Find a record that matches your test booking.
  • If you see it: The connection is working. You may need to fix your Salesforce flow.
  • If not: Go back and check your connection status. #### Some events aren’t syncing

If only certain events are missing, try this: #### Step 1 – See what you’re syncing

  1. Go to the Salesforce Integration Page.
  2. Check if Calendly is syncing:
  • Events from your entire org, or
  • Only from certain groups

If syncing by group, make sure the missing events are from users in those groups. #### Step 2 – Create a test event

  1. Book a new event for a user whose event is missing in Salesforce.
  2. Search for the test event in Salesforce.
  • If it shows up: Continue to the next step.
  • If not: Skip to Step 4. #### Step 3 – Check event assignment

Make sure the event is assigned to the right Salesforce user.

If it’s not, go to the next section: Events assigned to the wrong user. #### Step 4 – Check for flow errors

If you received a Salesforce flow error email, review the flow logic or your event type settings. #### Step 5 – Review entry conditions

If you’re using a custom flow:

  • Look under Object: CalendlyAction
  • Check the Entry Condition. If it’s not set to “None,” it could be blocking the event. #### Events are assigned to the wrong user

If events appear in Salesforce but are assigned to the wrong user: #### Step 1 – Make sure the event exists

First, confirm that the event is syncing. If not, go back to the Some events aren’t syncing section. #### Step 2 – Match the user’s email

  1. In Salesforce, go to Setup > Users.
  2. Check if the user’s email matches their Calendly email.
  • If not, update the Salesforce email and test again. #### Step 3 – Look for duplicates

Search Salesforce for other users with the same email address.

Duplicate users can cause incorrect assignments. If needed, update or remove the extra user, or adjust your flow logic.

You can also manually assign the event to the correct user in Salesforce. #### Integration won’t connect or install

Step 1 – Use the correct domain and user

Open an incognito browser window to avoid auto-login problems.

If your company uses a custom domain:

  1. On the login screen, select Use Custom Domain.
  2. Enter your domain and login info.

Getting an “Oops! Something went wrong” error?

This may mean Calendly is blocked. Ask your IT team to unblock the OAuth app. #### Step 2 – Update OAuth settings in Salesforce

  1. Go to Setup > OAuth and OpenID Connect Settings in Salesforce.
  2. Turn off PKCE Extension, then try again. #### Step 3 – Confirm your permissions

To connect Calendly to Salesforce, you need:

  • A Salesforce Enterprise edition or higher
  • Admin permissions #### Step 4 – Refresh the connection
  1. Open your Salesforce Integration Page in Calendly.
  2. Select Disconnect.
  3. Reconnect using the correct user credentials.

SAML SSO

How to configure Auth0 SAML SSO

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans #### Auth0 SAML SSO features

  • Identity Provider Initiated SSO (IdP-initiated)
  • Service Provider Initiated SSO (SP-initiated)

NOTE: Just-in-Time (JIT) user creation is not supported. You can provision users via SCIM on Calendly’s Enterprise plan. #### Before you begin

  • SAML SSO is included on Calendly’s Enterprise plan. To learn more, contact your Account Executive or Calendly Sales.
  • To configure SAML SSO, you must be a Calendly owner or admin.
  • You must use the same email address in Calendly and Auth0.
  • During setup, you’ll switch between Calendly and Auth0. It’s best to keep each platform open in a separate browser window. #### Configure Auth0 SAML SSO

Go to the Calendly single sign-on configuration page

From any Calendly page, select Account, Organization Settings, then Single sign-on. #### Create a Calendly application in Auth0

  1. In a new window, log in to Auth0.

  2. Select Applications.

  3. In the drop down menu, select Applications.

  4. Select Create Application.

  5. In the Name field, enter “Calendly”.

  6. At Choose application type, select Regular Web Applications.

  7. Select Create.

  8. Select Settings.

  9. Scroll to the bottom and select Advanced Settings.

  10. Select Grant Types.

  11. Deselect all selections. (Note: You won’t be using OAuth2, so none of the selections are needed for this Auth0 application.)

  12. Select Save Changes. #### Add Auth0 details to Calendly

  13. Scroll back to the top of the page and select Addons.

  14. Select SAML2 Web App.

  15. Copy the Issuer ID in Auth0 and paste it into the Entity ID field in Calendly.

  16. In Auth0, copy the Identity Provider Login URL and paste it into the Identity provider’s SAML HTTP Request URL field in Calendly.

  17. In Auth0, at Identity Provider Certificate, select Download Auth0 certificate.

  18. In Calendly, select Upload certificate. Locate and enter the certificate downloaded from Auth0.

  19. At Session duration, set the appropriate value for your organization’s security policies.

  20. Select Save & continue. #### Add Calendly details to Auth0

  21. In Auth0, select Settings.

  22. In Calendly, copy the ACS URL and paste it into the Application Callback URL field in Auth0.

  23. Copy the following JSON and paste it into the Settings field in Auth0:

    javascript

    { "audience": "{Audience URL}", "mappings": { "given_name": "firstName", "family_name": "lastName", "email": "email" }, "passthroughClaimsWithNoMapping": false, "mapUnknownClaimsAsIs": true, "signatureAlgorithm": "rsa-sha256", "digestAlgorithm": "sha256", "signResponse": true, "nameIdentifierProbes": [ "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress" ] }

    [Image: 4404102330263]

  24. In Calendly, copy the Audience URL.

  25. In Auth0, in the JSON in the Settings field, replace 0 with the Audience URL value you copied from Calendly in step 4.

  26. Select Enable. When you see the success message, close the modal. #### Create a rule in Auth0

  27. In Auth0, copy the Client ID and paste it somewhere safe for later use.

  28. In the lefthand sidebar, click Actions > Flows.

  29. Select the Login flow type. In the righthand sidebar, select + then Build Custom.

  30. In the dialog, enter “Calendly SAML” for the name.

  31. Select Create.

  32. Delete the existing code and copy and paste the code below into the editor.

  • javascript

    /** * Handler that will be called during the execution of a PostLogin flow. * * @param {Event} event - Details about the user and the context in which they are logging in. * @param {PostLoginAPI} api - Interface whose methods can be used to change the behavior of the login. */ exports.onExecutePostLogin = async (event, api) => { const {client, user} = event if (client.client_id !== '{Client ID}') { return } const name_parts = (user.name || '').split(' ', 3); const given_name = user.given_name || name_parts.at(0); const family_name = user.family_name || name_parts.at(-1); api.idToken.setCustomClaim(0, given_name); api.idToken.setCustomClaim(1, family_name); };
  1. Replace 0 with the Client ID copied in step 1.
  2. Select Save Draft, then Deploy.
  3. Select Back to Flow.
  4. In the righthand sidebar, click Custom.
  5. Drag and drop the Calendly SAML Action into the flow.
  6. Select Apply. #### Test the connection

Note: Before you test the connection, you must be logged in to Calendly and Auth0 with the same email address.

In Calendly, select Enable SSO for yourself, then select Test connection. If successful, you’ll see a confirmation.

[Image: 18192288642071] #### Enforce Auth0 SSO for your organization

Note: If your organization has any application restrictions for users, update those rules so the appropriate users can use Calendly.

In Calendly, select Enforce SAML SSO for my organization, then Apply.

[Image: 18192336470039]

Once SSO is enforced, all users will be logged out and need to use SAML SSO to log into Calendly. Only the organization owner can log in using their fallback (original) login method by selecting Log in using another method on the login page.

How to configure Duo SAML SSO

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans #### Duo SAML SSO features

  • Identity Provider Initiated Login
  • Service Provider Initiated Login

NOTE: Just-in-Time (JIT) user creation is not supported. You can provision users via SCIM on Calendly’s Enterprise plan. #### Before you begin

  • SSO is included on a Calendly enterprise plan.
  • To configure SAML SSO, you must be a Calendly owner or admin.
  • You must use the same email address in Calendly and Duo.
  • During setup, you’ll switch between Calendly and Duo. It’s best to keep each platform open in a separate browser window. #### Configure Duo SAML SSO

Go to the Calendly single sign-on configuration page

  1. In Calendly, go to Account, Organization Settings, then Single sign-on. #### Add Duo details to Calendly

  2. In a separate window, open Duo and go to Applications.

  3. Select Protect an Application.

  4. Search for Generic SAML Service Provider. For the row that has Single Sign-On in the Protection Type, select Protect.

  5. In Duo, copy Entity ID. Paste it into Entity ID in Calendly under Step 1: Enter your identity provider information.

  6. In Duo, copy Single Sign-On URL and paste into Identity provider’s SAML HTTP Request URL in Calendly.

  7. In Duo, select Download certificate. In Calendly, upload the downloaded certificate by selecting Upload certificate.

  8. In Calendly, set Session duration to the appropriate value for your organization’s security policies.

  9. In Calendly, select Save & continue.

  • Duo: Entity ID →; Calendly: Entity ID
  • Duo: Single Sign-On URL →; Calendly: Identity provider’s SAML HTTP Request URL
  • Duo: Download certificate →; Calendly: Upload certificate

Add Calendly details to Duo

  1. In Calendly under Step 2: Enable SSO for yourself, copy Audience URL and paste into Entity ID in Duo.
  2. In Calendly, copy ACS URL and paste into Assertion Consumer Service in Duo.
  3. In Calendly, copy Default Relay State into Default Relay State in Duo.
  • Calendly: Audience URL →; Duo: Entity ID
  • Calendly: ACS URL →; Duo: Assertion Consumer Service
  • Calendly: Default Relay State →; Duo: Default Relay State

Update attributes and settings in Duo

  1. In Duo, ensure NameID format is set to urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress.

  2. Ensure NameID attribute is set to 0.

  3. Ensure Signature algorithm is set to SHA256.

  4. For Signing options, ensure both Sign response and Sign assertion are checked.

  5. Under Map attributes, configure the following:

  6. 0 → email

  7. 0 → firstName

  8. 0 → lastName [Image: 4402754492951]

  9. Under Settings, update Name to Calendly.

  10. In Permitted groups, select the group you wish to have access to Calendly. You can also return here after testing the SAML connection.

  11. Select Save. #### Test the SAML connection

In Calendly under Step 2: Enable SSO for yourself, select Test connection. You will be redirected to the Identity Provider and then back to Calendly.

[Image: 18192260878487]

  • If successful, you’ll receive a success notification at the top of the page in Calendly.
  • If unsuccessful, you will land on an error page in Okta or receive an error notification in Calendly. Check your SAML setup, then try test the connection again. #### Enforce Duo SSO for your organization

When you enforce SAML SSO, all users will be logged out of their accounts. When they next log in to Calendly, they will be required to use Duo.

  1. In Duo, assign all Calendly users the app.
  2. In Calendly, select Enforce SAML SSO for my organization, then Apply.[Image: 18192213138839]

Once SSO is enforced, all users will be logged out and need to use SAML SSO to log into Calendly. Only the organization owner can log in using their fallback (original) login method by selecting Log in using another method on the login page.

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans #### Go to the Calendly SSO Configuration Page

  1. Go to the Admin Center.

  2. Select Login.

  20. To download the Base64 certificate, select the 3 dot menu and select Base64 certificate download. Select Save. [Image: 1500001343902]

  21. Copy the contents of the certificate and paste it into the X.509 certificate for SAML authentication field on Calendly’s SSO settings page.

  23. In Microsoft Entra ID, select the pencil icon within the Basic SAML Configuration box. [Image: 1500001343942]

  24. In Calendly, copy the Audience URL and paste it into the Identifier (Entity ID) field in Microsoft Entra ID.

  25. In Calendly, copy the ACS URL and paste it into the Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL) field in Microsoft Entra ID.

  26. In Calendly, copy the Default relay state and paste it into the Relay State field in Microsoft Entra ID.

  27. In Microsoft Entra ID, select Save.

  28. Select the pencil icon in the User Attributes & Claims box. [Image: 360102417393]

  29. Under Required claim select Unique User Identifier (Name ID).

  30. At Source attribute, search for user.mail and select.

  31. Select Save.

  32. Under Additional claims, delete all existing claims by selecting the 3-dot menu and Delete.

  33. Add an email claim

  • Select + Add new claim
  • Under Name, enter email.
  • At Source attribute, search for user.mail and select.
  • Select Save.
  1. Add a firstName claim
  • Select + Add new claim
  • Under Name, enter firstName.

  • Select Save.

  • Under Name, enter lastName.

  • Select Save.

[Image: 1500001406621] #### Assign your user to the Calendly application

  1. In Azure, return to the Enterprise Applications page.
  2. Select the application.
  3. Select 1. Assign users and groups.
  4. Select + Add user.
  5. Select Users.
  6. Search for your user, select them, and hit Select.
  7. Select Assign. #### Test connection

In Calendly, select Enable SSO for yourself.

[Image: 18192191647383]

Select Test connection.

Once you’ve verified that you can log in, assign your remaining Calendly users to the application in Azure before you enable and enforce SSO for all users. #### Enforce for your organization

In Calendly, select Enforce SAML SSO for my organization, then Apply.

[Image: 18192205258519]

Once SSO is enforced, all users will be logged out and need to use SAML SSO to log into Calendly. Only the organization owner can log in using their fallback (original) login method by selecting Log in using another method on the login page.

Note

If you are on our Teams plan and would like to add single sign-on (SSO) features to your Calendly account, you can do so from your billing page. The SSO add-on costs $3 per user, per month.

How to configure Okta SAML SSO

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

Single Sign-On (SSO) is a login method that lets users access Calendly using credentials managed by your company’s Identity Provider (IdP) — the service managing your company’s user accounts, such as Okta. SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) is the protocol Calendly uses to exchange authentication data with your IdP.

See also: SAML SSO overview #### Before you begin

You’ll need:

  • A Teams or Enterprise Calendly plan:

  • Teams plan users: Add the SSO feature from your Billing page for $3 USD per Calendly user, per month (billed as an add-on on top of your Teams plan).

  • Enterprise plan users: SSO is included

  • To be a Calendly Owner or Admin.

  • To use the same email address in both Calendly and Okta. #### Okta SAML SSO features

What’s supported:

  • Identity Provider Initiated SSO (IdP-initiated)

  • Login through Okta and open Calendly from the dashboard.

  • Requires a Default Relay State in Okta — a value that tells Okta where to redirect users after they authenticate (in this case, to Calendly).

  • Service Provider Initiated SSO (SP-initiated)

  • Users can log in via calendly.com and your identity provider will authenticate the user. Calendly is the Service Provider (SP) in this flow.

Not supported:

  • Just-in-Time (JIT) user creation — automatic account creation on first login — is not supported. Enterprise owners and admins can provision users with System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), a standard for automatically syncing user accounts between your IdP and Calendly. #### Configure Okta SAML SSO

Add Calendly as an Okta application

  1. Open the Okta admin dashboard.
  2. Select Applications > Add Application.
  3. Select Browse App Catalog.
  4. Search for the Calendly and select Add.
  5. Under General Settings, review:
  • Application Visibility - Check Do not display application icon to users to hide during setup. (You will need to change this after configuration to make the app visible to your users.)
  • Browser plugin auto-submit

  1. Select Next.

  2. Select SAML 2.0 under Sign On Methods.

  3. Select View Setup Instructions.

  4. Keep this tab open. #### Configure Okta SAML SSO on Calendly

  5. Open the Okta admin dashboard and select Applications, Calendly (or whatever you chose to name the Calendly application)

  6. Select the Sign On tab.

  7. Select View Setup Instructions.

  8. In a new tab, go to your Calendly home page.

  9. Open your Admin center.

  10. Select Login, then select Single Sign On.

  11. In Okta, copy the Identity Provider Single Sign-On URL.

  12. In Calendly, paste the URL into the Identity provider’s SAML HTTP Request URL field.

  13. In Okta, copy the Identity Provider Issuer.

  14. In Calendly, paste it into the Entity ID field — the unique identifier Calendly uses to recognize your Okta tenant.

  15. In Okta, download the X.509 Certificate in PEM text format. X.509 is the certificate standard used to verify the authenticity of SAML responses from Okta, and PEM (Privacy-Enhanced Mail) is the text encoding format of the certificate file.

  16. Upload the certificate into Calendly in the X.509 certificate for SAML authentication box.

  17. Set Session duration to the appropriate value for your organization’s security policies.

  18. In Calendly, select Save & continue. #### Update the Application SAML URLs within Okta

  19. From the Okta admin dashboard, select Applications, Calendly (or whatever you chose to name the Calendly application).

  20. Select the General tab.

  21. Scroll down to SAML Settings and select Edit.

  22. Scroll down and select Next.

  23. In Calendly, select Copy Audience URL.

  24. Go to Okta and paste it in the Audience URI (SP Entity ID) field — the value that identifies Calendly as the Service Provider to Okta.

  25. In Calendly, select Copy ACS URL.

  26. Go to Okta and paste it in the Single sign on URL field. The ACS URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL) is the Calendly endpoint that receives SAML responses from Okta.

  27. (Optional, but required for IdP-initiated SSO.) In Calendly, select Copy default relay state. In Okta, paste it in the Default Relay State field.

  28. In Okta, for Application username format select Email.

  29. Select Save. #### Test connection

  30. Under the Assignments tab in Okta, assign your Okta user the Calendly application by selecting Assign > Assign to People.

  31. Select the user to assign it to.

  32. If the user’s email is different from the one used to log in to Calendly, enter the correct email address in the User Name field.

  33. Select Save and Go Back.

  34. In Calendly, select Test Connection. If successful, you’ll see a confirmation and be able to proceed to the next step. #### Enforce for your organization

  35. In Okta, assign Calendly to the desired users. If you’re assigning many users, you can follow these instructions from Okta.

  36. In Calendly, select Enforce SAML SSO for my organization

Once SSO is enforced, all users will be logged out and need to use SSO to log into Calendly. Only the organization owner and admins can log in using their previous login method by selecting Log in using another method on the login page.

How to configure Ping Identity SAML SSO

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans #### Go to the Calendly SSO Configuration Page

  1. Go to the Admin Center.

  2. Select Login.

  3. Select Single sign-on. #### Add Calendly as a Ping Application

  4. Open your Ping Identity dashboard in a separate tab.

  5. Select CONNECTIONS.

  6. Select + Add Application.

  7. Select WEB APP. Then, in the SAML row, select Configure.

  8. Enter an Application Name (e.g. Calendly) and Description (e.g. online appointment scheduling software).

  9. Select Next.

  10. In ACS URLs, enter **example.com** (you’ll change this later).

  11. In ENTITY ID, enter example.com (you’ll change this later).

  12. Select Download Signing Certificate and select X509 PEM (.crt). [Image: 360100242394]

  13. Under SIGNING ALGORITHM, select RSA_SHA256.

  14. Under ASSERTION VALIDITY DURATION (IN SECONDS), enter 60.

  15. Select Save and Continue.

  16. Under PINGONE USER ATTRIBUTE, choose Email Address.

  17. Add an Email Address attribute

  18. Select +ADD ATTRIBUTE.

  19. Select PingOne Attribute.

  20. Under PINGONE USER ATTRIBUTE, select Email Address.

  21. Under APPLICATION ATTRIBUTE, enter email.

  22. Check the box for Required.

  23. Add a Given Name attribute

  24. Select +ADD ATTRIBUTE.

  25. Select PingOne Attribute.

  26. Under PINGONE USER ATTRIBUTE, select Given Name.

  27. Under APPLICATION ATTRIBUTE, enter firstName.

  28. Check the box for Required.

  29. Add a Family Name attribute

  30. Select +ADD ATTRIBUTE.

  31. Select PingOne Attribute.

  32. Under PINGONE USER ATTRIBUTE, select Family Name.

  33. Under APPLICATION ATTRIBUTE, enter lastName.

  34. Check the box for Required.

  35. Select Save. #### Set up IDP

  36. Expand the Calendly app by selecting the down arrow. [Image: 360102417133]

  37. Select Configuration.

  38. Copy the ISSUER ID and paste it into the Entity ID field on Calendly’s SSO settings page (from Step 1: Navigate to the Calendly SSO configuration page).

  39. Copy SINGLE SIGNON SERVICE and paste it into the Identity provider’s SAML HTTP Request URL field on Calendly’s SSO settings page.

  40. Upload the PEM certificate you downloaded into the X.509 certificate for SAML authentication field on Calendly’s SSO settings page.

  41. In Calendly, select Save & continue.

  42. In Ping, select the pencil icon on the right. [Image: 360102417173]

  43. Select SAML SETTINGS to expand the section.

  44. In Calendly, copy the ACS URL from Step two.

  45. In Ping, under ACS URLs, remove the existing text and paste.

  46. In Calendly, copy the Audience URL from Step two and paste it into Ping, under ENTITY ID.

  47. In Calendly, copy the Default relay state and paste it in Ping under TARGET APPLICATION URL.

  48. In Ping, select Save.

  49. Select < To Application List at the top of the page.

  50. Use the toggle to turn on the Calendly app. [Image: 360102417193]

  51. If you are registered on Ping with the same email as your Calendly Org admin, continue to Step 5: Test connection. #### Creating an Identity

  52. In Ping, select IDENTITIES in the menu.

  53. Select the + Add User button.

  54. Enter GIVEN NAME (first name) and FAMILY NAME (last name).

  55. Under EMAIL ADDRESS and USER NAME, enter your test user’s email.

  56. Select Save.

  57. Find the user in the list, then select the down arrow to expand. [Image: 360100242454]

  58. Select Reset Password.

  59. Enter a temporary password (you’ll need to change this when logging in).

  60. Select Save. #### Test connection

In Calendly, select Enable SSO for yourself, then select Test connection. If successful, you’ll see a confirmation.

[Image: 18192512205975] #### Enforce for your organization

In Calendly, select Enforce SAML SSO for my organization, then Apply.

[Image: 18192512219415]

Once SSO is enforced, all users will be logged out and will need to sign back in with SAML SSO. Only the organization owner can use a backup log in by selecting Log in using another method on the login screen.

How to set up SAML SSO with Microsoft AD FS

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans #### Set up SAML SSO with Microsoft AD FS

  1. In How to set up SAML SSO with your identity provider, complete Steps 1-3.
  • When you reach Step 3. Configure attributes in your IdP, one way to do this is by creating two Issuance Transform Rules. To create a rule, view Microsoft’s Create a Rule to Transform an Incoming Claim, and check the screenshots below: [Image: 4411142158487] [Image: 4411142163223] Note: Many user has used rules to configure attributes, but you can use other methods too.

  1. Contact support with this message: I request a metadata file to connect ADFS with SAML SSO. NOTE: You must complete Step 1. Configure Calendly before sending a message. This step creates the IdP record in Okta.

How to set up SAML SSO with OneLogin

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams with SSO add-on and Enterprise plans.View plans

SAML single sign-on (SSO) lets your team sign in to Calendly using OneLogin. It gives your organization more control over how users access Calendly.

For example, you can:

  • Let users sign in at calendly.com and get verified through OneLogin.
  • Let users log in to OneLogin first, then select the Calendly app.

Note: Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning isn’t supported. To create users automatically, use SCIM. #### Before you begin

  • Your Calendly and OneLogin accounts must use the same email.
  • You need admin access in OneLogin.
  • Open Calendly and OneLogin in two separate browser windows. #### Add Calendly to OneLogin

  1. In OneLogin, go to Applications > Applications.

  2. Select Add App.

  3. Search for Calendly and choose the result labeled SAML 2.0.

  4. Select Save. #### Add a temporary SCIM URL

  5. In OneLogin, go to Configuration.

  6. In SCIM Base URL, enter 0 (you’ll update this later).

  7. Select Save. #### Add identity provider (IdP) details in Calendly

  8. In OneLogin, go to SSO.

  9. Copy these fields into Calendly:

  • Issuer URL → Entity ID
  • SAML 2.0 Endpoint (HTTP) → SAML HTTP Request URL
  1. For the X.509 Certificate:
  • Select View Details > Open in new tab.
  • Copy the certificate and paste it into X.509 certificate for SAML authentication in Calendly.

  1. Change SAML Signature Algorithm to SHA-256 in OneLogin.

  2. In Calendly, choose your Session Duration and select Save & continue. #### Add Calendly details in OneLogin

  3. In Calendly, copy each of the following and paste it into OneLogin:

  • Audience URL → SAML Audience URL
  • ACS URL → SAML Consumer URL
  • Default Relay State → RelayState

  1. Select Save. #### Add parameters in OneLogin

  2. Go to Parameters.

  3. Select SAML NameID (Subject).

  4. Set Value to Email.

  5. Select Save. #### Assign Calendly to a test user

  6. In OneLogin, go to Users and choose a test user with the same email as in Calendly.

  7. Select Applications > + > Calendly.

  8. Select Continue. #### Test your connection

  9. In Calendly, select Test Connection.

  • If the test works, you’ll see a success message.
  • If it fails, you’ll see an error in Calendly or in Okta. #### Enforce SAML SSO for your team
  1. In OneLogin, assign Calendly to all users. Make sure emails match.
  2. In Calendly, select Enforce SAML SSO for my organization.

Once enforced, users will be signed out. Next time they log in, they must use SSO.

The organization owner can still choose Log in using another method on the login page.

How to set up SAML SSO with your identity provider

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams with SSO add-on and Enterprise plans.View plans

Use SAML single sign-on (SSO) to let users log in to Calendly with their identity provider. This makes signing in faster, more secure, and easier to manage.

For example, you can:

  • Help IT and security teams manage users more easily.

  • Let users access Calendly through any SAML-based provider, such as:

  • Okta

  • OneLogin

  • Ping Identity

  • Auth0

  • Microsoft Entra ID

  • Duo

  • Microsoft AD FS

Calendly supports the SAML 2.0 protocol and works with most enterprise IdPs. You can follow these steps for any IdP, even if it’s not listed above. #### Before you begin

  • You must be a Calendly Owner or Admin.
  • Use the same email address in Calendly and your IdP.
  • Open Calendly and your IdP in two browser tabs for easier setup.
  • Calendly doesn’t support Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning. Use SCIM instead to manage users. #### Configure SAML SSO in Calendly

Enter your IdP info in Calendly

  1. In Calendly, go to Admin center > Login > Single sign-on.
  2. Under Step 1, enter the following info from your IdP:
  • IdP setting: Issuer or Entity ID; Calendly field: Entity ID; Required?: Yes; Notes: Also called “Issuer URL” or “Issuer ID”
  • IdP setting: SSO URL; Calendly field: Identity provider’s SAML HTTP Request URL; Required?: Yes; Notes: Also called “Login URL” or “SAML 2.0 Endpoint”
  • IdP setting: x.509 certificate; Calendly field: X.509 certificate for SAML authentication; Required?: Yes; Notes: Must be in PEM format
  1. Choose Save & continue. #### Configure your identity provider

Add these Calendly values in your IdP settings

  • IdP setting: Audience; Value: Calendly’s Audience URL; Required?: Yes; Notes: May also be called “Entity ID”
  • IdP setting: ACS URL; Value: Calendly’s ACS URL; Required?: Yes; Notes: Also known as “Reply URL” or “Callback URL”
  • IdP setting: Recipient/Destination; Value: Calendly’s ACS URL; Required?: Yes; Notes: Some IdPs fill this in automatically
  • IdP setting: Request Binding; Value: 0; Required?: Yes; Notes: May be shown as “POST”
  • IdP setting: Default Relay State; Value: Calendly’s Default Relay State; Required?: Yes if using IdP-initiated login; Notes: Needed to log in from your IdP dashboard
  • IdP setting: Assertion Signature; Value: SHA256; Required?: Yes; Notes: Required
  • IdP setting: Response Signature; Value: SHA256; Required?: No; Notes: Optional
  • IdP setting: Encrypted Assertion; Value: Not supported; Required?: No; Notes: Calendly doesn’t support this
  • IdP setting: Name ID; Value: User’s email address; Required?: Yes; Notes: Must match Calendly email
  • IdP setting: Name ID Format; Value: 0 or 1; Required?: Yes; Notes: Use either option

Set attribute mappings

Add these exact attribute names in your IdP:

  • Name: 0; Required?: Yes; Description: User’s main email address
  • Name: 0; Required?: Yes; Description: User’s first name
  • Name: 0; Required?: Yes; Description: User’s last name

Assign user access

Update your IdP rules so the right people can access Calendly. #### Test the connection

  1. In Calendly, turn on Enable SSO for yourself.
  • This activates SAML SSO only for your own admin account so you can verify the connection before applying it organization-wide.
  1. Select Test connection.
  2. If the test works, you’ll see a success banner.
  3. If it fails, check that:
  • The user’s IdP email matches their Calendly email.
  • The attributes in your IdP are mapped correctly. #### Enforce SSO for your organization
  1. In your IdP, assign the Calendly app to all users.
  2. In Calendly, select Enforce SAML SSO for my organization, then choose Apply.

Note

Enforcing SAML SSO logs out everyone in the organization. They must sign in using SAML SSO. The org Owner can still log in with their original method (such as Google OAuth or email and password) by choosing Log in using another method. #### What’s next?

  • Provision users with SCIM.
  • Review your Admin settings

SAML single sign-on (SSO) overview

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams with SSO add-on and Enterprise plans.View plans

Single sign-on (SSO) lets your team log in to Calendly using their existing company credentials, managed by your company’s identity provider (IdP) — the service that stores and authenticates user accounts (such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or OneLogin). Calendly’s SSO uses Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0, an industry-standard authentication protocol.

With SAML SSO enabled, your team can:

  • Sign in to Calendly through your company’s IdP using one set of credentials.
  • Avoid managing separate Calendly passwords. #### What SSO features does Calendly support?

Supported SSO features

  • Service Provider Initiated SSO (SP-initiated): Users go to calendly.com and log in through your company’s IdP. (“Service Provider” refers to Calendly in this flow.)

  • Identity Provider Initiated SSO (IdP-initiated): Users start from your IdP dashboard and select Calendly to log in. #### What’s not supported

  • Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning is not supported. To manage users automatically, use System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM). #### Which identity providers does Calendly SSO support?

Calendly SSO supports any identity provider (IdP) that uses SAML 2.0. Calendly has tested and documented setup steps for these IdPs:

  • Okta
  • OneLogin
  • Ping Identity
  • Auth0
  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Duo

For other identity providers, follow the steps in How to set up SAML SSO with your identity provider. #### What are the requirements to set up SSO?

To set up SAML SSO for Calendly, you must:

  • Be on the Teams plan with the SSO add-on or the Enterprise plan.
  • Be a Calendly Owner or Admin.
  • Work with your IT admin, who will manage the IdP-side setup.

Other notes about SSO setup:

  • Calendar and integration settings won’t change when SSO is enabled.
  • The session timeout is 21 days by default. Owners and Admins can shorten this in Calendly settings.
  • Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is configured in your identity provider (IdP), not in Calendly.
  • If your company has more than one Calendly organization, you’ll need to set up SSO for each organization separately.
  • Don’t enable SSO if you have Calendly users who aren’t in your identity provider (IdP) — those users won’t be able to log in. #### What happens when SSO is enabled?

Once SAML SSO is turned on:

  • All users are signed out of Calendly.
  • Users must log in again using their identity provider (IdP) credentials.

Owners and Admins can still select Log in using another method to access their Calendly account directly. This option is helpful for disabling SSO or troubleshooting IdP issues. #### How to notify your team before enabling SSO

Before enabling SAML SSO, send an email to your team to let them know about the change. You can use the template below — replace the bracketed placeholders with your organization’s information.

Subject: [Action Required] Log back in to Calendly

Hi,

This is to let you know that [Your Organization Name] is changing the way we access Calendly. Going forward, you’ll be able to log in to Calendly using your [IdP] credentials.

We made this change so you can access Calendly and other applications using the same username and password — that way, you don’t have to remember multiple passwords. If you’re unable to log in using your [IdP] username and password, please let your network administrator know.

Thank you, [Signature] #### How to manage users with SSO enabled

Owners and Admins manage users with SAML SSO using the steps below. #### How to add new users with SSO enabled

  • Add the user in your identity provider (IdP) and in Calendly.
  • Users must accept their Calendly invite before logging in with SSO. #### How to remove users with SSO enabled (without SCIM)

If you don’t have SCIM enabled, removing a user with SSO enabled requires action in both systems:

  • Remove the user from your identity provider (IdP) and from Calendly.

  • Removed users will revert to a Calendly Free plan account.

  • Removed users will sign in using their original sign-in method (for example, Google OAuth — signing in with a Google account).

  • To automate user removal, enable SCIM. #### How to change a user’s email with SSO enabled

  • Update the user’s email in your identity provider (IdP).

  • Then contact Calendly Support with the new email address to update the Calendly account.

SCIM

How to automate group provisioning

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

Automated group provisioning uses SCIM to place users into specific groups in Calendly. This setup mirrors your company’s structure and makes it easy to assign the right event types to each team.

For example, you can:

  • Automatically assign sales teams specific event types.
  • Organize users by department, job title, or region.

This feature builds on SCIM user provisioning. Learn more about setting up SCIM user provisioning. #### Before you begin

  • Group provisioning is available for accounts using SCIM and SSO.
  • You’ll need admin access in Calendly and your IdP (like Okta, Azure, or OneLogin).
  • Make sure users are already being added through SCIM. #### Turn on group provisioning in Calendly

Export your user list

  1. Go to the Admin center in Calendly.
  2. Select Users in the left sidebar.
  3. Export the list of Active and/or Pending users.
  4. Open the file and find the column called Identity Provider Group.
  • This column shows the group values from your identity provider. These values are case-sensitive. #### Map group values
  1. Go to the Admin center in Calendly.
  2. Select Login.
  3. Open the User provisioning tab.
  4. Select Step 2: Map to groups (Optional).
  5. Turn on Mapping attributes to open the Group Mapping table.
  6. Copy each group value into the Value in Identity Provider field.
  7. Choose the matching Calendly group for each value.

Note: Depending on your SSO, you might need to create a new attribute for group mapping. #### Preview and save your mappings

  1. Choose whether to apply changes to existing users.
  2. Select Preview changes.
  3. Review your changes.
  4. Select Save and continue. #### What’s next?

You’re all set! New users added through SCIM will be placed in the correct groups automatically.

Learn more:

  • Managing groups
  • Provisioning users with SCIM

How to configure SCIM with OneLogin

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

You can use System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) provisioning to manage Calendly users from OneLogin — an Identity Provider (IdP) that manages your organization’s user credentials. With SCIM, you can:

  • Create users
  • Update user attributes (like name and email)
  • Deactivate and delete users

Changes in OneLogin will automatically sync to Calendly. SCIM is only available on the Enterprise plan. Contact your Account Executive or Calendly Sales to learn more. #### Before you begin

Make sure you meet these requirements before you set up SCIM:

  • You must configure and enforce Security Assertion Markup Language Single Sign-On (SAML SSO) — the authentication standard that lets users sign in to Calendly through your IdP.
  • You must be a Calendly Owner or Admin.
  • Open Calendly in one browser window and OneLogin in another for easier setup. #### Enable SCIM provisioning

  1. In Calendly, go to Account > Organization Settings > Single sign-on.

  2. Under Optional: Connect SCIM, toggle on SCIM provisioning. #### Add details to OneLogin

  3. In OneLogin, go to Applications > Applications.

  4. Search for the Calendly app and select it.

  5. In the left menu, select Configuration.

  6. In Calendly, select Copy Base URL. In OneLogin, paste the Base URL into the SCIM Base URL field.

  7. In Calendly, select how long the bearer token should last. (A bearer token is a credential that authorizes OneLogin to make SCIM requests to Calendly on your behalf.)

  8. Select Generate new bearer token.

  9. In Calendly, select Copy token and paste the bearer token into OneLogin in the SCIM Bearer Token field.

  10. In OneLogin, select Enable.

  11. Select Save.

  • Calendly value: Base URL; OneLogin field: SCIM Base URL
  • Calendly value: Bearer/API token; OneLogin field: SCIM Bearer Token

Add parameters in OneLogin

  1. In OneLogin, go to the Parameters tab.

  2. Select SCIM Username.

  3. Set Value to Email.

  4. Select Save. #### Enable provisioning in OneLogin

  5. In OneLogin, go to Provisioning.

  6. Under Workflow, select Enable provisioning.

  7. Under Require admin approval before this action is performed, choose the appropriate values for each action:

  • Create user:

  • If the Create user approval box is selected, admins must approve new users before those users can log in.

  • If the Create user approval box is not selected, users are created automatically when they are assigned the Calendly application.

  • In either case, users will get an invite email to join Calendly and must accept the invite before logging in.

  • Delete user: You must approve deletion. ⚠️ Because deleting a user is a non-reversible action, you should require admin approval and keep the Delete user approval box checked.

  • Update user: You must approve any updates made in OneLogin.

  1. Under When users are deleted in OneLogin, or the user’s app access is removed, perform the below action, select Suspend.

⚠️ Note on Suspend vs. Delete deprovisioning: While Calendly supports delete-based deprovisioning, choose the Delete action with caution. The Suspend action deactivates the Calendly user account and revokes access, but preserves the user’s data so the account can be reactivated later. The Delete action permanently removes the user’s Calendly account and all their data, and is non-reversible.

  1. Select Save. #### Approve users

  2. In OneLogin, go to Applications > Calendly > Users.

  3. Check that the correct Calendly users are listed.

  4. To approve all users, select Bulk approve X pending logins for the same app, then select Approve. Alternatively, you can individually approve each pending user. If you do not approve a user, that user won’t be able to log in to Calendly.

  5. If some users are not Pending, select Apply to all, then Reapply Mappings.

Note: To check the SCIM provisioning logs, go to Users > Provisioning. Under All Apps, select Calendly. #### Assigning groups in Calendly

For larger organizations, managing group membership in Calendly may require some level of automation. Group assignment can be achieved through SCIM by mapping existing user-profile attributes from OneLogin to Calendly groups. Read more in our guide on how to use groups in Calendly.

OneLogin does not currently support custom attributes for catalog applications — the pre-built Calendly app available in OneLogin’s Applications catalog. An update request has been made to OneLogin to support the custom attribute needed for group mapping. In the meantime, OneLogin does support a standalone SCIM application — a generic SCIM connector that you configure manually, separate from the pre-built catalog Calendly app — which does support custom attributes. To use the standalone SCIM application, follow our Generic SCIM documentation on how to configure the standalone SCIM application.

How to set up SCIM on Okta

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

IT departments are often responsible for managing many software products and applications for their organizations. IT admins need the ability to automatically sync user information for all the applications an employee may use. The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) developed from this need as a way to reduce mistakes and inconsistencies between identity ecosystems. #### What features are supported with SCIM

With SCIM enabled, you can:

  • add new users

  • update user attributes

  • map attributes to Calendly groups

  • deactivate users #### Before you begin

  • SCIM is only available for accounts on our Enterprise plan.

  • SAML Single Sign-On (SSO) must be set up before SCIM can be set up. #### How to set up SCIM with Okta’s identity security platform

  1. Sign in to Okta.

  2. Go to Applications and select Applications.

  3. Search for the Calendly application and select it.

  4. Select the Sign On tab and ensure the Application username format is set to Email.

    [Image: 1500015157642]

  5. Select Configure API Integration.

  6. Select Enable API integration.

  7. Sign in to calendly.com.

  8. Go to your Admin center, select Login, then select Single sign-on.

  9. Turn on SCIM Provisioning.

  10. Select Copy base URL and paste it into the Base URL field in Okta.

  11. In Calendly, select Generate bearer token, then select Copy token.

  12. Paste the token into the API Token field in Okta.

  13. Select Test API Credentials. You should see a success message. Then select Save.

  14. Select To App under Settings on the right.

  15. Select Edit.

  16. Select Enable for Create Users, Update User Attributes, and Deactivate Users. Then select Save.

  17. Under Attribute Mappings, remove all attributes except Username, Given name, Family name, Primary email, and Display name.

    [Image: 1500013716161]

  18. Select the Assignments tab.

  19. Assign the people in your organization who should have access. #### Assigning users to groups

For larger organizations, managing group membership in Calendly may require some level of automation. This can be achieved through SCIM by utilizing existing attributes of a user’s profile and mapping that value to a Calendly group. Read more about how to use groups here.

NOTE: Once you configure Map to groups, you will no longer be able to manage groups manually. This assumes user group membership is sourced from your identity provider.

  1. Create a new attribute with the following parameters: [Image: 9752338775831]
  • Display name: Calendly group
  • External name (attribute): 0
  • External namespace: 0
  • Attribute type: User
  1. Create a new mapping from a source attribute of your choosing to the newly created attribute for provisioning. [Image: 9752441564951]
  2. Once the mapping has been saved, provision a user to Calendly using your typical provisioning process.
  3. Inside your Calendly application, under Organization setting → Single sign-on, click the optional Map to groups button.
  4. In the left column, type in the exact value(s) from your identity provider’s profile.
  5. In the right column, either select an existing Calendly group or start typing to create a new group on the flow. [Image: 9752750731543]

You can then Preview and Save your new provisioning!

How to set up SCIM with your identity provider

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

Use SCIM 2.0 to automate user provisioning with identity providers like Okta, OneLogin, and Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure). This guide shows you how to connect SCIM with Calendly and enable automatic user management. #### Before you begin

Make sure you’ve completed these tasks before setting up SCIM:

  • Set up SAML single sign-on (SSO) in Calendly.
  • Open two browser windows: one for Calendly and one for your identity provider (IdP).
  • Have your SCIM base URL and bearer token ready. #### Set up SCIM provisioning

Step 1 – Create or use your identity provider app

  1. In your identity provider (IdP), create a custom app for Calendly.
  • If you already set up SSO, use the existing app instead.

  1. Follow your IdP’s documentation for setup instructions. #### Step 2 – Enable SCIM in Calendly

  2. In Calendly, go to Account > Organization Settings > Single sign-on.

  3. Under Optional: Connect SCIM, toggle SCIM provisioning on.

  4. Select Copy base URL and paste it into the matching field in your identity provider.

  5. Choose when your token should expire.

  6. Select Generate new bearer token, then Copy token. Paste it into your identity provider.

  7. In Calendly, select Test Connection.

  8. Select Save.

  • Note: If the connection fails, re-paste the base URL and token and try again. #### Step 3 – Map SCIM attributes

In your identity provider, map the attributes exactly as shown below:

  • Calendly attribute: Name (required); SCIM API attribute: 0; Description: The user’s name as shown in Calendly
  • Calendly attribute: Email address (required); SCIM API attribute: 0; Description: Used to log in to calendly.com
  • Calendly attribute: Active (required); SCIM API attribute: 0; Description: Must be set to 1 to allow login. Setting to 2 disables the user.
  • Calendly attribute: No equivalent (optional); SCIM API attribute: 0; Description: Unique identifier in your identity provider

Important: Only use the attributes listed. Extra attributes will cause errors. #### Step 4 – Enable provisioning

  • In your IdP, turn on provisioning.
  • Follow your provider’s steps to assign users to the app.

SCIM user provisioning overview

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

Calendly supports SAML single sign-on (SSO) for user authentication and SCIM for user provisioning.

After you turn on SSO, you can use SCIM to automatically add, update, deactivate, or remove users in your Calendly organization. SCIM helps you manage users directly from your identity provider (IdP), so onboarding and offboarding is easier at scale. #### What you can do with SCIM

From your identity provider, you can:

  • Add a user
  • Update a user’s name and email
  • Remove a user
  • Add a user to a group
  • Remove a user from a group #### Supported identity providers

Calendly supports any identity provider that uses SCIM 2.0. We’ve tested and documented steps for:

  • Okta
  • OneLogin
  • Microsoft Entra ID

For other identity providers, follow the steps in this article. #### Before you begin

  • Typically, an IT admin is the best person to set up SCIM. You’ll need to be on the Enterprise plan and be a Calendly owner or admin.

  • Make sure SSO is enabled before setting up SCIM.

  • Check that you have enough available seats in Calendly. If all seats are full, provisioning will fail and your IdP will show an error.

  • Check the Users page to see the number of users and available seats listed at the top.

  • To add more seats, follow the steps in this article.

  • Enabling SCIM doesn’t affect calendar or integration connections. Users can still manage these in their own accounts. #### After you provision a user

Accept the Calendly invite

After you add a user with SCIM, Calendly sends them an invite. They need to accept the invite and sign in using SSO. Once they do, they’ll take one of your open seats.

[Image: 4403420476055]

If the user didn’t get the invite, contact support. Be sure to mention if they’re a new employee. #### Assign Managed Events and groups

Calendly gives each new user a default event type. To assign other event types, use Managed Events. You can also group users by department during provisioning. #### Managing members

Making changes to a user

  • Update the name: Change it in your IdP. Calendly will sync the change automatically.
  • Update the email: Change it in your IdP. The user must verify the new address from their inbox before the update appears in Calendly.
  • Update the role: Go to the Users page in Calendly and make the change.
  • Update the group: Change it in your IdP. Calendly will sync the update automatically. #### Removing users

When SCIM is enabled, users can only be removed through your IdP.

Your IdP may send one of two actions to Calendly:

  • Deactivate: The user loses access to Calendly, including login and scheduling. You can reactivate them later.
  • Delete: The user is permanently removed from your organization. This action cannot be undone. If the user had a previous Calendly account, they’ll regain access as a free, solo user.

Security & compliance

Abuse prevention

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

To protect your scheduling experience from abuse, spam, and unwanted bookings, Calendly has implemented strong security measures. Explore the following tips to avoid unwanted bookings and protect your calendar.

Note

If you receive unwanted bookings, follow the steps in this article to report them. #### Tips to avoid unwanted bookings

To further protect your calendar, try these suggestions:

  • Be careful with public sharing: If your scheduling link is in your email signature, consider removing it when emailing recipients who shouldn’t have access to book meetings.
  • Make events secret: Hide event types from your landing page. This way, only invitees with the direct event link can book with you.
  • Share single-use links: Create single-use links to ensure invitees cannot reuse the link for additional bookings.
  • Set a limit for booking in advance: Control how far into the future invitees can schedule meetings by adjusting your availability date range.
  • Change your event link: Update the URL of a specific event type to create a new, secure link.
  • Require email verification: Require invitees to verify their email before confirming their booking.

By following these practices, you can maintain control over your calendar and reduce the risk of abuse and unwanted bookings.

Account Suspension

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Seeing the error message “Your Calendly account has been suspended” when you try to log in? Your account may have been flagged by our team or by our automated tools.

This article explains the common reasons for account suspension and what you can do next. #### Why your account may be suspended

Calendly protects its platform using a mix of internal and third-party tools. These tools help us detect and remove accounts that violate our Terms of Use.

Here are the most common reasons an account might be suspended: #### 1. You may have violated our Terms of Use

Calendly’s Terms of Use list what’s allowed and what’s not. Please review the terms to make sure your account is following our guidelines. #### 2. Your account contains prohibited content

Calendly reviews your event types, account details, and SMS messages. If they contain things like:

  • Illegal activity
  • Illicit substances
  • Explicit content
  • Threats or harassment

your account may be flagged or suspended. #### 3. You used a disposable email address

Calendly doesn’t support disposable or anonymous email domains. These are often used for spam or fraudulent activity. Use a trusted email like Gmail, Yahoo, or a business or school domain when creating your account. #### 4. Your account was flagged for spam

We may investigate accounts for spam-like activity such as:

  • Sending malicious or suspicious links
  • Impersonating another user
  • Sending many notifications at once
  • Using Calendly to send aggressive marketing messages

If we receive a report about your account, our team will review the issue and decide if a suspension is needed. #### How to reinstate your account

If you received an email about your suspension, you can reply to it to appeal the decision. Our team will check your account details and let you know if it can be reinstated. #### How to prevent your account from being flagged

Here are some ways to keep your account safe in the future:

  • Let invitees book for themselves Share your scheduling link so each person can choose their own time. This shows that invitees have agreed to receive event messages.
  • Reduce the number of messages you send Sending too many notifications—especially via SMS—can cause them to be marked as spam.
  • Use other tools for promotions Calendly is not a bulk marketing tool. Avoid sending large batches of invites through Calendly. Doing so can lead to suspension.

The activity log

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

As your organization grows, you can use your activity log to keep track of what is occurring within your Calendly account. Calendly owners and admins on our Enterprise plan have access to this log. #### What you’ll see in the activity log

Each entry in the log includes:

  • Category: what type of change was made
  • Activity: what action was taken
  • By whom: who took the action
  • Date and time: when the action happened

You can also select Details to view more information. What’s shown may vary depending on the action. #### Activity categories

  • Category: Availability; Activities and details captured: - Modified - Schedule created
  • Category: Calendar; Activities and details captured: - Connected - Disconnected - Error
  • Category: Compliance; Activities and details captured: - Data deletion completed - Data deletion request
  • Category: Event Type; Activities and details captured: - Collective created / modified / deleted - Group created / modified / deleted - Modified one-on-one link created - One-off created / deleted / reservations cleared - One-on-One created / modified / deleted - Poll created / deleted / reservations cleared / scheduled / modified - Round robin created / modified / deleted
  • Category: Groups; Activities and details captured: - Admin assigned - Admin unassigned - Created - Deleted - Logo created - Logo updated - Logo removed - Member added - Member removed - Modified
  • Category: Integrations; Activities and details captured: - GoToMeeting connected / disconnected / revoked - Microsoft Teams disconnected / revoked - Salesforce connected / disconnected / error - Webex connected - Zoom connected / disconnected / revoked
  • Category: Login; Activities and details captured: - Failed - Succeeded
  • Category: Managed events; Activities and details captured: - Assigned - Created - Deleted - Modified - Unassigned
  • Category: Permissions; Activities and details captured: - Event types modified - SMS Communication modified - Workflows modified
  • Category: Routing Forms; Activities and details captured: - Created - Deleted - Modified - Published
  • Category: Settings; Activities and details captured: - Branding enabled - Branding disabled - Domain added - Domain removed - Domain verified - Domain Control enabled - Domain Control disabled - Domain Control modified - Email auditing enabled - SAML configured - SAML disabled - SAML enforced - SCIM deleted - SCIM disabled - SCIM enforced - SAML updated - SCIM token created - SCIM token revoked
  • Category: Teams; Activities and details captured: - Created - Deleted - Member added - Member removed - Modified
  • Category: User Management; Activities and details captured: - Added - Deactivated - Deleted - Error - Invite canceled - Invite declined - Invite resent - Invite sent - Modified - Reactivated - Removed - Role changed - User pending (specific to domain control)
  • Category: User Profile; Activities and details captured: - URL slug modified - Welcome message modified
  • Category: Workflows; Activities and details captured: - Assigned - Created - Deleted - Modified

Access the activity log

  1. Log in to your Calendly account.
  2. In Calendly, go to the Admin center > Security page.
  3. Select the Activity log tab.

On the Activity log page, you’ll see a table with activity info.

Note

Data in the activity log is deleted every 90 days. #### Search and filter the activity log

Use the search bar to look through all columns and event details.

  • You can search by things like email address, event name, or team name.
  • Wrap your search in quotes to find exact phrases (e.g., “30 minute meeting”).

Use the Filter button to narrow results by:

  • Category
  • Activity
  • User (By whom)
  • Date range #### Export the activity log

You can export log data as a .CSV file with up to 10,000 events.

If the export includes fewer than 1,000 events, you can download the file right in Calendly.

[Image: 8499391183895]

If it includes more than 1,000 events, Calendly will email you a download link. The link will expire after 24 hours.

[Image: 8499450718743] #### Use the API to receive logs remotely

Enterprise owners or admins can send activity log data to a SIEM or logging service using our API. For setup instructions, visit the Calendly developer portal.

Calendly Platform Security and Compliance

Calendly is a cloud application that provides meeting scheduling as a service. Our platform creates a seamless experience to schedule meetings through securely integrating with calendar providers to check availability.

Our software is designed to request the minimum access necessary to customer resources to achieve a seamless scheduling experience. We are continuously mindful of our customer’s privacy and limit access to all customer data on a need to know basis internally. Calendly applies best security practices retaining a minimal amount of customer data and operating with the fewest privileges necessary to provide a great experience to our users.

This document is meant to be an overview of platform-related privacy, security, and compliance. #### Calendar Integrations

Google Calendar and Office365 Integrations

A Calendly user may use either the Google Calendar or Office365 integrations to connect their calendar with Calendly to simplify scheduling. Calendly is built to only access the minimum data needed from connected calendars to deliver its service. #### Calendly Outlook Plug-in

The Calendly Platform uses websockets to communicate when new bookings are available with the Calendly for Outlook plug-in. Calendly will write appointment time, duration, subject and scheduled attendee information from Calendly to Outlook. All data is encrypted in transit using TLS. Data stored at rest in the underlying storage is encrypted including automated backups, read replicas, and snapshots. #### iCloud Calendar Integration

Info

As of August 20, 2024, Calendly no longer supports new connections to iCloud Calendar. Existing connections will continue to be supported, but new users or those who have not previously set up an iCloud Calendar connection will not be able to do so. To learn how to connect a Google, Office 365 or Outlook.com, or Exchange calendar, check out Connecting your calendar.

The Calendly iCloud Calendar integration uses your iCloud credentials to access the iCloud API. Apple has an all or nothing approach to data access in that the same credentials are used for all services. While Calendly securely stores and restricts access to the iCloud credentials we collect, Calendly recommends setting up two-factor authentication on iCloud accounts and using an app-specific password when setting up the Calendly iCloud Calendar Integration. #### Authenticating with calendar integrations

We avoid collecting third-party passwords by utilizing OAuth authentication with Office365 and Google Calendar. Calendly users can disconnect their calendar connection at any time through the Calendar settings page within their account.

When using the Calendly Outlook Plug-in, Calendly requires installation on customer devices to read calendar conflicts and schedule events. Most of our customers prefer to use OAuth calendar integrations. #### Booking Pages

The Calendly platform allows users to customize booking pages to collect relevant information from invitees. Calendly is not intended to be used by users to collect sensitive personal information. #### Data Encryption

  • All connections from the browser to the Calendly platform are encrypted in transit using TLS SHA-256 with RSA Encryption.
  • All data is encrypted at rest.
  • Calendly user passwords are stored as salted password hashes
  • User passwords for the iCloud Calendar integration are encrypted #### Physical Infrastructure

The Calendly application is hosted on Kubernetes / Google Cloud Services (GCS). GCS’ data center operations have been accredited under:

  • ISO 27001
  • SOC 1 and SOC 2/SSAE 16/ISAE 3402 (Previously SAS 70 Type II)
  • PCI Level 1
  • FISMA Moderate
  • Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX)

For additional information see:

<cloud.google.com>

kubernetes.io #### Vulnerability Management

We keep our systems up to date with the latest security patches and continuously monitor for new vulnerabilities through compliance and security mailing lists. This includes automatic scanning of our code repositories for vulnerable dependencies. All of our services run in containers that isolate processes, memory, and the file system using LXC while host-based firewalls restrict applications from establishing local network connections. The services are configured with tight network security constraints to further limit any potential risk. The Google Cloud Platform regularly conducts internal vulnerability assessments and patch the underlying systems. #### Incident Response Plan

Identification

Calendly routinely monitors our external services and open source libraries for security issues and has executed Data Processing Addendums (DPA) with our vendors to ensure prompt notification of data breaches. Calendly continuously scans Calendly for service interruptions, performance degradation, and security vulnerabilities with automated tools to immediately alert our engineers when an incident has been detected. Users may also report security issues to the security@calendly.com #### Containment

Whenever our engineering team is alerted to a security issue, the team determines what systems are affected and quickly contains the problem by disconnecting all affected systems and devices. Because all of our services run in containers that isolate processes, memory, and the file system they are easily replaced and updated in their entirety inhibiting further escalation. #### Recovery

If data was found to be affected, it is restored from clean backup files, ensuring that no vulnerabilities remain. Secondary backups are also stored in Google Cloud. Systems are monitored for any recurrence. Ephemeral services are patched and redeployed eliminating any chance of malware persistence. #### Retrospective

The Calendly engineering team analyzes every operations incident and how it was handled, making recommendations for better future response and for preventing a recurrence. #### Change Management Plan

New releases to the Calendly Platform are thoroughly reviewed and tested to ensure high availability and a great customer experience. Changes to our codebase are required to include unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end tests. Changes are also run against our continuous integration server. This enables us to automatically detect any issues in development.

Once a changeset is completed, it is manually peer reviewed by one or more members of the engineering team. The changeset is then evaluated and manually tested by our quality assurance team to thoroughly test areas of expected impact, regression test, and further evaluate the user experience.

After a changeset is released, we continue to monitor application exceptions and log exceptions. These exceptions are regularly reviewed and triaged for resolution. Performance impacts of the changeset are monitored through several monitoring services. #### Employee Screening and Policies

As a condition of employment, all Calendly employees undergo pre-employment background checks and receive training during onboarding and throughout their employment on company policies, security, GDPR, and other related security, privacy, and compliance topics. #### Compliance

PCI Compliance

Calendly uses a PCI-compliant pay processor Stripe for encrypting and storing credit card details. More information on Stripe’s commitment to security and compliance can be found here. We utilize the direct Stripe javascript integration so your credit card information never reaches Calendly’s servers. #### Legal Documents

Calendly Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, Data Processing Addendum (DPA), and End User Licence Agreements

Can all be found in our Legal hub.

Data Storage and International Data Transfers

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Having trouble understanding where your Calendly data is stored or how it’s protected? Use this guide to learn how Calendly manages and secures user data, and what to do if you need help with international data transfers. #### Data Hosting Location

Calendly stores user and invitee data in U.S.-based data centers managed by Google Cloud Services (GCS) and Amazon Web Services (AWS). #### Infrastructure Compliance

Calendly’s hosting providers meet several industry standards:

  • ISO 27001
  • SOC 1, SOC 2 / SSAE 16 / ISAE 3402
  • PCI Level 1
  • FISMA Moderate
  • Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX)

Learn more:

  • Google Cloud Security
  • Kubernetes Security #### Data Encryption

Calendly encrypts your data to protect it both in transit and at rest:

  • All web traffic uses TLS SHA-256 with RSA Encryption
  • Data at rest is encrypted using industry standards
  • Passwords are stored as salted hashes
  • iCloud Calendar passwords use salted encryption #### Transferring Personal Data from the EEA or UK

If you collect data from individuals in the European Economic Area (EEA) or the UK, Calendly uses legal tools to ensure safe transfer. #### Key Safeguards

  • Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) are included in Calendly’s Data Processing Agreement (DPA)
  • UK Addendum is also part of the DPA for UK-specific requirements
  • All sub-processors that handle your data have signed DPAs #### Frequently asked questions - International transfers

SCCs are standard agreements that define how personal data is protected when transferred outside the EEA.
