Domain Control overview

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

Domain Control helps you manage who creates Calendly accounts in your organization. You control which employees can sign up and enforce your IT security rules.

For example, you can:

  • Review all accounts using your company domain
  • Require approval before new users sign up
  • Lock your domain so only approved people can use it #### What to expect

Complete account visibility

Review all existing accounts linked to your domain. Download a report that shows who is using your domain with Calendly.

Faster onboarding and fewer support tickets

Your Enterprise account comes pre-configured with features like Managed Events and Salesforce integrations. New employees sign up faster and can start scheduling right away.

Secure scheduling with your IT policies enforced

Make sure users follow your IT policies (like single sign-on). All company activity stays in one place you can review and audit. #### Before you begin

To use Domain Control, your organization must have Single Sign-On (SSO) enabled. You also need to be an Owner or Admin on an Enterprise plan. #### How Domain Control works

Require approval before signup

When you enable Domain Control, new users must request access. They cannot create an account on their own. An admin must approve the request before the user can continue.

Control who has access

You can route approval requests to a specific person, email address, or URL. You can also lock the domain so no one can sign up with it.

  • If someone’s request is denied, they can still sign up. They just need to use a different email address. #### Getting started with Domain Control

These Help Center articles walk you through setting up and using Domain Control:

  • How to set up Domain Control: Step-by-step instructions for your domain provider
  • Domain Control FAQs: Answers to common questions
  • Domain Control: the user experience: What employees see when Domain Control is enabled
  • Managing users outside your Calendly organization: How to handle people outside your organization using your domain #### FAQs

Use Domain Control if you are a large organization and need to manage who uses your domain with Calendly. It helps you enforce security rules and prevent unauthorized accounts.

Yes. Once you verify your domain, you can download a report showing all Calendly users with your domain. The report includes users in your organization and users outside your organization.

The report includes all Calendly users with your verified domain, including:

  • Users already in your organization
  • Users outside your organization using your domain

You can add free users from this list to your org using the “Add new user” process.

Yes. Any new user outside your account cannot connect a protected domain’s calendar. This applies to all supported calendars except the Outlook plug-in.

Yes. There is no limit to how many domains you can verify and control.

If you reach your seat limit and a user requests access, add more seats from your billing page before you approve them.

Yes. Your organization must have Single Sign-On (SSO) enabled to use Domain Control.

How does Calendly help customers with data subject rights?

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Certain privacy laws, such as GDPR and CCPA, provide people with rights and control over how their personal data is processed. These rights are often called data subject rights or consumer rights. As a customer, when you use Calendly Services, the people whose data you collect, process, import, store or interact with – such as your invitees, contacts, meeting attendees and other people – are generally considered your data subjects.

Specific data subject rights and how Calendly helps you comply can be found below. If you have additional questions or would like assistance, please contact us.

  • The right of access: The right to rectification (‘right to correction’); The data subject’s right to know what data you have about them and how you are using that data. The contacts tab generally lists your data subjects that are stored within the Calendly app and data associated with those contacts. Depending on what Calendly Services you are using, there may be additional data stored about these people in other locations within the Calendly app. For example, if you have scheduled a meeting with a person, that meeting will be listed in your meetings tab. You can export your meeting details, filter, and provide the resulting data to your data subject.: The data subject’s right to correct inaccurate information you hold about them. Within the contacts tab, Calendly provides the ability to update information you have about your contacts.
  • The right of access: The right of erasure (the ‘right to be forgotten’); The data subject’s right to know what data you have about them and how you are using that data. The contacts tab generally lists your data subjects that are stored within the Calendly app and data associated with those contacts. Depending on what Calendly Services you are using, there may be additional data stored about these people in other locations within the Calendly app. For example, if you have scheduled a meeting with a person, that meeting will be listed in your meetings tab. You can export your meeting details, filter, and provide the resulting data to your data subject.: The data subject’s right to have their data deleted. You can delete a data subject’s information by following the instructions in this article. Depending on the Calendly Services you are using, you may have additional data associated with that person, such as meeting history, meeting recordings, and/or emails. Calendly provides functionality to delete this information, however, you may need to delete the entries individually.
  • The right of access: The right to restrict processing; The data subject’s right to know what data you have about them and how you are using that data. The contacts tab generally lists your data subjects that are stored within the Calendly app and data associated with those contacts. Depending on what Calendly Services you are using, there may be additional data stored about these people in other locations within the Calendly app. For example, if you have scheduled a meeting with a person, that meeting will be listed in your meetings tab. You can export your meeting details, filter, and provide the resulting data to your data subject.: The data subject’s right to restrict further processing of their data, either temporarily or permanently. Calendly can attempt to assist if you contact us. Alternatively, in some cases, you can ask the data subject if you can simply delete their information.
  • The right of access: The right to data portability; The data subject’s right to know what data you have about them and how you are using that data. The contacts tab generally lists your data subjects that are stored within the Calendly app and data associated with those contacts. Depending on what Calendly Services you are using, there may be additional data stored about these people in other locations within the Calendly app. For example, if you have scheduled a meeting with a person, that meeting will be listed in your meetings tab. You can export your meeting details, filter, and provide the resulting data to your data subject.: The data subject’s right to receive the data concerning them. To fulfill this request, you can follow the information provided in “the right to access” section above.
  • The right of access: The right to object; The data subject’s right to know what data you have about them and how you are using that data. The contacts tab generally lists your data subjects that are stored within the Calendly app and data associated with those contacts. Depending on what Calendly Services you are using, there may be additional data stored about these people in other locations within the Calendly app. For example, if you have scheduled a meeting with a person, that meeting will be listed in your meetings tab. You can export your meeting details, filter, and provide the resulting data to your data subject.: The data subject’s right to object to a certain type (or all types) of processing of their data. Calendly can attempt to assist if you contact us. Alternatively, in some cases, you can ask the data subject if you can simply delete their information. If the data subject is objecting to the processing of cookies, please visit our Cookies FAQ for more information.

How to add legal disclaimers to text notifications

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

Enterprise plan Owners and Admins can add legal disclaimers to text notifications, in addition to Calendly’s required default disclaimer.

Note

Legal disclaimers can only be added at the organization level and are in addition to Calendly’s required disclaimer, which cannot be disabled. #### Adding an additional legal disclaimer

  1. From the Admin center, select Branding.
  2. In the Organization SMS Legal Disclaimer text box, enter the additional disclaimer you’d like to include with your text opt-in.
  3. Select Save Changes to add the disclaimer to all meetings with text reminders. #### Previewing the legal disclaimer

Any events with text reminders will now display your additional legal disclaimer below Calendly’s default disclaimer on the scheduling page.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.

  2. Find an event type that includes text notifications.

  3. Select the [Image: 33405605706647] three dots in the event card, then choose Add to website.

  4. Follow the invitee scheduling flow by selecting a date and time.

  5. On the Enter Details page, preview your additional legal disclaimer. #### Removing an additional legal disclaimer

  6. From the Admin center, select Branding.

  7. In the Organization SMS Legal Disclaimer text box, delete the additional disclaimer.

  8. Select Save Changes to remove the disclaimer from all meetings with text reminders.

How to block someone from booking with you

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

If someone misuses your booking links or repeatedly books unwanted meetings, you can block them in Calendly.

Blocking someone helps prevent future bookings from that source. You can also view and manage blocked sources from your account settings at any time. #### Block someone from a meeting

You can block someone from an upcoming or past meeting within 90 days of the meeting creation date.

  1. Go to the Meetings page and select the meeting.
  2. Under Details, find the person you want to block.
  3. Select the [Image: 38279683459351] three dots next to their name, then choose:
  • Block invitee (for an upcoming meeting), or
  • Block attendee (for a past meeting)
  1. Complete the form.
  2. Select Submit.

You’ll see a confirmation message when the block is complete. #### What happens after you block someone

  • Any upcoming non-group meetings with this source are canceled and removed from your calendar.
  • Calendly prevents future bookings from this source.
  • You can manage or reverse this action from your account settings. #### View or unblock blocked sources

You can view everyone you’ve blocked and unblock them at any time. After you unblock someone, they’re no longer blocked from booking with you. #### View and unblock from account settings

  1. Select your profile picture.
  2. Go to All settings > Security > Blocked sources.
  3. Find the person you want to unblock.
  4. Select Unblock, then confirm. #### Unblock from a past meeting

You can also unblock someone directly from a past meeting.

  1. Go to the Meetings page and select the meeting.
  2. Under Details, find the person you want to unblock.
  3. Select the [Image: 38279683459351] three dots next to their name and choose Unblock attendee.
  4. Select Unblock to confirm. #### Prevent unwanted bookings

To learn about other ways to protect your scheduling experience, see Abuse prevention.

How to delete personal data in Calendly

Available to Owners and Admins on all plans.View plans

Stay compliant with GDPR, CCPA, and other privacy laws by deleting personal data in Calendly - No need to contact support. #### GDPR and CCPA compliant

For more details on how Calendly helps you adhere to data rights under GDPR and other privacy laws, view How does Calendly honor my data rights? #### Types of data to delete

  • Contact and invitee data (your customers)

  • Calendly user data (your employees) #### About contact and invitee data deletion

  • Scenario: Ways to delete data; Your customer requests that you delete their data.: - For selected invitees: enter invitee email addresses - For all invitees: specify a data range

  • Scenario: Who can delete data; Your customer requests that you delete their data.: Owners and admins on any Calendly plan

  • Scenario: Data deleted from; Your customer requests that you delete their data.: Your organization’s Calendly instance

  • Scenario: Results; Your customer requests that you delete their data.: - Contact or invitee name is deleted. - Contact or invitee email and domain is anonymized. - For example, contact / invitee email will display as 1e99adf8a31ad9@deleted.calendly.com. - Invitee questions and answers are deleted. - See image in Once data is deleted.

Before you begin

  • You must be a Calendly owner or admin.
  • If you’re not an owner or admin, visit your Org directory to find someone who can help. #### Deleting contact and invitee data

To delete specific contact or invitee data by email address

  1. In Calendly, select Admin center > Security.

  2. Select Data deletion.

  3. Under Delete specific contact or invitee information, enter the invitees email address. Note: To delete more than one invitee, separate emails with commas (up to 100).

  4. Select Delete, then Yes to confirm. #### To delete all invitee data within a date range

  5. In Calendly, select Admin center > Security.

  6. Select Data deletion.

  7. Under Delete information within a period of time, choose a date range and select Apply.

  8. Select Delete, then Yes to confirm.

Note

  • Deleting data by date range removes event data only.
  • It does not delete contacts. Follow the steps above to delete a contact. #### Once you’ve made a request

On the Data deletion page in the Security section of the Admin center, a log of invitee data deletion requests will show under Data deletion history.

[Image: 28922766685079] #### To cancel a data deletion request

Calendly will process the deletion within 7 days of the request. To cancel a pending data request:

  1. Select the three vertical dots next to the request on the data deletion history table.
  2. Select Cancel.

[Image: 28922774875927]

Once data has been deleted, it cannot be recovered. #### About Calendly user data deletion

  • Scenarios: Ways to delete data; You want to delete data for your account.: Self-delete your Calendly account; You want to delete data for an employee.: Delete other users’ Calendly accounts
  • Scenarios: Who can delete data; You want to delete data for your account.: All users can delete their own accounts. Note: If an owner deletes their own account, they will automatically disband the organization, but users will not be deleted.; You want to delete data for an employee.: Owners and admins can delete accounts that were created upon joining their organization. Note: They cannot delete pre-existing Calendly accounts.
  • Scenarios: Data deleted from; You want to delete data for your account.: - Your organization’s Calendly instance. Personal data removed from: - Scheduled meetings - Contacts - Invitees - Event types - Organization and teams - Integrations - User directories - Calendly email newsletters - Customer relationship management tools - Data lakes - All sub-processors that Calendly uses

How to delete, transfer or disband your Calendly account

Deleting your account

  1. Select your profile picture, then go to Account Settings >Profile.
  2. Scroll down and select Delete Account.
  3. Choose one of the following options:
  • Transfer ownership and delete my account: Before you can delete your account, you must transfer ownership to another team member so they can manage the organization. All users are selectable for ownership.
  • Keep my account and leave organization: If you don’t want to delete your account, you can transfer ownership and leave the organization.
  • Delete my account and disband the organization: If you don’t want to transfer ownership, you can delete your account and disband the organization.
  1. If transferring ownership, select a new owner.
  2. Choose a reason for deletion.
  3. Select Delete. #### Disbanding your organization’s Calendly instance (for owners)

As an owner, deleting your account will disband your Calendly organization:

  • All users will be removed, but will not be deleted.
  • Users will have their own free, solo account.
  • All teams will be deleted.

To delete your account, follow the steps in How to delete your account. Users can follow these same steps to delete their own accounts. #### Removing and deleting a Calendly user (for owners and admins)

For step-by-step instructions, view How to add or remove users and seats. Depending on when a user created their account, you may not be able to delete them. For more details, view the note in How to remove users and paid seats. #### Deleting a user with SCIM enabled

As an owner or admin with a SCIM-enabled account, you must remove users via your identity provider (idP). With SCIM enabled, you cannot remove users from the Admin center.

Within your identity provider (idP), you may have the option to deactivate or delete a user. Consult your identity provider’s documentation for more details. #### What happens after you delete personal data

Restrict usage of SMS/text messaging

Available to Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans.View plans

Calendly can turn off all SMS messages to help your organization stay compliant with privacy rules. Once SMS is turned off, no messages will send, even if reminders or workflows already include them.

When SMS messaging is turned off, users may no longer see SMS-related features or may see messaging that explains the feature has been turned off.

Your privacy and security

Calendly is a cloud service that simplifies meeting scheduling by securely connecting to calendar providers to check availability. We follow strict security practices.

With OAuth calendar integration, Calendly doesn’t need access to your device. However, if you use the Calendly Outlook Plug-in, it must be installed to read calendar conflicts and schedule events. #### Calendly’s commitment to trust

Customer trust is key to everything we do at Calendly. Our software asks for only the necessary access to provide smooth scheduling. We protect your privacy by limiting access to customer data internally. Employees receive security training, and access to internal systems is secured with multi-factor authentication. #### Physical infrastructure

The Calendly application is hosted on Kubernetes / Google Cloud Services (GCS). GCS’ data center operations have been accredited under:

  • ISO 27001
  • SOC 1 and SOC 2/SSAE 16/ISAE 3402 (Previously SAS 70 Type II)
  • PCI Level 1
  • FISMA Moderate
  • Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) #### PCI compliance

Calendly uses Stripe, a PCI-compliant pay processor for encrypting and storing credit card details. More information on Stripe’s commitment to security and compliance can be found here. We utilize the direct Stripe javascript integration, so your credit card information never reaches Calendly’s servers. #### Customer security best practices

We avoid collecting third-party passwords by utilizing OAuth authentication with Office365 and Google Calendar. #### Data Encryption

  • All connections from the browser to the Calendly platform are encrypted in transit using TLS SHA-256 with RSA Encryption.
  • All data is encrypted when written to disk.
  • User passwords are stored as salted password hashes and never accessible by any Calendly employee. #### FAQs

Calendly is fully committed to compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). We understand the importance of incorporating standards put forth by GDPR into our data practices and making sure our customers, whether citizens of the EU or businesses that use Calendly with European customers, feel secure and confident to continue using Calendly.

In response to GDPR, we have developed new features (including cookie management tools and data deletion processes), enhanced existing functionality (such as Terms of Use opt-ins), improved our documentation, and incorporated a Data Processing Addendum into our Terms of Use.

Calendly has designed its data privacy program to be compliant with GDPR, both now and as future developments come along.

We have incorporated a Data Processing Addendum into our Terms of Use. There is nothing additional for you to sign or execute, and by accepting the Terms of Use, the DPA is already in place for you.

Yes. Calendly updated our DPA in September, 2022 to include the new UK Addendum. As one of the many data privacy law changes the UK is working through since Brexit, the UK’s Information Commissioner’s office released in May, 2022 its own data transfer agreement, as well as an addendum it will allow entities to add to the 2021 EU Standard Contractual Clauses to allow for legal transfers of UK personal data to countries not deemed adequate with regard to their data protection laws, such as the United States. Parties are required to start using the transfer agreement or Standard Contractual Clauses addendum in new contracts on September 21, 2022, and are required to update existing contracts by March 21, 2024. More information regarding the UK addendum can be found on the ICO’s website. Calendly previously updated our DPA so that it includes the new version of EU Standard Contractual Clauses which came out last year. Since our DPA already incorporates the EU Standard Contractual Clauses, we have added the UK addendum to them to account for customers transferring personal data to us from the UK.

Please contact us and we will be happy to process your request.

What to expect when Notetaker joins your meetings

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users. Release notes

Note

Notetaker is being gradually rolled out to eligible users. Join the waitlist.

Learn what happens when Notetaker joins your meeting — so everything runs smoothly from start to finish. #### Before you begin

  • Enable Notetaker for your meetings.
  • Notetaker can record Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams meetings, regardless of whether you’re the host or if the meeting was scheduled through Calendly or your Google Calendar. #### What to expect when you’re the host

At the scheduled start time:

  • Notetaker joins your Zoom meeting.

  • If you have a waiting room, be sure to Admit Notetaker.

  • A message asks you to Approve or Decline Notetaker.

  • Notetaker will wait up to 30 minutes for you to join before leaving.

  • Once in the call, Notetaker will wait about 90 seconds for you to approve the recording prompt before leaving.

[Image: 36159802268183]

  • If you select Decline, Notetaker leaves and won’t record.

  • If you select Approve, Notetaker joins and starts recording.

  • You and your attendees will see a message that the meeting is being recorded.

  • Select Got it to continue or Leave meeting to exit.

  • Notetaker also sends a chat message confirming the meeting is being recorded.

If you are a meeting attendee and would like your meeting host to remove Notetaker, please let them know.

Learn how to remove Notetaker from an in-progress meeting.

Note

On some Zoom plans, you can change what attendees see in Zoom by customizing the consent message. Note: This must be done in Zoom settings, not Calendly.

You’re responsible for getting consent from attendees to record and transcribe meetings. Learn more in Zoom’s recording consent guide. #### What to expect when you’re an attendee

What to expect as an attendee in someone else’s meeting:

  • At the scheduled start time, Notetaker will automatically join the meeting.

  • If the host has a waiting room, they will need to Admit Notetaker.

  • When the host joins they will be prompted to Approve or Decline Notetaker.

  • Notetaker will wait up to 30 minutes for the host to join before leaving.

  • Once the host has joined the call, Notetaker will wait about 90 seconds for them to approve the recording prompt before leaving.

  • If the host doesn’t approve Notetaker, the meeting will not be recorded.

  • If the host approves Notetaker, you’ll see a message: “This meeting is being recorded…”

  • Choose what to do next:

  • Click Got it to stay in the meeting.

  • Click Leave meeting if you don’t want to join.

  • Notetaker also sends a chat message confirming the meeting is being recorded. #### What the host sees when Notetaker joins:

  • At the meeting’s start time, Notetaker will join automatically.

  • The host will see a message: “[Notetaker user]’s Calendly Notetaker is requesting to record this meeting.”

  • The host can choose to:

  • Click Approve to allow recording.

  • Click Decline to deny recording.

  • They can also check “Apply these permissions to all future requests in this meeting” to save their preference. #### How can the bot be removed?

Learn how to remove Notetaker from a meeting. #### Contacts and Notetaker

When Notetaker joins a meeting from your Google Calendar, Calendly automatically creates contacts for all meeting attendees.

Learn more about Contacts in Calendly.

Sharing & booking

Advanced booking form features

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly’s invitee question features help you collect the right information from attendees. Whether you’re meeting one-on-one or hosting a larger event, you can customize your questions to save time and improve the experience for everyone.

This guide shows you how to use these features to make scheduling faster and more helpful. #### Invitee name and email

By default, invitees must enter their name and email address to book with you.

You can choose how the name field appears:

  • One field: Name
  • Two fields: First Name, Last Name

To change the name fields:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the [Image: 33458168330391] three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. Select More options at the bottom.
  4. Expand the Invitee form section.
  5. Under Invitee details, choose your preferred name format.
  6. Select Save changes. #### Autofill name and email from past bookings

You can let Calendly remember an invitee’s info and autofill it the next time they book. This includes name, email, and phone number (for text reminders).

By default, this is turned off.

To turn it on:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the [Image: 33458168330391] three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. Select More options at the bottom.
  4. Expand the Invitee form section.
  5. Check the box for Autofill Invitee Name, Email, and Text Reminder Phone Number (when applicable) from prior bookings.
  6. Select Save changes. #### Collect phone numbers

Add a Phone number invitee question to your booking form to capture invitee contact details. This adds a phone field to your booking page.

If you’re hosting a phone call meeting, you can set your meeting location to Phone call so invitees are prompted to enter their number automatically. #### Add guests to the meeting

Invitees can add up to 10 guests when booking. Guests get a meeting invite, and you’ll see all guest names on your Meetings page. This feature is not available for group events.

Guest invitations are turned on by default.

To turn them off:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the [Image: 33458168330391] three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. Select More options at the bottom.
  4. Expand the Invitee form section.
  5. Toggle Invitee guests off.
  6. Select Save changes.

How to add a cancellation policy

Available to all users on all paid plans.View plans

You can include a cancellation policy to let invitees know what to expect if they need to cancel or reschedule.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the [Image: 33458179781655] three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. At the bottom of the editor, select More options.
  4. Open the Notifications and workflows section.
  5. Under Basic notifications, select the [Image: 28926500946711] three dots next to Calendar invitation/Email confirmation, then choose Edit.
  6. Scroll to the bottom and locate the Cancellation policy section. Add your policy here.
  7. (Recommended) To let invitees cancel or reschedule on their own, check the box for Include cancel and reschedule links in email invitations and reminders.
  8. Select Save and close.

Note

Calendly will display your cancellation policy, but it doesn’t restrict cancellations or reschedules based on the policy.

How to book meetings in real time

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

With Calendly, you can quickly schedule a meeting with your invitee when you’ve agreed on a time. Use the Book meeting option to schedule without sending a link.

For example, you can:

  • Book a meeting directly for your invitee using your event type’s settings, Workflows, and integrations.

  • Customize the meeting name, duration, and location for this specific booking.

  • These changes won’t affect your event type settings and aren’t available for Group event types.

  • Override available times to schedule outside your availability when flexibility is needed.

  • Book on behalf of other team members when you set up event type permissions.

This feature is available from your Scheduling and Contacts pages on desktop, the browser extension, and the mobile app. #### Overriding available times

Calendly’s Override available times feature gives you more flexibility when scheduling outside your regular availability. Your invitee will still receive the reminders, notifications, and workflows from the event type.

Notes: You can’t override busy events on another host’s calendar. The override option is also unavailable for Round Robin event types. #### Book a meeting from the Scheduling page

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. (Optional) Open the My Calendly dropdown to switch to another user or team.
  3. Find the event type you want to schedule and hover over it to see more options.
  4. Select [Image: 31727479674135] Book meeting.
  5. Under Invitee details, enter the invitee’s name and email. You can also select + Add guests to include others in the meeting.
  6. (Optional) Customize the meeting name, duration, or location.
  7. Choose an available time from the calendar, or select Override available times in the top-right corner to schedule outside your regular availability.
  • To view availability in your invitee’s time zone, use the Time zone display dropdown at the top of the calendar.
  1. Under Invitee questions, answer any required or optional questions on behalf of your invitee.
  2. Select Book meeting.

Once the meeting is scheduled, you’ll be taken back to your Scheduling page. You can view or manage the meeting from your Meetings page. #### Book a meeting from the Contacts page

  1. Go to the Contacts page.
  2. Select the contact to open their details. You can also hover over the contact to access the Schedule menu.
  3. Select Schedule, then choose [Image: 31727479674135] Book meeting.
  4. Select the event type you want to schedule, then select Continue.
  5. Under Invitee details, the invitee’s name and email are automatically filled out. You can also select + Add guests to include others in the meeting.
  6. (Optional) Customize the meeting name, duration, or location.
  7. Choose an available time from the calendar, or select Override available times in the top-right corner to schedule outside your regular availability.
  • To view availability in your invitee’s time zone, use the Time zone display dropdown at the top of the calendar.
  1. Under Invitee questions, answer any required or optional questions on behalf of your invitee.
  2. Select Book meeting.

Once the meeting is scheduled, you’ll be taken back to your Contacts page. You can view or manage the meeting from your Meetings page. #### Text notifications

When booking a meeting from the desktop experience, if your event uses text notifications, the invitee’s phone number is automatically filled in when it’s available in the invitee’s contact information. Otherwise, you can enter it manually.

After you book the meeting, your invitee will receive a text message with a confirmation link asking them to confirm before text notifications are sent.

When you change a link, old links stop working. Be sure to share or embed the new links. #### Change the link for your landing page

How to pre-fill invitee information in your Calendly link

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

You can customize your Calendly link to automatically fill in your invitee’s details, such as name, email, or answers to questions, before they land on your booking page. This saves time and gives your invitees a smoother scheduling experience. #### What you can do with a pre-filled link

  • Save your clients time by filling in their details ahead of time.

  • Pre-answer questions on the booking page for your invitees.

  • Add guests to your meeting on behalf of your invitees. #### Before you begin

  • Make sure you’ve already created your event type.

  • We recommend connecting your calendar before sharing links. #### Customize your link

Step 1 – Copy your event link

Go to the Scheduling page, find your event type, and select Copy Link. #### Step 2 – Paste the link where you’ll send it

You can paste it into an email, text message, or other messaging tool. #### Step 3 – Add a question mark (?) to the end of your link

This starts the custom information string.

Example:

calendly.com

Note: If your link already includes a variable (like a calendar date), skip this step. #### Step 4 – Add the variable and value you want to pre-fill

  • Use the format variable=value.
  • Use %20 to add a space between words.

Example:

?name=John%20Doe #### Step 5 – Add more variables using &

To add more info, place an ampersand (&) before the next variable.

Example:

?name=John%20Doe&email=john@example.com #### Information you can pre-fill

  • Field: Full name; Variable: name; Example: name=John%20Doe
  • Field: First name; Variable: first_name; Example: first_name=John
  • Field: Last name; Variable: last_name; Example: last_name=Doe
  • Field: Email; Variable: email; Example: email=john@example.com
  • Field: Location; Variable: location; Example: location=Main%20Office
  • Field: Custom answers; Variable: a1, a2, etc.; Example: a1=Resume%20review
  • Field: Checkboxes or radios; Variable: aX=#; Example: a3=2,3
  • Field: Guests; Variable: guests; Example: guests=jane@example.com,john@example.com

Note

You can’t pre-fill “Other” fields for radio buttons or checkboxes where users type their own text. #### Pre-fill a phone number

You can add a phone number to the link, depending on how your event collects it:

  • If the phone number comes from the event’s location (e.g. a phone call):

  • Use location=1234567890

  • If it’s a custom question:

  • Use the matching variable, like a1=1234567890

Note

SMS reminder fields can’t be pre-filled. #### Example full link

calendly.com

This will pre-fill the name, email, and first custom question response.

How to redirect invitees to another site after booking

Quick answer

To redirect invitees after booking:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the three dots menu for that event and select Edit.
  3. Select More options at the bottom of the editor.
  4. Expand the Confirmation page section and under After booking select Redirect to an external site.
  5. Enter the redirect webpage URL, optionally enable Pass event details to your redirected page to include booking info, and book a test event to verify.

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

After an invitee books a meeting in Calendly, they’ll see a confirmation page by default. You can choose to automatically redirect them to another webpage, such as a thank-you page or survey, to share follow-up information or track conversions. #### Redirect invitees after booking

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the [Image: 35940719014423] three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. Select More options at the bottom of the editor.
  4. Expand the Confirmation page section.
  5. Under After booking, select Redirect to an external site.
  6. Enter the webpage URL where invitees should be redirected.
  7. (Optional) Select Pass event details to your redirected page to include booking info like the invitee’s name, email, or event time. See next section for more details.

After you set up the redirect, book a test event to make sure invitees are taken to the correct page. #### Include booking details in the redirect URL

If you turn on Pass event details to your redirected page, Calendly adds booking information to the end of your redirect URL. These details can include things like the event name, invitee name, email address, and UTM tags.

Your web developer can use this information to personalize the destination page, track conversions, or record booking data in other tools. They can set this up on your website by reading URL parameters with JavaScript. #### Redirect URL variables

The following parameters can appear in your redirect URL, depending on the event and invitee details.

  • Event variables: event_type_name

  • Event variables: event_type_uuid

  • Event variables: event_start_time (in invitee timezone (iso8601 format))

  • Event variables: event_end_time (in invitee timezone (iso8601 format))

  • Event variables: guests

  • Event variables: assigned_to

  • Event invitee variables: invitee_uuid

  • Event invitee variables: invitee_email

  • Event invitee variables: invitee_first_name (when applicable)

  • Event invitee variables: invitee_last_name (when applicable)

  • Event invitee variables: invitee_full_name (when applicable)

  • Event invitee variables: invitee_payment_amount (when applicable)

  • Event invitee variables: invitee_payment_currency (when applicable)

  • Event invitee variables: text_reminder_number (if available)

  • Urchin Tracking Module (UTM) variables: utm_source (if available)

  • Urchin Tracking Module (UTM) variables: utm_medium (if available)

  • Urchin Tracking Module (UTM) variables: utm_campaign (if available)

  • Urchin Tracking Module (UTM) variables: utm_content (if available)

  • Urchin Tracking Module (UTM) variables: utm_term (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_1 (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_2 (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_3 (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_4 (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_5 (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_6 (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_7 (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_8 (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_9 (if available)

  • Custom answer variables to invitee questions: answer_10 (if available)

How to reschedule a meeting

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

If your plans change, you can reschedule a meeting from the Meetings page. Your invitee will receive updated details with the new date and time.

If you no longer need the meeting, you can cancel it instead. Learn more in How to cancel a meeting.

Reschedule a meeting in Calendly

  1. Go to the Meetings page.
  2. Select the meeting.
  3. Select Reschedule.
  4. Choose how you’d like to reschedule:

  • On the Free plan, you’ll go directly to the booking page to select a new time.

  • On paid plans, you can:

  • Share new times to meet – Cancel the current meeting and email them to choose a new time. You can customize the message and add a reminder if your invitee hasn’t scheduled in 1, 3, or 7 days.

  • Reschedule meeting now – Choose a new time for your invitee.

The original meeting is canceled or updated, and your invitee receives a notification email.

Reschedule notes (desktop)

  • Group events: You can reschedule one invitee at a time. Select the [Image: 38395036682007] three dots next to their name, then Reschedule invitee.
  • Round Robin events: When rescheduling, you’ll be prompted to either keep the Round Robin assignment or choose a specific team member as the host.
  • Other event types: To change the host, cancel the meeting and schedule a new one.

Reschedule a meeting from Google Calendar

If you connect your Google Calendar, you can reschedule meetings directly from your calendar.

When you update the date or time of the event in Google Calendar, Calendly also updates the meeting and notifies your invitee.

To use this feature, make sure automatic sync is turned on in your calendar settings. Learn how to sync cancellations and reschedules with Google Calendar.

How to schedule with conference rooms

Available to Owners and Admins on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Looking to use a conference room to schedule meetings in Calendly? You have a few easy options, depending on how you manage your rooms. This guide covers how to set up conference rooms as event locations using three methods.

  • Creating Collective event types
  • Creating conference room sub-calendars
  • Manually adding conference rooms #### Option 1: Using a Collective event type

A Collective event type helps prevent double-booking by checking everyone’s availability, including the conference room, before a meeting is booked. To use this option, add each conference room as a new user with a unique login email and paid seat.

  1. Add each conference room as a new user.
  2. Go to Scheduling.
  3. Select + Create and choose Collective.
  4. Add the team member(s) and conference room as hosts.
  5. Complete the remaining event type settings, then save the event type. #### Option 2: Using a sub-calendar and Zapier

This method works well if you’re managing one conference room or shared meeting space.

  1. Create a new “sub-calendar” in your connected calendar for the room
  • Create a sub-calendar in Google
  • Create a sub-calendar in Outlook
  • Create a sub-calendar in Office 365
  • Create a sub-calendar in Exchange
  1. Share the calendar with anyone who will use the conference room.
  2. Use Calendly’s Zapier integration to send Calendly meetings to the conference room calendar.
  3. Optional: Set Calendly to check this sub-calendar for conflicts. This will help prevent double bookings. #### Option 3: Manually add a conference room to meetings

Use this method if you prefer to set the room yourself each time you book a meeting.

  1. After booking a meeting, open your personal calendar.
  2. Update the location to include the conference room.

This works best for smaller teams or rooms with low booking activity. For higher traffic, consider the collective or sub-calendar methods above to prevent double-booking.

How to share your availability with Gmail or Outlook in Calendly

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Use Calendly’s Share availability feature to send your scheduling link from your connected Gmail or Outlook account. This helps the email feel more personal and recognizable to invitees. You can also choose to automatically send a reminder email if the invitee hasn’t scheduled in 1, 3, or 7 days.

Plus, Calendly automatically tracks which contacts you’ve shared availability with. If they don’t schedule within 3 days, they’ll appear in your recommended follow-ups list for easy outreach. #### Before you begin

  • You’ll need to be on a paid plan.
  • Connect the Gmail or Outlook for Workflows integration.
  • The automatic reminder email can’t be customized at this time. #### Share availability from the Scheduling page
  1. Go to the Scheduling page in Calendly.
  2. Find the event type you want to share and hover over it to see more options.
  3. Select [Image: 33359140002967] Share availability to open the email composer.
  4. In the To field, add your invitee’s email address.
  5. (Optional) Customize the message and turn on the reminder email.
  6. Select Send to share your availability. #### Share availability from the Contacts page

Make sure your contact is already in your list. If they’re not, add them as a contact first.

  1. Go to the Contacts page in Calendly.
  2. Find your contact and select [Image: 33359140002967] Share availability.
  3. Choose an event type and select Next.
  4. (Optional) Customize the message and turn on the reminder email.
  5. Select Send to share your availability.

Note

When you select a contact to share your availability with, that person becomes the main email recipient and can’t be changed. To email someone else, close the draft. Then, select Share availability for the correct contact from the main contacts list. #### What to expect after sending the email

When you use Share availability, the email is sent from your connected Gmail or Outlook account and will appear in your Sent folder.

If an invitee replies to your email, their response will go directly to your Gmail or Outlook inbox, not in Calendly.

Once they select a time and book, the meeting will appear in Calendly and on your connected calendar as usual.

What happens if they don’t schedule?

Note

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users.

After 3 days, if the recipient hasn’t booked a meeting, they’ll automatically appear in your Recommended follow-ups list. You can then:

  • Send a personalized follow-up email with your scheduling link
  • View the original message history to provide better context
  • Dismiss contacts who are no longer relevant
  • Track follow-up success and meeting conversions

Learn more about Recommended follow-ups.

How to share your scheduling link

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Easily share your Calendly scheduling links so invitees can book time with you using landing pages, event types, and more. #### Share a landing page

A landing page is a public page where invitees can view and book all active event types for a personal or team page. Share this link to let them choose the option that works best.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. (Optional) Open the My Calendly dropdown to switch to another user or team page.
  3. Select the three dots [Image: 33336155670679] in the top-right corner, then choose Copy link. #### Share an event type scheduling page

An event type scheduling page lets invitees book a specific event type. Share this link when you want someone to schedule that exact meeting.

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. (Optional) Open the My Calendly dropdown to switch to another user or team.
  3. Find the event type you want to share and hover over it to see more options.
  4. On the event type card, choose one of the following:
  • [Image: 38389386901783] Offer time slots in email – Insert available time slots into an email.
  • [Image: 38389371686423] Single-use links – Create a link that expires after one booking.
  • [Image: 38389386904471] Share availability - Send your scheduling link from Gmail or Outlook.
  • [Image: 38389386907415] Copy link - Copy the event link to paste anywhere.

Note

The image preview for a Calendly link is automatically pulled from your profile or organization logo. Updating your logo will update the preview for newly shared links. #### Additional ways to share your link

  • Add to website – Embed Calendly on your website so visitors can schedule with you directly.
  • Email signature – Include your link in your email signature for easy access.
  • Browser extensions – Quickly access your links in Chrome, Firefox, and Microsoft Edge.

How to track conversions with UTM parameters

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

With a Calendly account, you can track where your scheduled meetings come from by using UTM parameters in your scheduling links.

Follow these steps to create and track a link: #### Step 1 – Choose Your UTM Codes

Pick the UTM codes that help you understand where your meetings are coming from. Calendly supports these values:

  • utm_source Use this to show which website sent the traffic. Example: utm_source=facebook
  • utm_medium This tells you how people found the link. Example: utm_medium=email
  • utm_campaign Name your campaign to group your links. Example: utm_campaign=summer
  • utm_content Track which part of a page a user clicked. Example: utm_content=header or utm_content=footer
  • utm_term Track keywords for paid ads. Example: utm_term=atlanta+realty #### Step 2 – Build Your Calendly Link

Start with your Calendly link, then add a ? followed by your UTM codes.

  • Use & to separate each code.
  • Use %20 for spaces.

Example:

www.calendly.com/yourlink?utm_medium=social&utm_source=facebook&utm_campaign=summer%20promotion #### Step 3 – Track Meetings in Calendly

  1. From your Home page, go to Meetings.
  2. Select Filter.
  3. Under Tracking IDs, choose All IDs.
  4. Enter the UTM code you want to track.
  5. Export the filtered list as a CSV file to use in a spreadsheet.

Note

UTM values must be 255 characters or less. If they’re longer, they may not be tracked.

How to view Google or Outlook meetings in Calendly

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Use the Meetings page to see all your scheduled events in one place. When you connect your Google or Outlook calendar, meetings from those calendars appear in your Meetings page alongside your Calendly meetings. #### How connected calendar meetings work

  • Meetings from your connected calendar appear in your Meetings page timeline.
  • These meetings are view-only and can’t be edited in Calendly.
  • The meetings that appear depend on the calendar selected in your Add to calendar settings. #### How to change meeting display settings

You can choose which meetings to show in your Meetings page.

  1. Go to the Meetings page.
  2. Select Settings.
  3. Choose one of the following options based on your connected calendar:
  • Scheduled through Calendly and Google Calendar
  • Scheduled through Calendly and Office 365/Outlook.com Calendar
  • Scheduled through Calendly only

Introducing the new Meetings page

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

The new Meetings page brings all your Calendly meeting details into one simple view. Everything you need to prepare, join, and follow up on meetings is in one place. #### What’s new on the Meetings page

Here’s what’s new and improved:

  • Simplified meeting view View your upcoming and past meetings on the same page. Scroll to see what’s coming up or review what’s already happened without switching tabs.
  • Clearer meeting details Click any meeting to quickly find the details you need. Attendees, location, invitee questions, and internal notes are all organized in a single panel.
  • All your meetings in one place Connected your Google or Outlook calendar? You’ll now see those events alongside your Calendly meetings for a complete view of your schedule. #### View meetings from your connected calendar

When you connect your Google Calendar, or Outlook calendar, you’ll see those meetings with your Calendly events on the Meetings page. This helps you keep track of all your meetings in one place.

Learn more about viewing Google or Outlook meetings in Calendly. #### Manage your meetings

From the Meetings page, you can view details, make updates, or take action on any meeting scheduled through Calendly.

Meetings from your Google or Outlook calendar appear here too, but they’re view-only. You can choose whether to show them on your Meetings page. Learn how toview Google or Outlook meetings in Calendly.

Select a meeting to open more information on the right side of the page. From there, you can:

  • View meeting details, like location and host
  • Edit invitee contact details and view their questions
  • Add internal meeting notes
  • Check the timeline for meeting actions and notifications

To take action on a meeting, you can:

  • Cancel or reschedule an upcoming meeting
  • Book a follow-up meeting
  • Mark an invitee as a no-show for a past meeting

For step-by-step instructions, learn more in How to manage your meetings.

Mutual availability overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

When visiting another Calendly user’s booking page, you can view mutual availability on the right-hand side.

This feature shows your upcoming meetings alongside your host’s availability, with green dots highlighting times when you’re both free to meet.

[Image: 4403029413655] #### Schedule with mutual availability

  1. Log into your Calendly account and visit the link your host shared.
  2. Select a date. Your host’s available times will appear on the left, while your upcoming meetings display on the right.
  3. Look for green dots indicating when you’re both free.
  4. To view the calendars Calendly is using for your availability, select the information icon next to your name.
  5. Choose a time, review your details, and confirm the meeting. Calendly will notify your host and add the event to your calendar. #### Time format settings

Your calendar displays in either a 12-hour (am/pm) or 24-hour format based on your account settings. If your host’s time format differs, you can adjust how their times are displayed by toggling the time zone setting on their booking page.

The perfect scheduling setup

Available to all users on all plans.View plans #### Overview

This guide will help you set up scheduling, step-by-step. Start by creating a one-on-one event, connect your video conferencing tool, then customize and share your event for easy scheduling. Finally, use Calendly’s Chrome extension to schedule effortlessly from anywhere on the web.

[Image: Play button]

Create your first one-on-one event type

Follow this article to create your first one-on-one event type. Next, explore other event types to learn other ways to set up meetings with invitees.

Connect your video conferencing tool

Now that you’ve created your first one-on-one event type, let’s connect your video conferencing tool so you can host virtual meetings.

You can connect the following video conferencing platforms:

  • Zoom
  • Google Meet
  • Microsoft Teams
  • GoTo Meeting
  • Webex

To connect those integrations, check out How to schedule with video conferencing.

Customize and share your first event type

Next, let’s customize your first event type to fit your specific scheduling needs and explore the three ways to share your scheduling page so you can start booking meetings. #### Customize your event type

From your Scheduling page, select the event type you wish to customize. From there, select More options at the bottom of the editor. Here you will be able to access your advanced event type settings.

Description

Tell your invitees what this meeting is about.

Limits and buffers

Add buffer time before or after booked Calendly events and set the maximum events allowed per day, week or month.

Free/busy rules

Allow invitees to book over selected meetings on your connected calendars.

Booking page options

You can edit the booking link for your event, set the frequency of available time slots for invitees, and set how the timezone shows on your booking page for invitees.

Invitee form

Collect invitees name and email, and set invitee questions to be asked on your booking form.

Payment

Collect payment for your event.

Notifications and workflows

Manage your notifications and workflows, including the method of scheduling confirmation notifications.

Confirmation page

Set your confirmation page settings to offer additional links, encourage users to book another meeting, and more. #### Share your scheduling link

Easily share your Calendly scheduling links so invitees can book time with you using landing pages, event types, and more. Learn how to share your scheduling link.

Schedule from anywhere with Calendly’s Chrome extension

Finally, install the Calendly for Chrome extension for easy access to your scheduling links, one-off meetings, and more. Once installed, you can access your scheduling links from your Chrome browser and Gmail toolbars, enhancing your scheduling flexibility.

For more information on the extension, check out Installing Calendly for Chrome.

Time Zones overview

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly automatically detects your time zone when you sign up. Any event an invitee schedules with you appears in your calendar based on your current calendar settings.

The time zone displayed on your Meetings Page is based on the time zone you have applied to your Calendly account. You can view or change this time zone anytime from your Account Settings. #### Change your time zone for schedules or event types

Calendly uses your account time zone for all schedules and event types by default. You can update it at any time. #### To change your schedule time zone:

  1. Go to the Availability page.

  2. Select a schedule from the Schedule dropdown.

  3. At the bottom of the List view, open the Time zone dropdown.

  4. Search for your time zone. You’ll see the local time next to each option.

  5. Choose the time zone. Your schedule saves automatically. #### To change your event type time zone:

  6. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.

  7. Open the [Image: 33458169470871] three dots menu and select Edit.

  8. In the Availability section, click the current time zone under your available hours.

  9. Search for and select the new time zone.

  10. Select Save changes. #### How Calendly handles invitee time zones

Calendly detects your invitee’s time zone automatically. It shows your availability in their local time.

When they book a meeting, the event appears on their calendar in their own time zone.

Want to see your availability in another time zone? Invitees can select a new one from the dropdown on your scheduling page. #### How Calendly adjusts for daylight saving time

Calendly handles daylight saving time changes for you. If someone books before or after a time change, we adjust the times so meetings happen at the correct local time. #### Lock an event type to one time zone

By default, Calendly detects your time zone and your invitee’s time zone. For in-person events, we recommend locking the time zone to the event location.

To lock the time zone:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the [Image: 33458169470871] three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. Select More options at the bottom of the editor.
  4. Expand the Booking page options section.
  5. Select the option to Lock the timezone.
  6. Select Save changes. #### Setting availability across times zones

If you’re traveling or working in different time zones, you can set date-specific hours to reflect your local schedule for those days. Each schedule in Calendly is tired to a single time zone, so enter your availability based on the local time where you will be. Calendly will automatically adjust and show the correct times to your invitees. #### Frequently asked questions

The time zone on your Meetings page comes from your Account settings.

To change it:

  1. Go to Account settings.
  2. Update your Time zone.

This setting controls how meetings appear inside your Calendly account.

Note: Changing your account time zone only affects how meetings display in your account. It does not change the time zone shown on your live booking page.

The time zone on your live booking page depends on your setup.

It is controlled by your:

  • Availability settings
  • Event type schedule settings

Your booking page may:

  • Automatically detect your invitee’s local time zone and let them choose a different one
  • Be locked to a specific time zone for that event type

Changing your Account time zone does not automatically update your booking page time zone.

To update how time zones appear on your booking page, review:

  • Change your time zone for schedules or event types (hyperlink to section)

Lock an event type to one time zone (hyperlink to section)

Teams & groups

Groups overview

Available to Owners and Admins on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Admins can set up groups in Calendly to manage users and track group activity.

For example, you can:

  • Organize users by department, team, or location.

  • Let group admins manage and report on their group.

  • Track meetings and activity by group. #### Before you begin

  • Owners and admins can manage all users and groups.

  • Group admins can view and manage users in their assigned group(s).

  • Enterprise customers can use SCIM to automatically provision users into groups. #### Best practices

For a group admin:

  • Manage groups - Oversee and report on your members without needing full admin access.
  • Create routing forms - Set up forms for your group without affecting others.
  • Multi-group admin - Manage more than one group without being a member.
  • Invite members - If allowed, invite new users to your organization. This feature is enabled by an admin under Permissions in the Admin center.

For an owner/admin:

  • Delegate permissions - Let group admins invite users or limit this to organization admins.
  • Track activity - Use reports to monitor invites, meetings, and user activity.
  • Export reports - Export group member reports to track activity metrics, like the number of events scheduled. #### Setting up groups

Ready to set up groups? These Help Center articles walk you through the steps.

  • How to create or delete a group
  • How to manage group members

How to create or delete a group

Available to Owners and Admins on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button] #### Overview

Admins can create and delete groups in Calendly to organize users and assign admin permissions. Follow these steps to create or delete your groups. #### Create a group

  1. Go to the Admin center, then select Groups.
  2. Select New group, enter the name, and select Continue.
  3. To add members, select Add members and enter their names or emails.
  4. When you’re done, select Add. #### Delete a group

When a group is no longer needed, it can be permanently deleted from your organization.

  1. Go to the Admin center, then select Groups.
  2. Choose the group you want to delete.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of the page and select Delete group.
  4. Confirm the deletion. #### Things to keep in mind:
  • Once deleted, a group cannot be recovered.
  • Only owners and admins can delete a group; group admins cannot.
  • Deleting a group does not remove members from your organization.
  • Any Managed Events owned by the group will also be deleted.

After the group is deleted, you can assign its members to a new group as needed.

What’s next?

Now that you’ve learned how to create groups, explore more ways to manage groups and members with these resources:

  • How to manage group members: Learn how to change roles, remove members, and export group data for better management and reporting.
  • How to create and assign Managed Events: Create reusable event types and apply them to your groups to standardize meetings.

How to manage availability for your users

Available to Owners and Admins on Standard, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Admins and users with editing permissions can update availability for personal and shared event types on behalf of other users. #### Before you begin

To manage availability, you must either:

  • Be an admin or owner, or
  • Have editing permissions for the event type

Learn more about event type permissions. #### Update a personal event type

Use these steps to update the availability of a personal event type for another user:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. Open the My Calendly dropdown.
  3. Select the user whose availability you want to manage.
  4. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  5. Open the [Image: 33458198199319] three dots menu and select Edit.
  6. Expand the Availability section.
  7. From the Schedule dropdown, select Custom schedule.
  8. Adjust the hours as needed.
  9. Check the time zone under Weekly hours.
  10. To add date-specific hours, select + Hours under Date-specific hours. #### Update a shared or team event type

You can manage availability in two ways:

  • By host – customize each host’s availability
  • For all hosts – set the same schedule for everyone #### Follow these steps:
  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. In the My Calendly dropdown, select the team or user.
  3. Go to the Scheduling page and locate the shared or team event type.
  4. Open the [Image: 33458198199319] three dots menu and select Edit.
  5. Expand the Availability section.
  6. Using the Schedule dropdown, choose to set hours by host or to set the same hours for all hosts.

Set availability by host

  1. Select each host’s name to view their individual schedule.
  2. Use the Schedule dropdown to select Custom schedule.
  3. Adjust each host’s hours.
  4. Want to reuse availability from another event? Select the Apply to/from event types icon.

Set availability for all hosts

  1. Choose Set the same hours for all hosts.
  2. Use the Schedule dropdown to select Custom schedule.
  3. Adjust the hours as needed.
  4. Confirm the correct time zone.
  5. To add one-time hours, select + Hours under Date-specific hours.

Note

You can’t apply or copy hours to Collective or Round Robin event types when all hosts are set to share the same availability.

How to manage group members

Available to Owners and Admins on Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Keep your groups up to date. This guide shows how to manage members, change roles, and export group info. #### Before you begin

  • Owners and admins can manage all users and groups.
  • Group admins can only view and manage users in their assigned group(s).
  • Group admins can manage more than one group.
  • A member can only belong to one group. #### Add a member to a group
  1. Go to the Admin center, then select Groups.
  2. Select the group you want to edit.
  3. Select Add member, then enter the member’s name or email.
  4. Select Add.

Organizations on the Enterprise plan using SCIM can automatically provision users into groups. #### Change a member’s role

  1. Go to the Groups page.
  2. Choose the group you want to edit.
  3. Select the checkbox next to the member(s).
  4. Select the [Image: 31356896419095] three dots next to a name.
  5. Choose the role you’d like to assign to the member(s):
  • Group members have no additional permissions.
  • Group admins can manage users, roles, and resend invites. #### Remove a member from a group
  1. Go to the Groups page.
  2. Choose the group you want to edit.
  3. Select the checkbox next to the member.
  4. Select Remove member(s) at the top of the page.
  5. Confirm the removal. #### Export group member data

Export a CSV file with these group details:

  • Who has activated their account
  • Who hasn’t accepted their Calendly invite
  • Total events scheduled by each member
  • Last scheduled meeting date
  • Total meetings scheduled in the last 30 days

To export the list:

  1. Go to the Groups page.
  2. Choose the group you want to export.
  3. Select Export.
  4. Choose Active or Pending group members.

How to manage shared Event Type creation

Available to Owners and Admins on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Owners and admins can control who can create new shared Event Types in their organization. #### Update shared Event Type permissions

  1. Go to the Admin Center.
  2. Select Permissions, and stay on the Event types tab.
  3. Under Who can create new shared event types?, choose one:
  • All members of my organization - Anyone can create a new shared Event Type.
  • No one - No one will be able to create new shared Event Types. Existing shared Event Types will not be affected.
  1. Select Save.

Note

If you select No one, admins can still create Collective and Round Robin events by setting up a team.

How to manage shared Event Types

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Once you’ve created a shared Event Type, you can update hosts, manage scheduled meetings, and share the scheduling link with invitees. #### Find your shared event types

Shared Event Types appear on your Scheduling page, below your personal event types. Once someone books a shared Event Type, it will also appear on the Meetings page under the assigned host(s). #### Share the link

Shared event types do not appear on your landing page. To share it with invitees, locate the event scheduling page link for the shared event type. #### Manage scheduled meetings

Once a shared event type is booked, who can update the meeting depends on the event type and permissions:

  • Collective - Any host or an Admin can manage the meeting or event type.
  • Round Robin - Only the assigned host or an Admin can make changes.
  • Anyone with Edit access (via permissions) can also update the event type or scheduled meetings. #### Add or remove hosts

To update hosts (including yourself):

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. Find the event type you want to edit and open its settings.
  3. Expand the Hosts section.
  4. Add new hosts by name or email:
  • For Collective, select + Add co-host.
  • For Round Robin, select + Add rotating-host.
  1. To remove a host, select the X next to their name.
  2. Select Save changes.

Note

When you remove yourself from a shared event type, you’ll lose access to manage it unless you’re an owner or admin. Any meetings already scheduled will remain on your calendar until you cancel the meeting or delete the calendar invite. #### Notifications when adding hosts

When a host is added to a shared event type, they are notified via email. They have the option to opt out of these notifications by selecting Unsubscribe at the bottom of the email, or from their Account settings > Communication settings page.

How to schedule with multiple groups of hosts

Available to all users on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

On Teams and Enterprise plans, you can create advanced Event Types that include both required and rotating hosts. This setup combines Collective and Round Robin logic. Some hosts always attend, while others are assigned from one or more rotating pools.

For example, you can set up:

  • A product demo with an account executive and a rotating sales engineer. The account executive always attends, and the sales engineer is assigned from a Round Robin pool.

  • A panel interview with a hiring manager, a team lead, and a peer interviewer. The hiring manager always attends, while the other two are pulled from separate Round Robin pools. #### Before you begin

  • We recommend learning how to create a shared Collective Event Type and a shared Round Robin Event Type.

  • The hosts must already be users in your Calendly organization.

  • When you reschedule an event with multiple host pools from your Meetings page, you won’t see the option to choose hosts. You’ll go directly to the booking page, and the meeting will be rescheduled using Round Robin logic. #### Create an advanced Collective and Round Robin event

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. Select the + Create button, then Collective or Round robin.
  3. Enter an Event name and set the Duration.
  4. Add your Hosts:

  • Select + Add co-host to add teammates as hosts who will always attend.

  • Select Create rotating host pool to include hosts in a Round Robin pool.

  • For each pool, you can edit its name, members, and distribution method.

  1. Set your Rescheduling preferences to reassign through Round Robin or to keep original hosts.
  2. Set the Location for this event type.

  • If a co-host is included, you can offer one location or let invitees choose from multiple options.

  • For video conferencing, assign one co-host to be the meeting organizer.

  • If all hosts are in Round Robin pools, set the location individually for each host in the first pool.

  1. Set the Availability settings for this event type.
  • Set the date range options.
  • Choose to set the schedule for each host or apply the same hours to all hosts.
  1. Select Create. #### What’s next?

Share your link or manage your shared event to update hosts and booked meetings.

How to set up a shared Collective event type

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Shared Collective Event Types let you co-host events with other users in your Calendly organization without needing a team page or admin assistance. Invitees can only book when all selected hosts are available.

For example, you can set up:

  • A sales call with an account executive and an SDR

  • A support call with a customer rep and an engineer

  • An interview with a recruiter and hiring manager #### Before you begin

  • All hosts must be available for time slots to appear.

  • The hosts must already be users in your Calendly organization.

  • If you’d like to organize and host these events through a team landing page, consider creating a team Collective event.

  • To include both required and rotating hosts in one meeting, you can set up an event type with multiple host pools. Available on our Teams and Enterprise plans. #### Create a shared Collective event

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. Select the + Create button > Collective.

  • To remove a host, select the X next to their name.

Multi-person scheduling options for your organization

Quick answer

Here’s an overview of multi-person scheduling options in Calendly:

  1. Round Robin — Rotate meetings among multiple hosts based on availability. You can balance workload or connect invitees with the next available person. (Available on Teams and Enterprise plans.)
  2. Collective — Show only times when all selected hosts are free. When an invitee books, everyone is added to the event. Good for meetings that need multiple hosts at once. (Available on Standard, Teams, and Enterprise plans.
  3. Group — Let one host meet with many invitees in the same time slot, ideal for webinars, info sessions, or workshops. (Available on Standard, Teams, and Enterprise plans.)

Shared vs. Team event types: * Shared event types are quick and flexible and can be created by hosts (unless restricted). * Team event types are structured, managed by admins or team managers, and show up on team landing pages with custom links.

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly has several ways for teams to schedule with others. This article explains each multi-person event type and when to use them. You’ll also learn how team pages and shared event types work. #### Multi-person event types

For event types that involve multiple hosts, such as Round Robin and Collective, each host must be a Calendly user with their own paid seat. Invitees don’t need Calendly accounts or seats. #### Round Robin

Info

Available on Teams and Enterprise plans

Round Robin event types rotate meetings between multiple hosts based on availability. You can distribute meetings evenly across your team or prioritize certain members first. This event type works well when you want to balance workloads or connect invitees to the next available person quickly. #### Collective

Info

Available on Standard, Teams, and Enterprise plans

Collective event types show only the times when all selected hosts are available. Once an invitee books a time, everyone is added to the calendar invite. This event type is ideal when someone needs to meet with more than one team member at the same time. #### Group

Info

Available on Standard, Teams, and Enterprise plans

Group event types let one host meet with multiple invitees in the same time slot. This format works well for webinars, info sessions, and workshops where several invitees attend at once. #### Share event types and pages with a team

Use teams to manage events together and keep scheduling consistent. When you’re part of a team, you’ll share a team landing page where invitees can view and book events. #### Work with anyone by using shared event types

Shared event types make it easy to collaborate across your organization, even if you’re not on the same team page. You can quickly create multi-person event types without involving an admin. #### Compare shared and team event types

Here’s a side-by-side comparison of shared vs. team event types:

  • Feature: Best for; Shared event types: Quick, flexible collaboration; Team event types: Structured, team-managed scheduling
  • Feature: Who can create?; Shared event types: Anyone (unless restricted by an admin); Team event types: Owners, admins, and team managers
  • Feature: Who can edit?; Shared event types: Hosts, owners, and admins; Team event types: Owners, admins, and team managers
  • Feature: Who can add/remove hosts?; Shared event types: Hosts, owners, and admins; Team event types: Owners, admins, and team managers
  • Feature: Visible on landing pages?; Shared event types: No; Team event types: Yes (team page only)
