Shared Event Types overview

Available to Owners and Admins on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Shared Event Types let you schedule meetings with your teammates without needing admin setup. This feature is available on paid Calendly plans and makes it easy to co-host events or rotate meetings to the next available host. #### Shared Event Type options

You can create two different Shared Event Types:

  • Collective: Invitees can only book when all hosts are available. Use this setup for sales calls with multiple roles, interviews with hiring panels, or internal team syncs.
  • Round Robin (Teams and Enterprise only): Invitees are automatically booked with the next available host. Best for sharing meeting load across a team, like for product demos, onboarding, or support calls. #### Combine multiple groups of hosts

For more flexibility, users on Teams and Enterprise plans can also create advanced Event Types that combine Collective and Round Robin logic using multiple groups of hosts. This lets you require certain hosts to always attend while rotating others from one or more host pools.

For example, you can set up a panel interview with a hiring manager, a team leader, and a peer. The hiring manager would always attend, while the team leader and peer would be assigned from two different Round Robin pools. #### What to expect with Shared Event Types

  • Shared Event Types don’t appear on a landing page. You’ll need to share them using a direct link or add them to your website
  • You can’t change or customize the URL of a Shared Event Type.

If you need it to show on a landing page or use a branded link, try a Team Event Type instead. #### Before you begin

  • Shared Event Types are only available to users in the same Calendly organization.
  • Your organization needs to allow the creation of Shared Event Types. If you don’t see the option to create one, contact your admin to review this setting.
  • Round Robin and multi-host setups are only available on Teams and Enterprise plans. #### Set up Shared Event Types

Ready to get started? Use these Help Center articles:

  • Set up a shared Collective event type - Set up a shared Round Robin event type, - Schedule with multiple groups of hosts - Manage Shared Event Types

Using Calendly with a team

Available to all users on all plans.View plans #### Overview

Learn how to set up your team on Calendly, add members, streamline scheduling with Managed and Round Robin events, and secure settings with SAML SSO or SCIM.

[Image: Play button]

Add teammates to start scheduling collaboratively

Let’s get started by adding your teammates to your Calendly organization. This will enable you all to schedule meetings collaboratively and enhance team coordination.

To learn more about how to view, manage, and organize your users, check out User management.

Streamline scheduling for the team

Next, let’s streamline your team’s scheduling using Managed and Round Robin events. #### Managed Events

Managed events are reusable event types that admins can edit, lock, update, and assign to users, helping standardize meetings and enhance control over your organization’s scheduling experience. #### Round Robin

Increase your team’s flexibility by setting up a team page and creating a Round Robin event, allowing invitees to choose a time with any available team member. You can choose to distribute events among team members evenly or by priority. Round Robin event types are available on the Teams and Enterprise plans.

Note

Looking to automatically route leads and prospects to the most suitable team member based on their expertise or availability? Check out Calendly Routing.

Manage secure settings for the team

Now that your team is set up for scheduling, let’s ensure the security of your system. Owners and admins on our Enterprise plan can secure settings be implementing SAML Single Sign-On (SSO) and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) to protect organizational data and simplify user management. #### SAML SSO

SCIM

Admin Center

See an overview of your organization’s activity, including:

Company admin guide

Available to Owners and Admins on all plans.View plans #### Welcome to Calendly!

We’ve put together a few simple steps for you, the company admin, to set up Calendly for your team.

Step 1 – Add your company logo

Each user in your Calendly organization has a booking page. This is where invitees book time with them. To give all pages a consistent look and reinforce your brand, you can upload a company logo. This logo appears at the top left of every booking page. #### How to upload your logo

To add a company logo, go to the Admin center > Branding page.

Once uploaded, you can apply the logo to all users.

Step 2 – Connect integrations

On the Integrations & apps page, you’ll see lots of integrations. Sort by category and use case to find the integration you are looking for. You’ll also see an Admin tag on integrations that you can install on behalf of all users in your organization.

Calendly works with many tools, like Salesforce and Google Analytics. The integrations listed here are built by us, but some companies have created their own custom integrations. If you don’t see what you need, try a quick Google search to find if the tool you want has a custom Calendly integration.

If you can’t find one, you can use Zapier, a no-code tool that connects Calendly to thousands of apps. Check out the Calendly + Zapier guide to learn more. #### Salesforce

Available on: Teams and Enterprise plans

If you want to connect Calendly with Salesforce, we recommend working with an IT admin or Salesforce admin.

Note: With the Salesforce package installed, Calendly’s Salesforce integration automatically sends meeting data to Salesforce to create and update your Salesforce records as your invitees book, cancel, and reschedule.

The out-of-the-box scheduling behavior is completely customizable, so your Salesforce admin can modify the default behavior to make sure Calendly aligns with your preferred Salesforce setup.

To learn more, check out some additional Salesforce resources:

  • Calendly + Salesforce
  • How to integrate Calendly with Salesforce
  • Default behavior of the Salesforce package
  • Customize Calendly’s Salesforce flow #### SAML single sign-on and SCIM provisioning

Available on: Enterprise plans or as an add-on for Teams plans

Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) Single Sign-On (SSO) lets your team sign in to Calendly using your company’s existing login credentials. System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) provisioning automates user account creation and removal through your identity provider — the service managing your company’s user credentials, such as Okta or Azure AD.

You’ll see a few identity providers under Security and Compliance on the Integrations page. You’ll also see a general single sign-on option if you need to connect with an identity provider that is not listed. We recommend working with an IT admin for setup.

Connect your identity provider on behalf of your members, so everyone can sign in with their company credentials. Once you’ve turned on SAML SSO, you can choose to set up SCIM provisioning, for easy onboarding and off-boarding of members. #### Video conferencing

Calendly supports:

  • Zoom
  • Google Meet
  • Microsoft Teams Conferencing
  • Webex
  • GoTo Meeting

You’ll notice there isn’t an Admin tag on these tiles, this means your users will each need to connect their own preferred video conferencing tools from within their own account Integrations page. Feel free to send your team this article on how to schedule with video conferencing. #### Other popular Calendly integrations

CRM

  • HubSpot

Recruiting Software

  • Greenhouse

Reporting

  • Google Analytics
  • Meta Pixel (formerly Facebook Pixel)
  • UTM Parameters
  • Webhooks

Step 3 – Create groups for your team

Before you start adding users to your Calendly organization, you can create groups.

Groups are an easy way for an admin to manage users and track group activity. For example, you can organize users by department, team, or location. #### How do I create a group?

To create a group, head to your Admin Center and select Groups. From there select New Group. For detailed steps on how to set up your group check out How to create or delete a group.

Step 4 – Create managed event types for your team

Before you start adding users to your Calendly organization, you can create managed events.

Managed events are standardized event types that you can assign across members of your organization. If your users tend to host similar events, like demo calls or advising sessions, then managed events can help keep these events uniform for all users. #### How do I create a managed event?

To create a managed event, head to your Admin Center and select Managed events. From there select New Managed Event. For detailed steps on how to set up your managed event, check out How to create and assign Managed Events.

Calendly supports two types of managed events:

  • One-on-one: an event between one team member and one invitee
  • Group: an event between one team member and many invitees

Before inviting users, make sure you are happy with your managed events set up. Note: While we suggest first creating a managed event and then inviting users, you can still apply managed events to any existing users on your account.

Step 5 – Invite teammates

With your account set up, you’re ready to add users!

Note that if you want to use SCIM provisioning to add users, you’ll need to first configure SAML, SSO and SCIM with your IT admin. For more details, check out An overview of SAML single sign-on for your organization. #### How do I add users?

You can add new users at any time from the Users section of your Admin center by clicking Invite users.

For step-by-step instructions on adding users or seats, see Adding or removing users and seats. #### How do I communicate the change to my team?

Invited users will receive an email invite from notifications@calendly.com. Once they successfully accept the email invitation, they will be added to your Calendly organization.

To prepare your users, feel free to send out an email in advance.

Here’s an example email template:

Subject: Get ready to join Calendly!

Body: We’re excited you’re joining Calendly!

Shortly, you’ll receive an invitation from notifications@calendly.com. You can follow the instructions in the email invitation to get set up. Once you’ve accepted this invite, you’ll be part of our Calendly organization.

To complete your account setup and get ready for scheduling, check out these important steps and additional resources:

  • How to connect your calendar
  • How to schedule with video conferencing
  • How to choose a meeting location
  • Set your hours of availability
  • How to share your scheduling link

How do I manage pending and active users?

Pending users

On the Users page, under Pending, you’ll see any users who haven’t accepted their invites to your organization. You can resend an invite by selecting the [Image: 32701549581719] three dots, but we recommend waiting at least a day before doing so.

Active users

Under Active, you’ll see all the users who have already accepted the invitation to join your organization. By default, anyone who joins is listed as a user but you can change their role by selecting the [Image: 32701549581719] three dots and Change role. #### Step 6 – Choose a plan and setup billing

Account owners & admins can set up your Calendly subscription from within your Admin center under Billing. When updating your Calendly subscription, there are a few key words to know:

  • Seats: The number of seats you have on a Calendly subscription represents the number of users you can invite to join your organization account.
  • Users: Users are the actual team members using a Calendly account for scheduling meetings.
  • Upgrade: Move current subscription to a higher tiered plan (ex. changing from the Free plan to the Teams plan).
  • Downgrade: Move current subscription to a lower tiered plan (ex. changing from the Teams plan to a Free plan).

Your Calendly billing can be set up annually (charged once a year) or monthly (charged each month). Subscriptions automatically renew unless you choose to downgrade.

Calendly charges per seat in your organization, whether or not the seat is occupied by a user.

For example, if you have 5 seats and 4 active users, you’ll pay for all 5, whether they’re filled or not. To manage your users and seats, check out How to add or remove users and seats.

Next steps

Thanks for following along! Calendly has a ton of additional functionality, from meeting polls to routing forms. We look forward to seeing you progress on your Calendly journey!

Using recaps

How to edit a Notetaker recap

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users. Release notes

Note

Notetaker is being gradually rolled out to eligible users. Join the waitlist.

Edit a Notetaker recap to fix details, add context, or remove items. Use these steps to open a past recap, update it, and save changes. #### Before you begin

  • Enable Notetaker for your meetings.
  • Notetaker can record Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams meetings, regardless of whether you’re the host or if the meeting was scheduled through Calendly or your Google Calendar. #### Edit a Notetaker recap
  1. Go to your Recaps or Meetings page.
  2. Find the past meeting you want to edit.
  3. Select the recap name, or choose View recap.
  4. Next to the section you want to edit, select the [Image: 34436536271127] three dots.

Note

To discard your edits, select Reset to original notes. This clears your changes.

How to manage and share Notetaker recaps

This feature is in limited availability and available to select users. Release notes

Note

Notetaker is being gradually rolled out to eligible users. Join the waitlist.

When enabled, Notetaker records your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams calls. It creates a recap you can keep private or choose to share.

For example, you can:

  • Share a link to a recorded meeting

  • Email a recap with notes and a video link

  • Protect recordings with a passcode #### Before you begin

  • Enable Calendly Notetaker for your meetings.

  • Notetaker can record Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams meetings, regardless of whether you’re the host or if the meeting was scheduled through Calendly or your Google Calendar. #### Find and open a recap

To locate a Notetaker recap:

  1. Go to your Recaps or Meetings page.
  2. Find a past meeting.
  3. Select the recap or choose View recap. #### Share a recap

Share a recap page link

To share a recap page link with others:

  1. Open the recap.
  2. In the top right, select the link icon.

Share by email

  1. Open the recap.
  2. Select Share recap in the top right.
  3. Choose to:
  • Send a follow-up email to attendees, or
  • Send to someone else
  1. Enter email addresses, update the subject or message as needed.
  2. Optional:
  • Add a video link
  • Protect the recap with a passcode (copy the passcode if used)
  1. Select Send Email. #### Revoke a video link

If needed, you can revoke a video link. This removes access for everyone who received it. To share with specific people again, revoke the old link first, then send a new one.

To revoke a video link:

  1. Open the recap.

  2. Select More in the top right.

  3. Select Revoke video link.

  4. Confirm by selecting Revoke video link again.

  5. Refresh the page to get a new link. #### Export a transcript as a TXT file

  6. Open the recap you want to export.

  7. Select Transcript.

  8. Select [Image: 36312577762583] Download as TXT. #### Download a recap

You can download a recap video to save or share it outside of Calendly.

To download a recap:

  1. Go to the Recaps page.
  2. Open the recap you want to download.
  3. In the video player, select Download in the bottom left.

The recap downloads as a video file to your device.

Video conferencing

Admin-Managed Zoom

Available to Owners and Admins on Teams and Enterprise plans.View plans

Connect Zoom to your Calendly organization to help users get started faster. This lets everyone schedule Zoom meetings right after signing up. #### Before you begin

Only Calendly owners or admins can connect an organization-wide Zoom account. But only a Zoom admin can approve and complete the connection.

When you try to connect, Zoom will let you know if you’re the right admin.

Note: The Zoom account must stay assigned to an admin role. If the admin is removed or their role changes, you’ll need to reconnect using a different Zoom admin account. #### Connect Zoom for your organization

  1. Go to the Integrations & apps page from your home screen.
  2. Select the Zoom integration.
  3. Click Connect Zoom for my organization.
  4. Locate the link provided.
  • If you’re the Zoom admin, follow the link to log into Zoom and finish the setup.
  • If not, copy the link and send it to your Zoom admin. #### After connecting Zoom

Once connected, all users in your organization can automatically add Zoom meeting details to their events.

If a user already connected their personal Zoom account, it won’t be replaced by the organization’s Zoom account. #### Optional settings

On the Zoom integration page, you can:

  • Automatically enable Zoom Meeting Summary for all your meetings

  • Learn more in Zoom’s article on AI Companion

  • Let users disconnect this integration #### Personal vs. admin-managed Zoom accounts

Users can connect:

  • One personal Zoom account
  • One organization Zoom account

If both are connected:

  • The setup page will show only the personal connection.
  • If they disconnect their personal Zoom, the admin-managed Zoom will take over.

To check a user’s Zoom connection:

  • Go to the Zoom integration page.

  • Scroll to Connected users.

  • You’ll see their connection status and whether it’s personal or organization. #### Disconnecting the organization’s Zoom account

  1. Go to the Integrations & apps page.
  2. Select the Zoom integration.
  3. Click Disconnect.

If you delete the Zoom account used for the integration, it will disconnect the organization-level setup for all users. This might also affect any location settings tied to Zoom.

Users can still connect their own personal Zoom accounts after disconnecting.

Calendly + GoTo Meeting

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

You can connect Calendly with your GoTo Meeting account to create a unique link for each event. #### Connect your GoTo Meeting account

Follow the steps in this article to connect your GoTo Meeting account. #### Offer dial-in numbers

If you have a paid GoTo Meeting account, you can include dial-in numbers for your invitees. To check if your plan supports this, visit the GoTo Meeting pricing page.

In your GoTo Meeting settings, these numbers come from the Preferred Numbers list. If you’ve selected numbers from more than one country, Calendly will show all of them in the invite.

To turn off dial-in numbers, go to your GoTo Meeting setup page and toggle the feature off.

Calendly will also turn off this feature if your plan doesn’t support it. #### What happens after someone schedules?

After a meeting is booked, you and your invitees will get the GoTo Meeting link by email and in your calendar invite. You can also find the link on your Meetings page in Calendly or in GoTo Meeting under Meetings on your Home page.

Calendly + Microsoft Teams Conferencing

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Create Microsoft Teams links automatically for every Calendly meeting. This integration adds video conferencing details to calendar invites and confirmation emails—no extra steps needed. #### Before you begin

You need a Microsoft 365 Business or Office 365 Education account to use Microsoft Teams Conferencing with Calendly. #### Connect your Microsoft Teams Conferencing account

If you’ve already connected your Office 365 or Outlook.com calendar, Microsoft Teams may already be connected.

To confirm, go to the Integrations page and select Microsoft Teams Conferencing.

If it’s not connected, you can connect it from that page. Learn more about connecting your video conferencing tools. #### Change which Teams account is connected

To change your Teams account integration:

  1. Disconnect the current Teams integration from your Integrations page.
  2. Once disconnected, there are two options:
  • Clear your browser cache & cookies.
  • Open an incognito browser window and log into to your Calendly account there.
  1. After you have cleared your cache & cookies or logged into Calendly within an incognito window, navigate to your integrations page to connect the new video conferencing account.
  2. Once the correct Teams account has been connected, schedule a test event to ensure a new link is generated.

If you are needing to change the Teams link for an event that has already been scheduled, you will need to reschedule that event for the same date/time with the new Teams account integrated. #### How your invitees can join your Microsoft Teams conference

When your invitees click on the link to join your conference, they can choose to download the Microsoft Teams application if they meet with you frequently. Guests and other invitees who need to immediately join your conference can click on Continue on this browser.

[Image: 25806333795223] #### Troubleshooting Microsoft Teams errors

If you’re experiencing issues with Microsoft Teams, such as missing meeting links or seeing an “Action required” message, disconnect and reconnect the Microsoft Teams integration. Then try booking a test meeting.

If you’re still experiencing issues after reconnecting, contact Support for help troubleshooting your Microsoft Teams integration.

Calendly + Webex

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Connect Calendly with Webex to automatically add secure video conferencing links to your scheduled events. If your Webex admin hasn’t approved the Calendly app yet, they can follow the steps below to approve access. #### Connect your Webex account

To connect your Webex account, follow the steps in this article. #### Get Calendly approved by your Webex admin

If you see an Access denied message when connecting Webex, your Webex admin must approve Calendly in the Webex Control Hub.

Your Webex admin can follow Webex’s guide to enable one of these options:

  • Approve Global Access to all apps
  • Approve access to just Calendly (requires Webex Pro Pack) #### Security

For an overview of Calendly’s security, visit our privacy and security standards. Below are Webex-specific details. #### OAuth Scopes

Calendly requests these scopes from Webex:

  • Scope: meeting:schedules_read; What it does: Lets Calendly pull Webex details into your account.
  • Scope: meeting:schedules_write; What it does: Lets Calendly create Webex meetings when you schedule in Calendly.
  • Scope: spark:people_read; What it does: Lets Calendly show the connected Webex account in your settings.

See Webex’s Meetings Overview for more details. #### What Webex data does Calendly store?

Calendly stores:

  • Webex meeting details to show as the location in your Calendly meeting.
  • Webex user details to link the right Webex and Calendly users.
  • Encrypted access and refresh tokens to keep your Webex connection active.

Calendly does not store or view your Webex recordings.

Calendly + Zoom

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Create Zoom links automatically for every Calendly meeting. This integration adds video conferencing details to calendar invites and confirmation emails—no extra steps needed. #### Connect your Zoom account

To connect your Zoom account, follow the steps in this article. #### Notes for Calendly organizations with multiple users

  • Zoom admins must pre-approve Calendly in the Zoom Marketplace.

  • If you see a message about pre-approval, follow the steps in this article.

  • Personal vs. admin-managed Zoom accounts

  • By default, users connect their own Zoom accounts.

  • Admins can use the Admin-managed Zoom feature to connect Zoom for everyone in the organization.

  • Zoom for Collective event types

  • For Collective event types, one team member must be set as the organizer to host the Zoom meeting. Set this up in your event type settings before any meetings are booked. #### After Zoom is connected

When someone books a meeting, Calendly:

  • Adds Zoom details to the calendar invite and confirmation email
  • Shows meeting info on your Calendly Meetings page
  • Lists the meeting in your Zoom Upcoming Meetings

You can also update dial-in numbers and passcodes in your Zoom account settings.

To include Zoom info in notifications and Workflows, use the dynamic location variable. #### Optional settings

On the Zoom integration page, you can enable Zoom Meeting Summary for all meetings you host.

Learn more about this in Zoom’s AI Companion article. #### Zoom customization options

From your Zoom account, you can manage meeting settings that affect how meeting links are generated and how invitees join.

This includes:

  • Using your Personal Meeting ID (PMI)
  • Adding passcodes to meetings
  • Turning on a waiting room
  • Adjusting dial-in and audio preferences #### Zoom permissions used by Calendly

Calendly uses these Zoom permissions to manage meetings for you: #### User-level permissions

  • Permission: meetings:read; Why Calendly uses it: retrieving dial in numbers for a meeting
  • Permission: meetings:write; Why Calendly uses it: create/delete meetings when they’re a “Zoom” type in Calendly
  • Permission: user:read; Why Calendly uses it: retrieving the Zoom user’s ID and email address

Admin-managed permissions

  • Permission: meetings:read:admin; Why Calendly uses it: retrieving dial in numbers for a meeting
  • Permission: meetings:write:admin; Why Calendly uses it: create/delete meetings when they’re a “Zoom” type in Calendly
  • Permission: user:read:admin; Why Calendly uses it: retrieving the Zoom user’s ID and email address

For a full list of Zoom permissions, review this Zoom support article.

How to manage your Zoom meeting settings

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

When using Zoom with Calendly, you can adjust a few optional settings in your Zoom account that control how meeting links are generated and how invitees join. This article walks through how to use a Personal Meeting ID (PMI), enable passcodes, turn on a waiting room, and adjust dial-in options. #### Before you begin

  • Connect your Zoom account with Calendly.
  • Add Zoom as a location for your event types.
  • Log in to Zoom to review your settings. #### Use your Personal Meeting ID (PMI)

By default, Calendly creates a new Zoom link for each meeting. To reuse the same link each time, enable your Personal Meeting ID (PMI) in Zoom. #### Add passcodes to Zoom meetings

When Zoom passcodes are enabled, Calendly will automatically include a unique passcode in each Zoom meeting invite.

For users on a Zoom Basic plan

Meeting passcodes are enabled and locked by default on all Zoom Basic plans. No additional action is required.

For users on a paid Zoom plan

Passcode settings must be enabled in your paid Zoom account. If you’re part of a Zoom organization, your Zoom admin may need to turn this on this setting. #### Turn on the waiting room

Zoom’s waiting room feature controls when participants can join your meeting. If enabled, invitees must wait to be admitted by the host. #### Adjust dial-in and audio options

You can change your Zoom settings to control how one-tap mobile and dial-in numbers appear when someone books time with you through Calendly.

Manage one-tap mobile and dial-in numbers

Zoom shows one-tap mobile and dial-in numbers if your Zoom meeting audio type is set to Telephone or Telephone and Computer Audio. To remove dial-in numbers, switch your Zoom audio type to Computer Audio only.

Choose global dial-in countries or regions

Use Zoom’s Global dial-in countries/regions setting to choose which countries or regions appear in your meeting invites for participants who may need to dial in.

Manage the Find your local number link

Zoom can include a Find your local number link in meeting invites, which directs participants to a page of international dial-in numbers.

How to schedule with video conferencing

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Calendly has native integrations with the following video conferencing platforms:

  • Zoom
  • Google Meet
  • Microsoft Teams
  • GoTo Meeting
  • Webex

Once connected and added as the location for your event type(s), Calendly will automatically generate video conferencing details when someone books with you. You and your invitee will also receive details via confirmation email and calendar event.

If you use a video conferencing platform that isn’t listed above, follow the steps in How to use other video conferencing options. #### Let your invitee choose how to meet

For One-on-one and Collective event types, you can connect multiple video conferencing platforms and let your invitee choose their preferred way to meet. #### Schedule a meeting with video conferencing

Step 1 – Connect your Zoom account

  1. Go to your Integrations & apps page from the left-hand menu.
  2. Select Zoom, then click Connect Zoom.
  3. Sign in to your Zoom account.
  4. Click Authorize to allow Calendly access.

If you’re prompted to pre-approve the app, follow the steps in Pre-approving Zoom. #### Step 2 – Set Zoom as your meeting location

After connecting your Zoom account, Calendly will prompt you to set it as the meeting location. Follow the steps below for your event type. #### Personal or Shared Event Type

  1. Go to your Home page.
  2. Select the event type.
  3. Select Location and choose Zoom.
  4. (Optional) For One-on-one or Collective events, select + Add location to let invitees choose between multiple options.
  5. Select Save changes.

Repeat for each event type where you want to use Zoom. #### One-Off Meeting

  1. Set up your one-off meeting.
  2. Under Location, select Zoom. #### Team Event Type

Round Robin Events

  1. Go to Event Details.
  2. Under Location, select Zoom for each team member who wants to use it.
  • Each team member must connect their Zoom account.

Collective Events

  1. Go to your Team page.
  2. Select the event type.
  3. Select Location and choose a Zoom organizer.
  4. Select Save & Close. #### Step 3 – Meet with Zoom

After someone schedules with you:

  • Calendly will add the Zoom meeting link to the calendar invite and confirmation email.
  • You and your invitee will receive full Zoom details automatically.
  • The meeting also appears in your Zoom account under Upcoming Meetings.

Customize your Zoom settings to require a Personal Meeting ID, passcode, or change dial-in settings. #### Frequently asked questions

If your meeting link is missing, it is usually due to how your event type was set up when the meeting was booked.

Video links are only added if video conferencing (like Zoom or Google Meet) was turned on in the event type settings at the time of booking.

If you update your event type after a meeting is scheduled, the change will not apply to that existing meeting.

To fix this for future meetings:

  1. Go to your event type.
  2. Select Location.
  3. Make sure your video conferencing option is connected and selected.
  4. Save your changes.

New bookings will include the correct meeting link.

For meetings that are already scheduled, you’ll need to manually share the correct link with your invitee. You can also reschedule the meeting for the same date and time to generate a new link.

How to use other video conferencing options

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Calendly supports Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, GoTo Meeting, and Webex platforms.

If you use a different video conferencing platform, like RingCentral, you have two options:

  1. Add your conferencing details as a custom location.
  2. Generate conferencing details after your invitee books. #### Option 1 – Add your conferencing link as a custom location

If your conferencing platform provides a permanent meeting link, room, or dial-in number, you can add this to your event type in Calendly.

  1. Open your event type settings.
  2. Under Location, select Custom.
  3. Enter your personal conferencing link.
  4. You can choose to display the link when invitees book or after they’ve booked.
  5. Select Save.

Calendly will automatically add your conferencing link to the calendar invite. #### Option 2 – Manually add your conferencing link after scheduling

If your platform doesn’t offer a permanent link, you’ll need to create a new meeting link for each appointment. To notify your invitees, add a note in the location field.

  1. Open your event type settings.
  2. Under Location, select Custom.
  3. Enter a message like: “I’ll send the video conferencing details before our meeting.”
  4. Select Save.
  5. After an invitee books, generate a new meeting link in your conferencing platform and update the calendar event with the details.

Note

If your conferencing platform integrates with Zapier, you can set up an automation (called a “zap”) to create a new meeting link for each booking. Learn how to automate this process.

Pre-approving Zoom

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

If you’re trying to connect Zoom to Calendly and see a Request pre-approve message, this means your Zoom account requires admin approval before apps can be installed.

Some Zoom accounts are configured to restrict third-party app installations. In these cases, a Zoom admin must approve the Calendly app before users can complete the connection. #### For Zoom users

If you see a Request pre-approve message while connecting Zoom to Calendly, click Request pre-approve. This sends a notification to your Zoom admin asking them to approve Calendly for Zoom in the Zoom App Marketplace.

What happens next:

  • Your Zoom admin will receive a request to review and approve the app.
  • Until approval is granted, you will continue to see the pre-approval message and won’t be able to complete the connection.

If you’re not sure who your Zoom admin is, contact your IT team for help.

If you’re also a Zoom admin, you can approve the app yourself by following the steps below. #### For Zoom admins

As a Zoom admin, you will need to pre-approve Calendly for Zoom before users in your account can connect it.

You can approve the app on one of two ways: #### Option 1: During the connection process

If you’re connecting Zoom to Calendly and see the pre-approval prompt:

  1. Select the option to review or approve the app.

  2. Follow the Zoom prompts to complete the approval. #### Option 2: In the Zoom App Marketplace

  3. Sign into your Zoom admin account.

  4. Go to the Zoom App Marketplace.

  5. Search for Calendly for Zoom.

  6. Select the app and choose pre-approve (or enable it for your account).

Once approved, everyone on your Zoom account can install the app. For more help, please see Zoom’s support article.

Troubleshooting Zoom

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Having trouble using Zoom with Calendly? This guide covers common Zoom issues and how to fix them fast. #### Zoom shows “Action Needed”

If you see an “Action Needed” message on your Meetings page, Calendly couldn’t add a Zoom link.

Common causes:

  • Zoom isn’t connected to your Calendly account.
  • You’ve hit Zoom’s API rate limits. #### Zoom isn’t connected to Calendly

Make sure Zoom is connected to your account. This helps Calendly add the right Zoom link to your meetings.

Note: To add Zoom to upcoming meetings, reschedule them for the same time and date.

For personal event types:

  1. Go to your Integrations & apps page and select Zoom.

  2. If Zoom isn’t connected, follow steps in How to schedule with video conferencing.

  3. If Zoom is connected:

  4. Open your browser in private/incognito mode.

  5. Log in to Calendly.com.

  6. Go to Integrations & apps and select Zoom.

  7. Select Disconnect, then Connect Zoom.

  8. Sign in to Zoom and select Authorize.

  9. (If needed) see Pre-approving Zoom.

  10. Reschedule your meeting for the same time and date. See How to manage your meetings.

For team event types:

Each teammate must connect their own Zoom account.

  • Round robin: Each person must connect Zoom.
  • Collective: Only the Zoom organizer needs to connect Zoom.

Have teammates follow How to schedule with video conferencing. #### Zoom API rate limits reached

Zoom lets each user schedule up to 100 meetings per day across all Zoom apps. If your Calendly bookings are high, you might reach Zoom’s rate limit.

If that happens, contact our Support team. We’ll check your account and help with next steps. #### Zoom meetings end after 40 minutes

Free Zoom accounts have a 40-minute limit. To hold longer meetings, upgrade to a paid Zoom plan. #### Zoom link missing from notifications

If the Zoom link isn’t showing in your calendar invite or email, the Location variable may be missing.

Fix for calendar invites:

  1. Open the event type > Notifications and Workflows.
  2. Select the three dots next to Calendar invitation > Edit.
  3. In the body, select + Variables > add Location.
  4. Save and close.

Fix for email confirmations:

  1. Open the event type > Notifications and Workflows.
  2. Select the three dots next to Email confirmations > Edit.
  3. In the body, select + Variables > add Location.
  4. Save and close.

Fix for workflows:

  1. Go to your Workflows page.
  2. Open your active workflow.
  3. Under Do this, select Edit next to the email.
  4. In the body, select + Variables > add Location.

Note: Zoom links may take a few seconds to appear. If your guest doesn’t see it, ask them to add the meeting to their calendar again. #### Zoom passcode is missing

If passcodes are on in Zoom, Calendly adds them automatically. Login to your Zoom account and check if the Zoom passcode is turned on. #### Wrong Zoom account is connected

If Zoom meetings show up wrong or have different links, you may have connected the wrong Zoom account. Disconnect and reconnect the integration with the correct account. #### Zoom error: Unable to assign alternative host

If you see: “Unable to assign [your email] as an alternative host because the user cannot be selected at this time.”

It means someone set as a host is no longer in your Zoom account.

Fix it:

  • Go to your Zoom Personal Meeting Room settings and remove the host. Or
  • Or turn off Enable Personal Meeting ID in your Zoom settings.

See How to use your Zoom Personal Meeting ID.

Calendly scheduling notifications

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

When someone schedules a meeting with you, Calendly sends the details to both you and your invitee. There are two types of notifications:

  • Calendar invitation (most common)
  • Email confirmation

Use the tables below to compare them and choose what works best for you.

Looking for reminders, follow-ups, text alerts, or Workflows?Learn more here. #### Compare notification types

How each one works

  • What happens; Calendar invitation: Your calendar creates the event and adds your invitee as a guest.; Email confirmation: Calendly sends an .ics file to you.
  • What your invitee gets; Calendar invitation: A calendar invite from your calendar.; Email confirmation: An email with an event file they can add to their calendar.

Email addresses used

  • Who sends the notification; Calendar invitation: Comes from your connected calendar account.; Email confirmation: Sent from notifications@calendly.com.
  • Who replies go to; Calendar invitation: Replies go to your calendar email.; Email confirmation: Replies go to your Calendly login email, unless you set a no-reply address.

How updates are handled

If you need to change details like time or location, only calendar invitations send updates to your invitee.

  • Will invitees see updates?; Calendar invitation: Yes. They’re added as event guests.; Email confirmation: No. They only receive a static file.

How titles are customized

  • Can I customize my calendar event title?; Calendar invitation: Yes. Title can be customized for the host and invitee’s calendar event.; Email confirmation: An event is added to the host’s calendar. The attached ICS file cannot be customized.

Which notification type should you use?

Use calendar invitations when:

  • You use Google, Office 365, Outlook.com, or Exchange calendars.
  • You need to make event changes and want invitees to get updates.
  • You want the invite to come from your calendar, not Calendly.

Note: For Collective meetings, the calendar event is added to one team member’s calendar, and other members are added as guests. #### Use email confirmations when:

  • You use the Outlook plug-in, iCloud, or no calendar.
  • You want to use a no-reply address to hide your email.
  • You’re hosting a group event (these use email confirmations by default).
  • You wish to include hyperlinks as these are not available for calendar invitations. Note:If you wish to include links in calendar invitations, you must paste the full URL. #### Change your notification type

Calendly automatically picks the notification type based on your calendar or event type. Most of the time, there’s no need to change it. But if you want to switch, follow the steps below. #### Switch to calendar invitations

  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the [Image: 33458167746199] three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. Select More options at the bottom.
  4. Open the Notifications and workflows section.
  5. Next to Email confirmation, select the [Image: 25835562495127] three dots, then Edit.
  6. If it says Calendar invitation, you’re already set.
  7. If not, select Switch to calendar invitation at the top.
  8. Select Save and close.

Note

You can’t switch to calendar invitations if you:

  • Use group events
  • Are using iCloud or the Outlook plug-in
  • Don’t have a calendar connected #### Switch to email confirmations
  1. Go to the Scheduling page and locate your event type.
  2. Open the [Image: 33458167746199] three dots menu and select Edit.
  3. Select More options at the bottom.
  4. Open the Notifications and workflows section.
  5. Next to Calendar invitation, select the [Image: 25835562495127] three dots, then Edit.
  6. If it says Email confirmation, you’re already set.
  7. If not, select Switch to email confirmation at the top.
  8. Select Save and close. #### Frequently asked questions

At this time, you cannot turn off these email notifications. If you want to reduce or stop receiving notifications, you may consider managing your email filters outside of Calendly.

First, you will need to identify whether you are using Calendar Invitations or Email Confirmations.

If your event uses Calendar Invitations:

When using Calendar Invitations as the notification method for your event, Calendly is not sending those invitations to your invitees. Instead, we are prompting your connected calendar to send these invites. To further troubleshooting, we recommend reaching out to your IT team or email provider for assistance.

If your event uses Email Confirmations:

Please contact us and we will be happy to review your logs.

Yes. You can do this by using Calendar Invitations as your scheduling notification. This allows you to login with one email and notify your invitees of their booking with you with the email address associated with the calendar you add new Calendly events to.

Follow these steps:

Step 1: Switch your event type to use Calendar Invitations (see “Switch to calendar invitations” above). This ensures notifications are sent through your connected calendar provider.

Step 2: Connect the calendar account that uses your preferred sending email address. You can follow the steps in the Connect your calendar to Calendly Help Center article.

Step 3: Schedule a test booking to confirm the calendar invitation is sent from your connected calendar’s email address.

Yes. When someone schedules a meeting, the event host automatically receives a booking notification email from notifications@calendly.com.

This default host notification:

  • Confirms the meeting details
  • Is sent in addition to any calendar event created
  • Cannot be turned off

If you’re using Calendar Invitations, your connected calendar will also create the event on your calendar.

If you’re using Email Confirmations, the invitee receives an .ics file, but hosts still receive the default booking notification from Calendly. #### What’s next?

  • How to set up basic notifications
  • How to add a cancellation policy
  • How to include cancel and reschedule links for invitees

How invitees can opt out or back in to texts

Available to all users on all plans.View plans

Invitees can manage text notifications from basic notifications or Workflows after scheduling a meeting.

They can update their preferences by replying with these keywords:

  • Opt out of text messages: Reply with STOP.

  • Opt back in to text messages: Reply with START.

  • Get help with text messaging: Reply with HELP. #### Important notes:

  • You won’t be notified when an invitee opts out of texts.

  • Invitees must reply to the same number they opted out from. Replies to a different number won’t work.

How to create a Workflow

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans #### Overview

Set up Workflows to automate email and text messages for meeting reminders and follow-ups. You can start with a template for a quick setup, or design a custom Workflow.

Create a Workflow

  1. Go to the Workflows page.
  2. Choose whether you want to use a template or create a custom Workflow.

  • To use a template:

  • Choose a Workflow template from our library and click Use workflow.

  • To create a custom Workflow:

  • Select Create your own workflow.

  • In the When this happens section, choose a trigger and set the time for your Workflow.

  • In the Do this section, choose an action, then select Next.

  1. In the Workflow name section, enter a name for your Workflow.
  • Workflows are organized by chronological order and are unable to be arranged. We recommend using a naming system so they are sorted based on your preferences.
  1. In the Which event types will this apply to? section, choose your event types for this Workflow, then select Apply.
  2. In the Do this section, select Edit and customize your email or text message, then select Done.

  • To insert variables that autofill meeting details:

  • Place your cursor in your message, click Variables in the toolbar, and choose a variable from the list.

  • It will automatically populate with the relevant information once the meeting is scheduled.

  1. (Optional) To include more actions in your Workflow, select Add Actions and repeat Step 3.
  2. After setting up your Workflow, select Save.

What’s next?

Now that you’ve created a Workflow, explore additional ways to manage and customize your Workflows with these resources:

  • How to edit, clone, or delete Workflows: Understand how to manage your existing Workflows.
  • How to send Workflow emails from your Gmail or Outlook account: Set up your email account to send Workflow emails directly through Gmail or Outlook.
  • Send text messages with Workflows: Discover the additional steps and settings required to set up automated text notifications with Workflows.

Variables are placeholders that automatically fill in event or invitee details after a meeting is booked.

  1. Open a Workflow from your list or start with a Workflow template.
  2. Under the Do this section, find an action and select Edit.
  3. In the text editor toolbar, select +Variables.
  4. Choose your variable from the list.
  5. When you’re finished, select Done.
  6. Save your Workflow. #### Link to another page or event type

Let invitees reschedule or book another meeting by linking to an external page or event type in your message. #### Using Email Workflows:

  1. In your Workflow message, highlight the text you want to hyperlink.
  2. Select the link button.
  3. In the Destination dropdown, choose where to send invitees:
  • Enter a custom link to direct them to a different page.
  • Select current event type to link to the meeting that triggered the Workflow.
  • Select a specific event type to link directly to that booking page.
  1. When you’re finished, select Done.
  2. Save your Workflow. #### Using Text Message Workflows:

Linking an external page or event type in your Text Message Workflow is as simple as copying and pasting into the message field

Note

  • Hyperlinking your external page or event type is available in email workflows.
  • When including a link in your text message workflow, be mindful the text can include up to 180 characters. A real-time counter helps you stay within the limit.
  • You’re encouraged to not use URL shorteners like Bitly — some phone carriers block these links. Use full URLs to make sure your messages are delivered. Learn more in this article.

How to edit, clone, or delete Workflows

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Edit, clone, or delete a Workflow using the three dots menu next to each Workflow.

[Image: 26356617170071]

Note

If you don’t see the menu, contact your admin to update your permissions or make changes to your Workflows. #### Manage a Workflow

  1. Go to the Workflows page.
  2. Locate the Workflow you want to manage and select the [Image: 31327952441751] three dots next to it.
  3. In the menu, choose one of the following options:
  • Edit - Make changes to the Workflow, then select Save.
  • Clone - Create a copy of the Workflow, edit as needed, and select Save.
  • Delete - Remove the Workflow by selecting Continue.

How to reconfirm meetings with Workflows

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Reduce no-shows by using Workflows to send automated messages that request invitees to confirm their attendance at your meetings. #### What to expect as an invitee

To confirm attendance, invitees can select the Yes, I’m attending confirmation button located in the email. [Image: 26009150287895]

They can also select the confirmation link found in the text message. [Image: 26009181338391] #### What to expect as a host

Once an invitee confirms their attendance, you will receive an automated email with the meeting details. [Image: 26009150292119]

In Calendly, meetings with confirmed invitees will show up under the Meetings page. For confirmed one-on-one events, Invitee confirmed will show up under the time of the event.

For each confirmed spot in a group event, Invitee confirmed will appear next to the invitee’s name. The total number of confirmed invitees will also be displayed next to the remaining spots.

Set up a reconfirmation email

Create or edit your Workflow

  • You can create a new reconfirmation Workflow by choosing the Email invitee to reconfirm template. [Image: 26009150299159]

  • If you’re creating a custom Workflow or editing an existing Workflow, you can manually include the reconfirmation button in your email in the next step. #### Edit your message

  • When you use the reconfirmation template, the Include reconfirmation button option is already checked. Keep it checked, so invitees can confirm the meeting. [Image: 26009181346327]

  • If you’re creating your own message or editing another Workflow, be sure to check this option. #### Save your Workflow

When you’re done, select Save.

Set up a reconfirmation text

When sending text messages, remember there are some special notes, like character count limits. #### Create or edit your Workflow

  • You can create a new reconfirmation Workflow by choosing the Text invitee to reconfirm template. [Image: 26009181349527]

  • If you’re creating a custom Workflow or editing an existing Workflow, you can manually include the confirmation link in your text message in the next step. #### Edit your message

  • When you use the reconfirmation template, the Confirmation Link variable is already in the text message. Keep it in your message, so invitees can confirm the meeting.

  • If you’re creating your own message or editing another Workflow, be sure to include the {{confirmation_link}} variable. [Image: 26009181350295] #### Save your Workflow

When you’re done, select Save.

How to send text messages with Workflows

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Use Calendly Workflows to automatically send text message reminders to yourself or your invitees. These reminders help reduce no-shows and keep everyone informed before and after meetings.

Note

You can’t send text reminders during the trial period. #### Before you begin

  • Calendly sends text messages through Twilio, a third-party platform.

  • Messages come from random U.S. numbers.

  • Replies from invitees aren’t delivered or monitored.

  • Invitees can choose to receive or stop text messages at any time.

  • Some phone carriers, especially outside the U.S., may block these messages. Read Twilio’s support article for more details.

  • Each message can include up to 180 characters. A real-time counter helps you stay within the limit.

  • If a variable exceeds the character limit, the message will still send without being cut off.

  • Calendly shortens invitee answers from booking forms to 40 characters or fewer to reduce message volume.

  • New accounts: To help protect against spam and misuse, new accounts have limited access to SMS customization. This restriction is temporary and will be lifted automatically as your account becomes more established. In the meantime, you can select from available built-in templates for your text notifications. #### Set limits and follow guidelines

To maintain quality, Calendly limits how many text messages an organization can send.

  • Text messages are only available for Group events with 100 or fewer invitees. Use email Workflows for larger groups.
  • Don’t use URL shorteners like bit.ly—some phone carriers block these links. Use full URLs to make sure your messages are delivered. Learn more in this article. #### Include reschedule or cancel links (optional)

By default, SMS reminders don’t include reschedule or cancel links. You can add them by inserting custom variables in your message.

Reschedule link:

0

Cancel link:

0 Replace 0 with your invitee’s unique ID using Calendly’s variable options. #### Which countries can I send SMS messages from?

Calendly follows Twilio’s Acceptable Use Policy. If your messages break these rules, Calendly will turn off your SMS feature.

Don’t send messages about:

  • Cannabis
  • Gambling
  • Firearms
  • Other restricted topics

Read Twilio’s Messaging Policy to understand all rules. #### SMS opt-in and privacy

Invitees must choose to receive texts before Calendly can send them automated messages. This is required under GDPR and other privacy laws to protect people from unwanted messages.

Important

Because invitees must opt in to receive texts, you can’t make the SMS phone number field required like you can with other booking questions. #### Frequently asked questions

Calendly uses Twilio to send SMS reminders for scheduled events.

Text messages are sent from a toll-free long code number. This is a standard phone number.

Messages are not sent from your personal phone number. They are also not sent from a short code.

The sending number is assigned automatically. You cannot choose or change this number.

No. You can’t edit or remove Calendly’s required SMS consent language shown during booking.

If you’re an Enterprise Owner or Admin, you can add your own legal disclaimer in addition to Calendly’s required consent language.

How to send Workflow emails from your Gmail or Outlook account

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Use Workflows to send emails directly from your Gmail or Outlook account. Use your own email address instead of the default notifications@calendly.com to make your messages more personal. Recipients can reply to your Workflows, and you’ll see responses in your inbox. This feature is only available for personal event types. #### Before you begin

  • You can only send Workflow emails from one connected email account (Gmail or Outlook). If both are connected, Calendly will default to sending from notifications@calendly.com.
  • Workflow messages will appear in your Sent folder.
  • You can also review the Timeline on the Meetings page in Calendly to confirm when the email was sent. #### Integrate your Gmail or Outlook account
  1. Go to the Integrations page and select Gmail for Workflows.
  2. Select Connect Gmail.
  3. Accept the permissions requested. The “Send email on your behalf” permission must be enabled for the integration to work. #### After integrating your Gmail or Outlook account

Once you’ve connected your email account, apply it to your Workflows. When creating or editing a Workflow, go to the email action settings. Under What email address should this email be sent from?, select your Gmail or Outlook account.

Moving forward, all new emails sent through Workflows will come from your email address.

How to send Workflow emails to non-meeting participants

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

[Image: Play button]

Learn how to configure Workflows to automatically send emails with meeting details to recipients other than the host or invitee. These emails keep your teammates and external stakeholders updated on your meeting status, so they know when to act and support your meetings.

For example, you can:

  • Prep meeting materials: Remind your teammates to create a meeting agenda or presentation

  • Make cancellation adjustments: Prompt your Executive Assistant to reschedule or fill the time slot.

  • Assist with follow-ups: Notify a contractor that the meeting ended so they get started on to-do’s. #### Before you begin

  • You can send Workflow emails to any email address, even if the recipient isn’t part of your Calendly organization or attending the meeting.

  • You can include up to 10 recipients per Workflow email.

  • Each Workflow can include only one Email to someone else action, and each event type can have up to three of these Workflows. #### Create the Workflow

  1. Go to the Workflows page.
  2. Select + New Workflow.
  3. Choose one of the Email to someone else templates:
  • Email reminder to someone else
  • Email follow-up to someone else
  • Email cancellation notification to someone else
  1. Follow the prompts to customize your Workflow. For detailed steps, see this article. #### Unsubscribing from Workflow emails

Recipients can opt out of future emails by clicking Unsubscribe from these notifications at the bottom of the email.

[Image: 27277939035927]

How to set up basic notifications

Available to all users on all paid plans.View plans

Keep your invitees informed with basic email and text reminders before and after events.

Looking for advanced automation with emails and text messages? See our Workflows overview. #### Before you begin

  • Owners, admins, and users can set up basic notifications for their event types.
  • Legacy Essentials plan users can only use default email notifications. #### Enable or disable basic notifications
  1. From the Scheduling page, select the event type you want to update.
  2. At the bottom of the editor, select More options.
  3. Open the Notifications and workflows section.
  4. Find the notification you want to update, then select the [Image: 14146649319831] three dots next to it.
  5. Toggle the notification On or Off.
  6. Select Save changes. #### Personalize email and text notifications

If you’re on the Standard plan or higher, you can customize:

  • The subject line of a basic email notification
  • The body of a basic email or text message
  • The dynamic variables used in a message

To edit a notification message:

  1. From the Scheduling page, select the event type you want to update.
  2. At the bottom of the editor, select More options.
  3. Open the Notifications and workflows section.
  4. Find the notification you want to change and select the [Image: 14146649319831] three dots > Edit.
  5. Update the message subject or body as needed.

To add or remove a dynamic variable:

  1. From the Scheduling page, select the event type you want to update.
  2. At the bottom of the editor, select More options.
  3. Open the Notifications and workflows section.
  4. Find the notification you want to change and select the [Image: 14146649319831] three dots > Edit.
  5. Select + Variables and choose the variable you want to include OR remove Variables you no longer want included.
  6. Select Save and close.

How to view your Workflows

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

You can see which Workflows are active for your event types and when email or text messages are sent for scheduled meetings. Use this guide to view Workflows, find which are applied to an event type, and check the timeline for each meeting. #### View all Workflows

To view all Workflows for your account:

  1. Go to the Workflows page.
  2. You’ll see both personal and admin-managed Workflows.
  3. If you’re an admin, open the My Calendly dropdown to select a user or team page. #### View Workflows for an Event Type

To find the Workflows connected to a specific Event Type:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.
  2. Open the Event Type you want to check.
  3. Select More options > Notifications and Workflows. #### View Workflow activity for a scheduled meeting

To see when Workflows ran for a meeting:

  1. Go to the Meetings page.
  2. Select the scheduled meeting you want to review.
  3. Scroll to the Timeline section.
  4. Review when the meeting was booked, who booked it, and when each Workflow ran. #### Frequently asked questions

If your invitees aren’t receiving Workflow emails or reminders, check the following:

  • Confirm that the invitee entered their email address correctly.
  • Review your Workflows activity to make sure that the Workflow triggered as expected.
  • Ask the invitee to check their spam and trash folders.
  • If the issue persists, review our community guide on troubleshooting Workflow emails not sending for additional steps.

Workflows overview

Available to all users on Standard, Professional, Teams, and Enterprise plans.View plans

Automate emails and texts around your meetings with Workflows. These customizable reminders and follow-ups help reduce no-shows and improve your meeting experience with less work.

[Image: 26008761925911]

For example, you can use Workflows to:

  • Remind invitees and yourself of upcoming meetings
  • Reconfirm event attendance
  • Prompt for feedback after a meeting with a survey
  • Thank invitees for their time
  • Follow up to get your next meeting scheduled
  • Send an email to a third party
  • Send an email to a no-show invitee to reschedule #### When your Workflow can be triggered

A Workflow can run at key moments in the scheduling process. Choose from these options when setting one up:

  • New event is booked

  • Before event starts

  • Event starts

  • Event is rescheduled

  • Event ends

  • Event is canceled

  • No-show marked #### Before you begin

  • You will need admin or owner permissions to create and manage workflows for a team. For more details, review our Workflows for admins article.

  • A Calendly user or team can create up to 50 workflows across all event types.

  • We recommend setting up your event types first. This makes it easier to apply a Workflow to multiple event types at once. #### Best practices

  • Reduce no-shows by requesting invitees to confirm attendance using reconfirmation Workflows.

  • Mark invitees as no-shows to prevent sending follow-up Workflows. You can also trigger a no-show reschedule Workflow.

  • Invitees marked as no-shows will only get no-show Workflows. They won’t get other post-meeting Workflows—like thank-you emails, surveys, and follow-ups.

  • For more tips on improving your Workflows, check out our blog. We have posts on automating communications before and after meetings and reducing no-shows with meeting reminders. #### Setting up Workflows

Ready to set up Workflows? These Help Center articles walk you through the steps.

  • How to create a Workflow - How to customize emails and texts for Workflows - How to edit, clone, or delete Workflows, - How to view your Workflows - Send text messages with Workflows - How to send Workflow emails from your Gmail or Outlook account

Troubleshooting Workflows

Updates to Workflows will only apply to future meetings. Meetings made before the changes will still use the old settings from when they were created.

Review our Community guide on troubleshooting when invitees are not receiving Workflows.
